Because HDMI cables are digital you either get the 0 and 1 feed or not, so there should not be much difference between cables. Yet there is a lot of anecdotal evidence that some cables are better than others.I was curious: Are there differences that the home user can detect? I bought an inexpensive DVI Gear cable (well, many sellers do add hefty shipping and handling charges), and a slightly more expensive Cables To Go - 40315 Velocity HDMI cable directly from Amazon. I set up a test that I invite others to replicate and expand.BACKGROUNDBoth cables are made in China. The DVI Gear cable is thinner than the Velocity. Its connectors' gold plating is noticeably thinner than the 24 Karat gold plating on the Velocity (some folks contend that thicker and higher quality plating will maintain a cable's performance over time). The Velocity is advertised as having "100% aluminum foil and braided OFC shield" which "protects against noise and interference." No similar claim for the DVI Gear cable. The Velocity is lifetime warranted; according to a vendor, the DVI Gear has a one-year warranty.SET UPRiders of Rohan scene from LOTR, vol. 2 upconverted to 1080p using a Sony DVP NS77H connected to a Toshiba 40XF550U 40" LCD with 120 Hz frame rate in "natural" picture mode. All gear in a cabinet with numerous cables and electrical cords bunched together. Potential for electrical interference high.TESTThe same scene was run several times using the DVI Gear cable and the Velocity cable. Cables were switched to two different ports on the television to ensure that one port wasn't skewing the test. Two people subjectively judged picture quality, one person (not me) got the test "blind" (not knowing which cable was connected). Audio was not tested.RESULTSWe were in agreement that the DVI Gear cable appeared to produce a slightly less sharp picture, possibly with slightly less color saturation than the Velocity. No artifacts detected, though.A BETTER TESTA better test would be to have exactly the same set-up with two TVs side-by-side, running different kinds of scenes or calibration disks. But our pocketbook isn't that deep!CONCLUSIONThe Velocity might cost roughly twice as much as the DVI Gear, but offers better performance (hence value) - at least on our gear.
summary: Comparison Test Suggests DVI Gear HDMI Cable Inferior

The rule, of course, has become "price rules when it comes to HDMI cables, so simply order the least expensive." However, occasionally there's an "exception that proves the rule." Such was the case for the past three days, when all of my remote controls seemed powerless to conjure up an image on my screen, an image delivered into our TV's Time-Warner set-top box, from whence a short cable is all that's needed to attach it to the back of the Sony TV. After calling Time-Warner, re-reading the manuals, I'd about had it (isn't it bad enough to have non-cooperative computers, turntables, and CD burners?).Then I noticed another 6 foot HDMI cable in my collection that wasn't being used and, more significantly, appeared to be close to twice the diameter of the one presently leading from the Scientific Atlantic set-top box (supplied by Time Warner) to my Sony. Why not swap 'em out? Yes, why not. I replaced the inexpensive generic cable with the thicker, heavier cable that even had a manufacturer's name of some sort on it--not "Monster" but that name would have suited the size. Voila, my Sony was doing the thing for which I got it--performing like a TV set instead of a non-responsive computer screen after another failed boot.I relate the anecdote not to discourage anyone who's decided to save a hundred by buying a three dollar cable, but to point out that every "rule" requires an "exception," and though it's highly unlikely, it's not impossible (improbable, yes) that the problems you're currently having with your hi-def flat screen (if any at all) may be remedied with the replacement of a thin cable with one that actually looks more like it's up to the task of transmitting broadband signals. Buy the three-dollar cable first, and don't be surprised if it works--for anything from a week or two to the lifespan of the TV set. But if it fails, no need to panic. Simply ignore the rule book and try the road least taken.
summary: Spend more money--if only to prove the rule.

The standard charger does not have the ability to report itself as an AC charger to the phone, so the phone will limit is draw to only 500mA (as per USB spec) which is not enough to charge it when the phone is navigating. This Motorola charger provides fast charging and the phone will show itself as being plugged into an AC charger with it, which allows it to draw a full 1000mA. This is enough to recharge the phone even when it is in the power hungry navigation mode. The only nit I might have about it is the bright blue light which indicates it is plugged in. I bought this as an extra to have around so I wouldn't have to drag one from vehicle to vehicle. You can't argue the price, it looks just like the $40 Motorola one I bought a few years ago, it even says Motorola on it. I do not think it is a real Motorola product though. Mine died after about a month. The light still lights up but it won't charge a phone. Another charger in the same port charges just fine.
Sorry even if this is a legit product it won't charge a Xoom. Make sure you check manual or surf the Xoom sites for compatible chargers.
summary: Micro USB does not work for Xoom

reviewText: Had to buy a new one within a couple weeks of using this. It possibly could have broke because of personal reasons. But also could just be a defect in the product.
It LOOKS like a Motorola product, but didn't LAST like a Motorola product. I had it for about a year before it died. For the price, that's not at all bad.

I've bought, well, three of them in the past year, interspersed with a few other styles (like the blackberry one that works, although a little slower). It rapid charges pretty well; My HTC Sensation, though, requests all it can handle I think from the charger, and the phone gets HOT, especially if I do anything with it while it's charging. I mean hot like, it shuts down, unless ambient temps are low like running the AC. But hey, I wanted a faster charge, gotta pay to play.The only major issue I have, and all 3 have had the same problem around the same time, is that after maybe 2-3 months of using it, the connection gets loose. Where before I could pick it up, glance at it (while stopped at a light, ahem), and the hold was solid, it starts to hold less after a couple months. I find myself pushing it back in with that same pick-up-the-phone-while charging, to the point where I can't hardly move it at all without it falling out, and then, the worst, I have to have the charger in at a certain angle with the phone port for it to work. Frustrating at that point, you think it's charging, but because it's not in the sweet spot, your battery says 16% - and those of you with Androids, you know the pain that brings.Maybe it's the fault of the design of micro-usb. But it's the standard it seems, and I'm thinking it's time to try another brand...

i bought this a year and a half ago and it just stopped working. at first it was puttering a charge and now it just doesn't charge at all. i mean, for $10 it's not a bad buy but now i wish i invested in something a little more durable.
I have used it with the Razer back then, and I still use it with the other phone I have.

I purchased this based on the high review ratings on Amazon. I don't like this charger. it charges way too slow to the point that I cannot run my phones GPS on it and keep the current charge, so how can it possibly charge the phone when the phone is in use? I have since purchased the New Trent Arcadia RapiduoNew Trent Arcadia Rapiduo (1PC) 10W 5V/2A Dual Port high-speed USB car charger w/ Free Full Speed Micro-USB Charging Cable (IMP80C)from Amazon because that charger is supposed to charge at higher speed. I am using this device on my Samsung Fascinate:I liked my first one so much, I ordered two more. This is very handy, since not all vehicles give power when the vehicle is turned off.
summary: Charges, Cheap, lets you know when you've got power

reviewText: Works great with my HTC One and my Plantronics Bluetooth. Standard attachment for both. would highly recommend this charger to anyone with the general connection.
I needed a car charger for hubby's mifi and didn't want to pay a high price with Verizon. This works great and the price was right.
summary: Works - what else can you ask for?

reviewText: For less than $10.00 delivered, via Prime, what more can you ask.The cable is not removeable, so you can only use it with micro-USB devices.I connected it to my Galaxy S3 and it works just fine. Small enough to travel with and cheap enough that if I lose it, I won't fret about it.**** Late breaking news ****I reduced the stars to as low as possible.I used it for a trip this weekend, and it failed. The little light was on, but the Galaxy saw nothing. Using a normal wall-wart charger works just fine. I will try taking it apart to see what happened.

I got this to charge my Galaxy S3 and it does a good job for that.I am not sure how fast it charges my phone as I never calculated the time, but it is not like the slower ones.The light on the glass makes it look really rich but the extra size it a little bad and hits the hand when changing the gears.

I like this charger because it does the job quickly for our phones. Charges them much quicker than the previous car chargers we had used. The little blue light is also kinda neat and pretty.I've bought 3 of these in the last 6 months, because one of the original two that I had purchased died about 5 months in.I don't know how long you're supposed to get out of a charger, technically, but that felt a bit short to me and I'm hoping it was indicative of a product that fell through the cracks of quality control, and not a trend.
Bought two of these and they are exactly the same as one I purchased at my local phone store for 3X as much. Live and learn :-)

Worked perfectly and fast on my Droid X. The version I had from Verizon cost three times as much and didn't give me more than a 30% charge increase on a two hour drive. This gave me 70% in about an hour and a half.

charged real well, for 4 months. then it stopped. it now only charges if you hold the cord in a certain direction. which means in a few weeks it wont charge at all. why cant someone make a charger that is decent?!

Tested this a few days ago. Began a short trip with Navigation enabled on my Incredible. The battery was at 80% charge at the start of my trip and after a short 20 minute drive the battery was up to 95% all the while having the GPS running.
summary: Charged faster than the GPS could drain

reviewText: This charger was fine when it worked, being used for charging a Samsung Galaxy Nexus. It does detect correctly as a full DC charger and not USB, so you'll be able to take advantage of faster charging at 1000mw as opposed to the measly 500mw you'd get from pure USB charging. Unfortunately, the charger stopped working after only 3 months of relatively light usage, and it doesn't appear to have any specified warranty -- not that it matters when considering the price, but I'm not tempted to buy another if it's only going to last a few months... I'd look elsewhere.

Ridiculously slow. When they are 4GB, ok, 15 mins to fill it, but if you are on a job, if you are in a hurry to backup some files and get to another job, this is the pits at 32GB. Forget about it. Best speed I could get was from FAT32 format, about 4mb per second, and this with larger files, not thousands of tiny ones.Two hours to fill the drive?I feel like I got cheated buying such a slow device. Heck, wi-fi at McD's is faster!"USB 2.0" is a standard that should mean something. I don't expect max speeds of 60mb per second, but many USB 2.0 devices deliver 20mb - 30mb with no problem. Only 4mb per second? This is nowhere near the standard and should be rejected.Only a little more money buys a faster 2.0 drive, and a little more than that a very fast 3.0 drive. I'm not specifying brands because this is not a plug, just a review written out of frustration.Look, this speed issue is going to catch up with SanDisk and its customers very fast. Just look at the size of files coming out of little cameras now! An hour to transfer 16GB? Really?
I bought 4 of these USB drives for our GPS receivers external drives and these did not lasted even 6 months of this use...
summary: Did not lasted 6 months of use connected!!!

reviewText: I bought this flash drive to watch movies on my TV, works perfect.One thing though - i do not know why but i can not copy MKV files on it. it says drive is full, when it is not.
This is a good product for temporary storage of data, and for quick transferring of data from one computer to another.
summary: SanDisk Cruzer 32 GB USB Flash Drive (SDCZ36-032G-AFFP)

reviewText: I received the 16GB USB Flash drive within 48 from placing the order. It comes with encryption software for protection, which I did not expect, but worse, it did not work once I established the password. It ended in the garbage can.

I purchased the 64gb to backup photos. I have always used Sandisk memory cards for photography, and used some USB thumb drives. They have always work great. I have to agree with the other reviewer, this USB drive is really slow to transfer files. I haven't done a test to see actually write-times, but just from experience of moving large photo files, I can tell a noticeable difference between this and other drives. I probably would not recommend this product, I may try the Kingston or Transcend brand, which are also cheaper. I emailed Sandisk support, and never got a response. Perhaps, the 64gb model just takes longer due to its size, I don't know...
I like the large capacity and the well made (albeit plastic) case.I would prefer a USB 3 connection for faster speed as filling the memory via USB 2 takes some time, but it performs as advertised

This Cruzer worked for one week. Now it is deader than the proverbial doornail. What's more, Sandisk has a complex process to download the uninstall tool for the preinstalled junk. I have had good luck with Kingston and they are smart enough to include the uninstall tool for the junk on the drive. Returning this Sandisk and will order a Kingston.
summary: Do Not recommend this Flash Drive

reviewText: I've had this flash drive for a couple of years now and it has yet to fail me; however, it is AGONIZINGLY slow. Sure, it'll hold 32 GB of information but you'll have to wait around 1.5 hours to transfer it. If you're looking to just carry around a multitude of small files, like doc files, small pictures, et cetera, it's great; however, if you want to transfer video files or large amounts of files, prepare for a wait. You can now buy 32 GB USB 3.0 drives for the same price, so I definitely would not buy this drive again.

Have been looking for a good quality high capacity thumb drive without a cap. This one fits the bill. When it comes to flash hard drives, I trust SanDisk. Have had other thumb drives and CF cards, etc and have had failures, SanDisk doesn't quit on me. I like that the USB is retractable instead of having a cap that is easily lost.

These flash drives have pretty slow write speeds. Writing one gigabyte took 6 minutes and 42 seconds, about 2.54 megabytes per second.This is fine if, like me, you just want a cheap flash drive you can use for small files (documents, etc), but I can't see why you'd want to get the 16/32 GB version since writing 32 GB to this thing would take over 3 1/2 hours.
Great storage at a low cost. I bought two of theses and they just work well. He uses them on a MAC and did reformat them before using them.
Great backup method. I always keep a few USB drives around as spare storage. Includes a space to hook a string or lanyard around which is great as these are so easy to lose.

I use USB drive attaching it to a key ring. I suppose many people does it because of its security.This drive simply cannot be attached to any key ring. The attachment for key ring is simply too small. The design has to be fixed. I hope SanDisk can address this issue for the next product.
summary: Key ring cannot be attached. A design flaw issue.

reviewText: I bought two of these back in late July 2011. As of last week both were totally dead. What's interesting is that I have never had a USB drive die on me before. I went as far as doing a low level format and trying to write zeros to the disk. Nothing revived them. Yet these cheap freebie 1G drives I have laying around from 7 years ago all work fine. I think its time for SanDisk and I to part ways. I've been loyal but the data loss was not cool this time. There's a million alternatives, why not try one out and save yourself the hassle in a year?

I caught the 32GB version of this flash drive on sale for $13 last weekend. I already had one so this was my second purchase of this one. Was almost tempted to buy a 3rd and 4th just because of the price point. While it isn't the fastest flash drive you can't beat the price and consistent quality SanDisk puts out. If you're looking for speed you should go for a USB 3.0 Patriot drive, but you're also looking at paying probably 3-5 times as much. This little drive gets the job done, isn't so small you're just going to lose it after the first use, and has enough capacity at the right price.If you can catch it on sale buy as many as you can. It's worth it.
I have a couple of usb 3.0 flash drives so i'm getting spoiled on those. This takes a little longer to transfer (3-5 minutes for a movie) but it is still useful. We use it with our PS3 mostly.

This flash drive has great storage capacity, and works across platforms. But at times I cannot get this flash drive to read first (or second and third time) when I insert it into the USB port. I often get a message telling me that is not formatted for the drive or is inaccessible. I suspect it has something to do with the sliding nature of the insert point.

Just a couple of things. The USB connection wants to be pushed back in when plugging it in to player. (may not be the fault of the Flash Drive) Down load speed is good and files are added correctly with no errors.
must have for sons schooling and great product

You not able to attach any kind of ring or even a small cable tie or wire to these drives any longer. the ring mount is tiny and at right angles and impossible to get a ring through. I contacted Sandisk and was told "it's a design flaw. please go buy one of our other drives"bye bye SanDisk.
summary: will not accept a ring to attach it to your keys or what ever.

reviewText: Serves the purpose but the USB connector retracts inside the drive so when trying to slide it in the USB slot on your PC you have to hold the red slide while pushing in as it has no locking position. This may be a good feature if you like to carry it around in your pocket to keep it from betting bent or broke but not for my use. I would choose a different one next time.

I chose this rating because SanDisk are the leaders of flash memory. The price is right and the storage is fast and reliable. I've had nothing but SanDisk flash drives and have had little to no problem with them. The only reason I bought more and more is because higher storage capacity was developed constantly over time and I wanted them. I started out with a 4GB, then a year later an 8GB, and then two years later, I jumped to a 32GB.SanDisk has proven themselves to be the most reliable. I have several SD cards and SDHC cards from them as well.What I didn't like here is what made me to leave 4/5: These newer SanDisk flash drive have a poorly designed keychain hook for lanyards. The older ones (prior to 2010) used to have a bigger hole and a bigger loop so that you could add it to other things. It seems as if SanDisk intentionally made this so hard to get a chain around it these days so that you can easily lose this and buy another one.I'd recommended this to anyone who needs reliable, ample and quick storage space to store high capacity files such as HD movies, music, high quality photos and even just regular documents.
summary: Great Flash Drive! Just Wish That It had a Better Keychain Ring And Hook.

reviewText: I bought this to store all the digital family pictures and digital content of importance and have it locked away in the fire safe. 64gb was perfect to hold all of that and store away so we will not be the ones to lose family papers and pictures if something happens. Seemed fairly fast transferring data and the price was right!
summary: Seems Perfect and a huge size

reviewText: worked perfect, no problems at all, more then enough space for what i needed to use it for and still have space left over
Its cheap and functional. I have bought more than one of these and have never had a problem. Would buy again if needed.

reviewText: Write speed is about 4.61 MB/s when writing (using H2testw 1.4), so don't go for it if you are looking for better writing performance. Besides that, it does the job storing files. I'd probably rate this at 3.5 stars.

reviewText: I bought this USB thumb drive back in February. I've formatted it in NTFS and Fat32. This drive is by far the s.l.o.w.e.s.t of any thumb drive I've used going back about 4 years. I've also used my Patriot Xporter 8GB, 16GB and 32GB thumb drives copying and moving the same data, which all of them did many times faster on various computers.I'm not against SanDisk, as my SanDisk MicroSDHC drives work fine with zero issues, but I'll stick with Patriot when it comes to thumb drives.

At one point, I lost a considerable amount of data that I thought that I had backed up. I had not properly saved my files. Since that time, I have studiously saved my files to memory sticks. The price of storage continually drops and when my external hard drive began to fail, I needed to replace it. I have a 16 GB SanDisk which works well. Buying this 32 GB was logical and probably cost less than the 16 GB that I had purchased a few years ago. It is relatively inexpensive and if your files are important to you, take it from a constant worrier, have more than enough redundancy in your back ups. My data is on my computer hard drive and on three different memory sticks; overkill perhaps, but as the title indicates, I'm neurotic.

I bought this to replace a 2gb cruzer I had lost. I thought I'd replace it with another cruzer, but upgrade to one with a larger capacity. As soon as I got the 32gb cruzer I found my not so lost 2gb cruzer. When I went to use my cruzer I found it to be extremely slow then I had flash backs to reading some reviews mentioning this, but since I already had my 2gb cruzer I assumed it was the same as that and people were just expecting faster. Well my 2gb cruzer is a lot faster than my 32gb. Next time I'll pay more attention to reviews. WOULD NOT BUY AGAIN.
just what i needed as i had had an earlier computer meltdown. it makes backing up my documents must easier.

reviewText: As every other Sandisk product, it is efficient and reliable. More capacity than I really needed, but it is always good to have some extra. I am glad to have it!

My Acer laptop has 2 side by side USB ports. The Cruzer drive will just barely squeeze into one of the slots (somwhat askew)if the other port is already occupied by another USB device. I am afraid that pressing it in like this may damage the slot itself. reviewText: When I first bought it, I was experiencing such slow speeds that it was like 2-3/mbs. I had to contact SanDisk and get them to replace my drive. This drive is HORRIBLE for transporting files. I'm an I.T. Professional and constantly need to move files back and forth. If it wasn't for the fact that I was in need of a 16GB drive, I would have returned it.
summary: Worst read/write speeds for any flash drive.

reviewText: When I received this items and tried to use it, my computer said it was not formated. I tried it in amother computer and had the same result. I then tried to format it as my computer suggested. It then listed the drive as 64M and the format failed.
this flash drive had software pre-installed that i did not want or need so I returned it as well as the one i bought to replace it.

Great storage capacity and is a good size. I love retractable heads with no cap so this is for me. Is fast and you can protect content if you wish to.Recomended.

I got a 16GB model of this flash drive as a gift, and I do like the product. The large capacity is nice, the drive seems pretty durable so far. Mine does 'lock' at the extended position, so I don't have the same problems as some reviewers getting it into a USB slot. I'm a PC technician, so my drives get more regular wear than some, and my need to transfer around files is probably not what a typical home computer user would have a need for, which ends up highlighting my main complaint:Compared to many flash drives, this one has a slow write speed. When trying to transfer a few gigs of data off a Windows 7 machine on a 2.0 slot, my write speed floundered between 3.5 and 1.5 MB/second. This was many small files, which is noticiably slower on nearly any flash drive, but even on large files I don't get much faster than about 4-5 MB/second. Now, the read speeds do appear to be much faster, copying 700MB off the drive onto my computer I typically hover around 15 MB/second, but that's still not topping out what USB 2.0 is capable of.For home use or student use, I think this would be just fine as long as you don't continously have to copy large files on and off the drive. For backup where speed isn't as big of a deal, the capacity and price of these drives is just fine. But for IT work, I want something faster. I'm waiting on a Patriot drive to arrive at my house, as people rave about their speed. I'm sure I'll write a review there when I have a chance to play with it and see how much of a difference the extra money really got me.To break it down:Pros: Price, large capacity, durableCons: Very slow write speeds, average read speeds.
summary: Excellent price, but slow compared to some

reviewText: The only real complaint I have with it is the design. It's always a bit of a pain to get the drive fully inserted because it always wants to retract into itself. Price was great, though!

this San Disc comes with some programmed 'safe' it didn't work. I tried re-installing it, calling the customer service and followed their instructions, they also couldn't help. Eventually I gave up on it but I use it for data storage and back up and that works fine.

this is a pretty outdated usb 2.0, the read/write speed is terrible compared to other things on the market, we are slowly coming into the age of usb 3.0 and it already has lightning speeds. This however is an outdated 2.0, if you just want something to store stuff on and forget about it and your not too tech savvy its probably good but I have things to do and I can't wait 15 minutes for a 2gb file to copy. look up read/write speeds when looking to invest in storage. I think this is like 2-4mb/s to be comfortable I need 15mb or higher. Think of it like your ISP....who wants 2mb/s of speed for networking? You can't even stream videos from youtube with that lol

I bought this product on one of amazon's sales that they have on electronic devices, and I figured for 32gb it wasn't a bad deal. I knew that sandisk wasn't some unknown manufacturer that I'd risk shoddy quality with and made my purchase in confidence. The package came in Amazon's frustration free packaging, which is really just a thin cardboard envelope with the drive inside with minimal protection. The drive wasn't damaged, but considering this thing is made of relatively cheap plastic there was a reasonable risk of that happening.Build Quality: There are copious amounts of cheap plastic used and frankly the whole housing doesn't inspire confidence. The mechanism to extend the usb end from the main body seems incredibly flimsy and prone to breaking. I would be very pleasantly surprised if this thing survived being plugged in and used regularly for more than a few months tops. I don't thankfully do that, but it's a issue for those that want to use this thing often. I feel that if I applied even just a bit of pressure I could snap the USB end off. Competitors and even Sandisk I see offer metallic housings that should survive a lot longer. But build quality is only half the problem.Performance: I've consistently been seeing sub 10mb/s sustained speeds over USB 2.0 on multiple devices when transferring movies over. It's also given me some periodic stuttering during playback of higher bitrate movies just completely ruining the experience unless I transfer the file locally onto something else. I primarily use this to store documents and transfer 1080p/720p MKV movie files between computers when I don't want to wait on my wireless network. If you're going to be transferring mainly small files the speed shouldn't be too much of an issue, but if you're transferring any sort of media files or large quantities of files I recommend you stay far away from sandisk. Looking at amazon reviews for the higher priced and better built sandisk drives it looks like slow speeds are a common problem.Overall I'd say this is just a terrible relatively large capacity drive to buy. I thought the sandisk name meant something, but clearly that's not true. My recommendation would be to spend the little extra and go for the corsair flash drives. They've always been very reliable and incredibly fast in the past. I know I'm going to keep my eye out for one in the future.
summary: By far one of the slowest and poorest built flash drives I've ever used

Very slow, its large size 64G makes it worse. It may be alright if you want to copy small files one at a time, but its totally useless if you want to copy large files all at once.
Works like it is supposed to. I think San Disk has consistently been at the top of the heap for external storage.

Sandisk USB ownership history:I own two 4GB Cruzer, an 8G Cruzer Micro, and two 16G Sandisk Cruzer Fit.Pros:+ Sandisk quality+ Compact sizeCons:- Extremely slow transfer speeds (almost unusable in my opinion)Summary;I bought this to replace a budget-priced 8GB Sandisk Micro I've had for over 6 years. It has been extremely reliable and had quite decent transfer speeds. I bought this usb to finally replace that old one and boy was I disappointed. I did a few tests and found that the new drive has only half the write speed and two thirds the read speed of my old drive. At first I thought that the USB must be a fake since the performance was so much slower than any other Sandisk USB I'd ever used but a call to Sandisk customer service resolved that notion. The Sandisk CS person told me that the larger drives are slower because they use a different kind of flash memory. That might have been fine if they had made that clear beforehand. Personally, I didn't buy a brand new USB drive in order to take a step backwards to the speeds I had to put up with 6 years ago, I bought what I thought was a similar product that should have a similar performance. I am very disappointed in Sandisk for not making this clear in the product descriptions. I have actually lost a bit of faith in Sandisk after this incident. If this drive can't deliver the performance of a Sandisk Cruzer, it shouldn't be called a Cruzer. This is going back ASAP.

So the sliding design initially looked like a feature to me because no cap to lose. If your USB slots are facing the correct way and are at the right orientation, it's no problem to hold the slider in place with your thumb and put the drive in. reviewText: Sandisk has flipped the 'fixed disk' bit on their newer USB drives so that they are no longer seen as 'removable' drives by Windows. This means that most, if not all, existing utilities and programs that are designed to create bootable USB drives will not recognize these drives. I threw mine in the trash. reviewText: Sixteen gigs is a lot of storage, and it does the job well. I recommend it for anyone looking for reliable, portable, and secure storage.

While read speed is kind of decent (~22Mb/s) write speed is a joke, ~4Mb/s. Even my (1Gb Sandisk Titanium) purchased on Jan-2006 was faster.Truth is that most manufactures do not publish the read/write speed of low end drives. My mistake was trusting a brand based on my experience with their high end products.Search for Nirsoft usbspeed to find a detailed list with the read/write speed of many USB flash drives.Avoid ANY low end Flash drives, work with them is just frustrating.

My flash drive arrived today. Seems ok but does not have 32 gigs of memory. I plugged it into my computer and it says it has 29.8 gigs! I feel like someone owes me 2.2gigs that I paid for. What say you, Amazon?
summary: This flash drive does not have 32g

reviewText: I never used a flash drive before.I had about 12 full lenth movies on my pc,which i knew i would ad plenty more and had to do something pretty soon to free up space for the long hall.I ordered the 16 gb sandisk cruzer usb,got it the next day(kind of in a rush) called tech support to show me how simple it really was to transfer my first movie all in 6 mins.now i just tell my friends bring it back after they watch something.really after all,I didn't have to call tech. I just did it to be sure , plus it was free.I will be stocking up on sandisk flash drives until the next invention comes out. i have about 40 movies just since 2009.don't have to worry about security they are just flix for now.good product.

How in the name if Heaven did this thing get over a thousand reviewes ????.1.11 minutes to write just 2GB of data using an INTEL i5 machine with 8GB of ram , say what ??????????.2. If you guys could see the kid of packaging that this thing came in trust me those over a 1000 reviews would carry very little weight .3. just like point number 1 above if it takes that long to write that small amount of data imagine the joy I'll have writing all the gigabytes I have stored...oh joy.DO NOT BUY THIS PIECE OF GARBAGE.

reviewText: I ordered this at a time when 16 GB was a good deal for the buck, but this has been replaced by a 64 GB USB 3.0 flash drive. When 128 GB USB 3.0 flash rive come down price some more (under $50) I will get one of these! But this unit has worked flawlessly.

Used a metal body version for years and replaced it with this one recently. The new design has a plastic body. It feels cheap and the slide mechanism is not as smooth. I would suggest looking at the Amazon Basics USB stick instead. It doesn't slide but the build quality is so much better.
summary: Not as good as the old design

reviewText: I was surprised to find that this stick did not come with a lanyard, as did the previous SanDisk drive I purchased. I looked back at the product description, it was accurate; I just assumed this one would also have the lanyard. I took away one star not for that reason, but that the one I had before had a nice green LED on the end that would flash when data was moving on or off the stick. This one has a dim light under the red handle, that almost looks like neon. Just like the old one, this 16 GB model locks into position nicely when you are using it.
What can you say one of the best producers of flash drives. I have and will continue to us their products.
Pros:Read/write for me is excellentNo issues transferring/copying dataGreat priceCons:Summary:Great item, great price, I recommend buying.

I really like the "clip", what I could use of it. The earbuds could not get a good connection. You had to get the connection in just right and then be careful you didm't touch the wire or you would lose your connection. I got the clip so I could wear it while I work and/or exercise, so this wasn't working out. But the company was cooperative and let me return the old one for a replacement. I should be receiving it any day now. A positive thought on it is that when I was able to use it, the sound was good, it was pretty easy to use, lightweight, and I liked the fact that I could attach it to my clothes as I generally do not have any pockets to carry it in. I have a SanDisk Sanza that I really like, but no way to carry it; hence the "clip".

I bought this to replace a broken Zune player that I used for 2 years and loved. I wanted something that could take an external SD card, and the price and reviews of this were good. I was not about to drop another $100 on a zune that did not take ext SD cards. If I had known this Sansa was about twice the size of a postage stamp, I would not have bought it. The menus are not intuitive and frustrating to understand. I guess I could read the manual, but these things should be intuitive. But I loved the screen and functions of the Zune, so it is not a fair comparison. The radio in this works better than the zume, once you figure out how to turn it on. I think if you are a man with big hands you are going to hate this thing with its tiny buttons. But I can see how people like it for running. I use it in the gym sometimes and the built in clip is really handy. I started using my phone more often for playing music at the gym after I bought this.

I bought this as a gift for my wife. I have not messed with it at all, but both my wife and her teenage cousin were unable to figure out how to load music onto it. The cousin spent several hours copying files over, using the directions, and I could only find a couple of MP3s on it.They aren't the most tech savvy by a long shot, but something like this shouldn't require ANY savviness to figure out.
summary: Not the easiest to figure out

reviewText: I'm happy with this MP3 player for what I paid. My one complaint is that the "random" feature doesn't seem to be all that random; it tends to repeat the same 5 or 6 songs and skip others completely. I haven't done a detailed analysis, but with 500+ songs on there I know I've been through some of them a half dozen times and others not at all. Again, for what I paid it's a good device. Battery life is great and sound quality is great. I use it mostly in the car through my aux port, and don't use the earphones very much, but they sounded okay too.Edit: I learned 6 months later that this player does not survive a trip through the wash. And the random feature I initially described got to be more and more annoying as the months went on. I'll be looking for something a bit heartier as a replacement.

Cons:The Sound quality-not even close to IPOD of IRIVER /kinda muddy, less detailed/Complicated setup and use!Very small display/impossible to see outside even in cloudy condition.Battery life 5-6 hours on full charge 3-5 hours? / IRiver-799, I use to have, was working 40 hours & needed 1 AA./Phones = good bass,not good details.Pros:Small size + 4 GB internal memory !Interchangeable SD memory card / up to 32 GB!Voice recording = wav, mp3,ogg. formats /Rec. quality is just tolerable /FM radio = surprisingly good reception even in NYC!I would forgive all disadvantages for the longer battery life & better sound quality.;)
summary: For the price & features its fine,but...

reviewText: These units produce a great sound with rich quality, nice highs and deep lows with no discernable distortion. It sometimes "freezes up" in a mode that it becomes inoperable. After letting it discharge down, it begins to operate again.

I've had a Sansa clip for almost 2 years now and LOVE the clip feature since I use it while working out and hate using armbands. I can clip it anywhere I want and it stays in place great.I don't do anything extra with this players, so I can't comment on how good or how bad some of the features are. I simply download MP3's from my collection on WM Player and go to the gym, turn it on and play. That is it. I listen to the volume just short of full volume and it is sufficient and with it up that loud the battery will typically last around 6 hours or a little more without having to charge it up.My problem is that it is one of the most unreliable pieces of electronic equipment I have ever owned in my entire life. I purchased it from an electronics store with a 2yr protection plan, thank goodness I opted for the 2yr plan. I have literally had to take it in for replacement half a dozen times now. I'm on my 6th one and I just recharged it and now it is completely frozen with the power on and the screen lit up. Will not respond to anything I do including the power button. This is the third unit I have had with this problem. 2 other units would occasionally erase all my files. I would turn on the power and no music would be available even though I had just used it the previous day with over 300 songs on it.I have no idea why I keep getting duds, but the longest I have had one last so far is 10 months. That was the first one. The rest of them have lasted around 2 months. I do not get them sweaty or wet during a workout, so I have no idea why they do not hold up.It is really a shame as overall I like the player as it is small, convenient,and does what I need. The problem is total lack of reliability. Will have to look for a new brand now as a replacement as my 2yr protection plan on it is almost expired.
summary: Great player, if you can get one that works.

reviewText: UPDATE: Add one huge con to the list. The player doesn't support m3u playlists. I'm not sure what to do now to create playlists, but for craps sake, how could they mess this up?!?One day I thought to myself, "They should make a cheap mp3 player that you can put a micro SD card in to increase the capacity." Low and behold I found the Sansa clip. Back in the day I had a 5th generation 30Gb ipod that cost me $300. The Sansa clip with a 32Gb micro Sd card does everything that old ipod did, and it cost me 1/5 as much.Pros:- It's very small and light. If dropped, it is light enough that the player doesn't come out of the headphones.- The screen is bright and easy to read. I'm glad I didn't play the extra 10 for the color LED version.- If feels well built. There is a satifying click whenever I plug in my headphones.- The clip on the back is really handy.- Scrolling through menus is quick and responsive. No lag, even with my fully loaded 32Gb micro SD card.Cons:- After disconnecting from the computer, it takes 10-20 minutes to rescan all the files on my 32 Gb microSd card. However, after this initial scan, you can turn the player on and off and it doesn't need to rescan.- The player doesn't play m4u type files (native to itunes), so I had to convert all of these files over.- When I navigate to a genre I can only play by the artist, or play all. I would like to be able to navigate to a genre and the select an album within that genre This is convenient for multi-artist albums like soundtracks.DISCLAIMER: Just so you know, I am a real person, and am not connected in any way to a manufacturer or retailer of this product. The rating I have given this product is genuine.
summary: Almost everything I want in an mp3 player....except playlist support

reviewText: This is my second sansa player, my first clip/clip+. I just spent twelve hours on the road and the battery lasted for a couple hours after I got to the hotel. The sound is fine - though admittedly I bought it for audiobooks. It did not have a problem that I have dealt with with four Sansa Fuze players, randomly shutting off on occasion or refusing to stop playing when paused.I am keeping the Fuze for my music, 4gb, with another 8gb on microsdhc (actually two swappable 8gb cards). I also use my Fuze as a photo album, something of course that the clip+ can't do. But this is a rocking little player. 8gb internal and another 8gb on a card. I love having the variety and on a player that I would probably not notice clipped to my shirt, were it not for the headphone wire weighing it down.I have not tried using the player with the card in it, but would assume that using it with a card will deplete the battery more quickly. My Fuze lasts considerably longer without the card, though it lasts plenty long for me. As I use my players most of the time I am awake, I often keep it plugged in while listening at home or in the car. I was mainly curious about the battery life - the only reason it wasn't plugged in on the way today.I will be back if anything changes, but thus far it has been all I was hoping for and more...(see update below) And I am indeed back. I have discovered that not only does it have the problem with shutting off at random that the Fuze has, it happens more often. And it also refuses to pause with great regularity. I am sending this back and intend to find something else - hopefully something that will not have these problems. (breaking up audiobook files into shorter chunks fixes this - except of course, Audible files are fixed as large files)Update - While I am still less than pleased about the problem with audiobooks, I have to say that this has been an excellent player for my eldest son. He absolutely loves it - especially it's size. He has been using it for almost two weeks (I would estimate abt. 35-40 hours runtime) and it is still above the half a bar for power. It is easy enough for him to use and navigate, the sound quality is good enough for him and he really appreciates the variety he gets out of 4gb internal and another 8gb external. He has several audiobooks that he can read along with (he still has issues with not so easy readers) and just about all the music he wants at a time. As my own Cowon mp3 player uses full size SDHC cards, I don't need my micro cards, so he has four 8gb cards to work with - making it easy as can be to set up cards with selections that can fit his mood (there is a lot of music that is on more than one card - some on all of them).The other great thing about this player is the price. I can't afford to throw down all sorts of cash, but for several reasons, my son's mp3 player is extremely important to him. The main reason for it's importance, is that it helps him calm down and control himself when he gets angry (he has emotional problems that are less his fault, than the fault of his mother and I). It also helps him feel like he has some control over something.
summary: I *did* love it, but alas no more (Update and higher rating)

reviewText: this mp3 player is just perfect! very small, very use to use, the clip is so useful and practical... it remembers what was the last song you heard. and the fact that you can put a microSD this is just awesome!!! mine has now 8 + 16 = 24Go!!!!I have it for just a couple of week, but it is the best mp3 I've ever had!

I have some Audiobooks but most of my books are MP3. I have tried loading them by disk/track#, just track#, used MP3 Tag to check the tags, used Audiograbber to make sure they were coded correctly, and after a month only ONE MP3 audio book plays tracks in order. The others play Disk1/track1, followed by disk2/track1, etc. Some books play tracks correctly for one disk then doesn't even find the next disk.....Get the idea?These are all commercial (purchased) disks and Sansa implies that ALL MP3 disks will play on this gadget.It is a perfect little player in every other way but it will not do what I purchased it to do.
summary: Wonderful Sound but a nightmare for audio book (NOT Audiobooks) listening.

reviewText: I got this as a device to listen to music while I was in my office and working. I loaded it up, and it holds an excellent amount of songs. But I have a few warnings that you should heed toFirst: the program that they send you with the MP3 does NOT work with Macs. It is a .exe file, and so it won't recognize it. If you want to get music on it, you have to manually drag the music into the folder via Finder. Its not much harder, but you don't have the advantage of a program to organize all your music.Second: Sometimes you will start to play a song, and it will begin to skip. It just keep skipping through your songs really really fast, and you have to turn it off/sleep it in order to get it to stop. You have to be careful of that, I don't know if this is just part of the MP3 or if mine was faulty. Either way, it isn't very fun.Overall, this is a fairly good device, good for listening to music, but it has just a few flaws that caused me to lower my score.

decided it was time to stop paying higher prices just because it has an Apple logo on it. This does what it is supposed to and even has an FM radio. Stop buying it just because it is Apple. This is slightly bigger, but lighter and less fragile. No complaints yet.
summary: no complaints yet, replaced broken ipod shuffle

reviewText: This is a compact unit and even if you get a 4 GB unit you can get a micro card inexpensively but there are many flawed units, in general.... no particular seller's fault.

I purchased the Sansa Clip+ in April 2011 and have used it nearly every day for running and working out only.Pros:- small size- light weight- simplicity of design- memory expansion- MTP interface (next three items)- drag and drop via Windows Explorer- can create & use playlists that are simply text files with folder/file names- ability to play by folderCons:- the power button stopped working (I understand this is a common problem)- the headphone jack was kind of bad -- you have to keep adjusting the cord until you can get both channels- the battery indicator wasn't of much value: I could start a run with the indicator down only one notch but it would soon dieBefore the Clip+, I had a Fuse whose display went out, presumably from sweat damage.Now I'm looking for a non-Sansa player. This one last 5 months using it about 7 hours a week.

I've given the same product 4 tries. You'd think, after the first three stopped working on me inexplicably, I would have learned my lesson. WELL, I've definitely learned it this time. Don't buy this no matter how good the rest of the reviews are. Don't buy it in another color either, they're all crap.

I researched various Sansa products and decided on the Sansa Clip+ instead of the Fuze. The device came with usb cable to charge via computer. Once it was charged up, my PC recognized the Sansa.I decided to not install the mini-CD included (Rhapsody software) and just copied the mp3 files I already have on my hard drive over to Sansa's "Music" folder. The resident 4GB in the Clip was enough to store more than 50 albums and 9 podcasts. The FM radio worked great and the sound quality via the included headphones was good too. I have not tested access/use of an added microSD card but I like the option of being able to add more memory.One issue I had so far: the Menu/Home button got stuck when I wanted to switch from FM Radio back to Music listening. I suspect the device crashed after I had finished copying all the mp3 files over to the device. Holding the power button down for 20 seconds resolved the issue.Hoping this cute little player will last. Wish the battery was replaceable just so we don't have to deal with yet another disposable product when the battery finally fails to recharge. Will be looking for a usb to AC/wall charger adapter next.

This is my second one. The first one lasted for several years before it just stopped working one day and I replaced it. I picked the same product because of the price, size and ease of use. And this product gets used close to daily. The clip makes it easy to fit on clothing, except after a while, it did eventually fall off and get lost. But I was still able to use it by tucking it in clothing. The FM radio does work, but I do find, as your body changes positions while wearing it, that the signal can go in and out at times, which can be frustrating. I did get another set of earbuds, as the ones that come with it are too hard and large for my ears. The only other thing I would say is that I don't think it will hold near as many songs as it claims. And even if you erase a song, it really doesn't delete it from the space it used up prior, so don't assume ahead that you can download a ton of songs and just erase and put other songs in it's place. There won't be enough room. But all-in-all, I did reorder the same player a second time, because it served a purpose of allowing me to listen to my favorite music while I was out and about. It is small and compact. Downloading songs on it is easy. And once again, despite what some of the other reviewers said, for whatever reason, my first one lasted for several years and it was used quite a lot.

I must have not researched at the dimensions for this tiny device, as it is very small. However, it is a great Mp3 player and the equalizing adjustment makes it better than my Ipod shuffle (IMO). I added an amp to this tiny rig and I am quite pleased.

I bought this Sansa to use with Rhapsody. The clip, though, broke off after only a few months which makes it surprisingly less useful. Loading Rhapsody songs onto the Sansa has been frustratingly slow and buggy. Maybe that's Rhapsody's fault, but maybe not.
It was nice until it died, just outside the 30 day return period. Now, I have to hassle with Sandisk and ship it and probably get a refurb.Not recommended
summary: Nice until it died, just outside the return period.

reviewText: I have 2 of these now! I thought I had ruined one so ordered another and the original works after all. I had a 4GB last time but the 8 is so much nicer and having 2 is even better lol I use this for my library MP3s and it works so well except getting rid of the book on this 8. On the 4GB I could eliminate the whole books at once but now I have to delete each part, some books have only 6 but one I just eliminated had 24 lol but I'll suffer - I love audio books! I listen most everyday while I do other things like clean, sew and crochet and I also read books and ebooks. Hard to believe there is so much that I like

Initially, I would have rated this 5 stars. I bought it for audio books and the huge memory capability (almost 35 GB) that allowed more than 50 books to be stored! WOW!However, after the first charge I realized two things:1) When you first turn the device on you better be ready to listen because it starts to play whether YOU are ready or not and it doesn't matter if NO headphones are attached!2) When I plugged it in for its first charge it immediately turned back on and then proceeded (over the next three hours) to play 27 chapters of a book while lying on the table unattended. Luckily I remembered where I was so I could back-up 27 chapters which is really easy.There appear to be no system settings (it has a bunch) to stop this "auto-play" problem and makes a simple device a hassle.Really bummed because this is really poor attention to detail in a VERY simple device.

reviewText: Practical, Great design and function. I threw in an extra External MicroSD card into the slot. Easy to use, good equalizers, simple lock function. Probably the best purchase that I have made on Amazon. Very small, just large enough to have a visible screen and functional buttons. I Like how if you power down while playing it starts up right where you left off. Boots up quickly too. Clearly a fan of this product and I dont even like SanDisk for flashdrives etc.

I bought one of these and it died because the wires came loose inside not long after buying it (which is a problem other commenters have noted). I soldered the wires back on. I lost that one, and bought another one recently. It died in about a month.SanDisk used to make a good mp3 player. In fact, I still have a Sansa that has lasted years, included several trips through the laundry. These Clips are poorly made. With how often you need to replace it, you might as well buy a more expensive mp3 player.
summary: Cheap, but still not worth it

reviewText: I was very happy to receive this little mp3 player. It's small, attractive, and has a straightforward setup. It's incredibly light as well, which is wonderful.Unfortunately, something went wrong when I was transferring files. I was using the drag-and-drop method described in the guide and everything was working beautifully, until the window's title bar text disappeared, and then I couldn't affect any of the folder's contents. So, I closed and went to reopen the folder. Nothing happened. I tried restarting my computer and reconnecting the device. Nothing.I figured I would at least see if it would play - it did, but the folder names were all titled "NewFolder(bunch of numbers and letters)", and the sound was unusually tinny. I borrowed another mp3 player to make sure where the problem was, and it was my player.I'm pretty sure I just got a lemon, but I'm too disappointed to try another of the same model, so I'm going to try one of the Coby micro players instead for now. :|Two stars instead of one, because aside from the issue I had, the unit seems well-designed.
summary: Something went wrong. Sending it back.

reviewText: I came home from the gym yesterday and when I took out my sansa clip from my gym bag the clip part of was broken off. I just bought it so hopefully warranty will cover it, but still an inconvenience
summary: Clip Broke Off In My Gym Bag

reviewText: Kind of hard to read the tiny monitor. It is quite small but it does play clear music. The only drawback is the size is small and harder to read. There is a slot where you can add a mini-card into for added memory.

I have a large classic video IPOD that I've used for many years. Thousands of songs are loaded on it and I use it to play my various playlists in docking speakers in both my home and car. Because of its size (and replacement cost), I've always hated to take it on any of my runs for fear of getting it ruined either through sweat, rainfall, or dropping on pavement. A neoprene armband seemed the best option for it, but still it was exposed to abuse.This tiny Sansa Clip+ is perfect for this purpose, though. I bought one as a stocking stuffer for my long-distance-runner husband since he likes to listen to music or audio books during workouts (and, like me, didn't want to ruin his IPOD). After seeing how happy he was with his, I bought one for myself.For starters, my favorite part of it is the size. At only about 1.25" x 2" (and .5" thick, including clip) it's a perfect size to tuck inside a pocket. It also has a durable clip on the back which works well for clipping onto a waistband or pocket edge.I've only loaded about 20-25 songs on my Sansa Clip, and am primarily using mine for audio books. While I would imagine that there is a sound quality difference between the IPOD and the much less expensive Sansa, the difference isn't detectable to my ears for most everything I listen to. The small MP3 player holds an amazing amount of music and books and it is quite easy to download to it using Windows Media Player. I usually can get about 9 hours of listening time per charge; although certain things such as repeated reversing of a book will shorten that time.I hesitate to mention any negatives about it since I'm thoroughly amazed at the quality of this tiny thing for its equally small cost. The only issues I have are that the buttons to stop-reverse-forward are more easily accidentally bumped. This simply becomes a learning curve thing, though, after numerous times of accidentally sending myself several chapters back or forward in a book (and then trying to find my place again). Another possible issue is that sometimes the sound is briefly garbled at the start of a new track; however I'm not sure if this is an issue with the downloading rather than a fault of the Sansa Clip since it doesn't happen with every track change. The final issue that I have with it is something that is simply due to its small size...while its tiny size is wonderful for ease of carrying, it also means that the print on the screen can be quite difficult to read (especially in daylight).All in all, though, I'm very happy with it.
summary: Its tiny size fits in a pocket or clips on...great for taking on walks or runs

reviewText: I really wasted time purchasing this thing. After dealing with an ipod shuffle, this was downgrade. I wanted something quick and easy to use. This was not it.

About two years ago, I bought my 1st Sansa Clip (SC) to replace my iShuffle due to its lack of flexible control for file folder management and for repeating a single song.After two years of happy and heavy usage, the clip was broken a few days ago, and I ordered a 2nd SC which came this morning.While checking on the product info on the web, I found the new firmware version update. Without further checking, I went ahead to update my old SC to the new V01.02.16A firmware, and then my headache began.First, with the firmware update to v01.02.16A, the old SC is no longer recognized by my PC (Windows XP-Pro-SP3), i.e., Windows Explorer could no longer recognize the Sansa Clip as a removable disk.I spent almost one hour to search a quick reset or restore. Based on some suggestion on similar but different problems, I tried to (1) reset, (2) format, (3) press the power button and hold for 15/30/60/... seconds, (4) press the power button while holding down the middle button, ..., nothing worked.Then, I called Sandisk tech support, and here's what I was told.1. "You have to update Windows Media Player (WMP) in order for Windows Explorer to see the removable disk."2. "The firmware cannot be down-graded (to revert to the old version)."Now, since I'm using the free VLC for playing all kinds of media, and since I don't like to be forced to use the WMP, the only alternative for me now is to look for another MP3 player other than the SC and the iShuffle.For this 2nd Sansa Clip just ordered from amazon, since it also has the new firmware version installed and becomes now useless without updating WMP, I have no choice but to return it.-----------Work-around for the USB non-connection:while turned off, hold down the middle button and then connect the USB cable, and the sansa will be seen as a USB removable disk.-----------More problem with the 2nd newly ordered Sansa Clip (black).1. the player died away while sitting on the table for several hours, and it's now dead, completely dark even with a USB connection.2. the earphone jack is so bad that it disconnected the plastic cover from its internal wire when pulling the earphone jack out; please note that the same earphone (JLAB) has been paired with the old Sansa and never had this problem.
summary: firmware update (v01.02.16A) destroy its USB connection...

reviewText: My spouse has used this model and found it suitable. I bought one from Amazon and had to return it because I could not get it to function. OK, I got a bummer and thought I would try another. Bad decision! It had the same problem. I could charge the battery and upload content, but could not get the menu to work. Therefore it was unusable. Look some place else for a MP3 player.
summary: I tried two and neither worked

reviewText: I have 2 fuses which are getting old now, but they still work great even after dropping them several times each. I wanted something smaller without the color screen. This is the one that I decided to get. I got the re-manufactured one saving a little money. The ear phones are not the kind I wear, so I can't comment on them. The player itself is great because it uses a mini usb plug that is very common. The only problem I ran into is that not all usb cables are created to work with the Clip + . I have a few cables with the matching end and only two out of six worked with this unit. Of course the cable that comes with it works fine, but it is only about a foot long. The Clip+ loads audiobooks from Audible, and Overdrive. When loading from Overdrive, you must go to advanced and rename the music folder to Audiobooks, so that when you access the book in play mode the book actually shows up in Audiobooks. If you forget that step, the book will show up under Music with all the songs that are on the unit. Using external memory is not a problem since Audible is no problem since Audible creates an Audible folder that shows up under Audiobooks on the unit's menu. Sound quality is typical of Sandisk Sansa line. Earphones have much to do with sound quality. I use ones that I like that are the in-ear type. The Germans make great earphones.

I am very happy with this little MP3 music player. It is tiny and extremely lightweight. The only thing I am disappointed with is the reception quality of the FM tuner. I own an older version of the Clip (with the round control dial) and it gets better FM reception than this version. Highly recommend, if you want a reliable player with good sound quality, and you aren't worried about trying to impress people with an expensive label!Pros:- Very small and lightweight.- Surprisingly good sound quality.- Spring clip securely holds player to sleeve, shirt pocket, or other piece of clothing.- Expansion slot holds micro SD card for extra storage capacity.- FM Tuner.- Great value.Cons:- FM reception is not as good as previous version of Clip.- No user replaceable battery.

I've owned two Sansa Clips over the past six years. Not bad longevity for a device that accompanies me to every visit to the gym (I workout 4-5 times a week). It's been bumped, dropped, banged around and has never broken. I had one issue with the "clip" part of the device breaking, but Sansa was great about sending me out a replacement part at no charge. I have to say, Sansa's customer service is great. The current player I have is a refurbished player that I got when I sent back the 2nd player that I bought because it froze, so in reality, I'm really on my 3rd player in six years which still isn't bad considering the use it gets.I have a Rhapsody subscription and the device is compatible with the service. For the most part, loading music on it via Rhapsody works fine, however, there are some pesky errors that I will occasionally get that I believe are more a problem with Rhapsody than my Clip. If I have an established playlist that is set to "auto-update", occasionally I will find that songs from the playlist are deleted from my Clip although I didn't delete any on the playlist. I can manually grab and pull them to the playlist while my Clip is plugged into my laptop, but I have to do it each time I plug my Clip into my laptop to sync it which is a pain. This has been a problem as long as I've had the Rhapsody subscription. Now that Rhapsody bought Napster, there isn't another good option for a music service that lets you download unlimited tracks to a device (if you know of one, please feel free to comment to me).You can't beat the size of the Clip and the clip holds quite good to whatever it is clipped to. I do wish the headphone jack was located at the top of the clip versus the side, but that's just my preference. The display is nice which is a big advantage the Clip has over the little Apple clip device (the name of which escapes me).My biggest complaint about the Clip is that it will die for a period of a few days to a week whenever any (and I mean ANY) moisture gets near it. So if you've got it clipped on your shorts and you're doing some intense cardio at the gym and sweating, know that all it takes is a little drop of sweat to hit the Clip and expect to be listening to a song and all of a sudden have it go quite on you. You can push buttons till the cow comes home, but the thing isn't going to be going anywhere until whatever got wet inside of it gets dry again. You can use the blow dryer, put it in the sun, shake it, used canned air on it --- it is going to restart when it is good and ready. Unfortunately, if I'm not plugged into my music, I cannot work out -- period. So I'll need to use my Android phone in the interim which I hate doing because it's so much bigger, so much more fragile, and since I don't have an arm band for it, I have to put it in my gym shorts and accessing it isn't quick if I want to switch to the next song or turn down the volume (plus, the volume is no where near as loud as it is with my Clip). I've been thinking I'll buy another Clip when I see them on sale to keep in case I need a backup, but that is a pain because I'll need to deauthorize the Clip that died and authorize the other clip with my Rhapsody subscription (I have the $9.99 monthly subscription that only allows syncing to one device -- it costs $14.99 for the subscription that allows syncing to three devices). If I sound cheap, I am because I haven't worked for the last year, otherwise, I'd just go buy the backup Clip now and switch to the higher Rhapsody plan, but I have to watch every dollar I spend these days. But the point I'm making -- and the reason it gets a 4-star review versus a 5-star review from me -- is I shouldn't have to have a "backup" player at all if the Clip was made better to prevent moisture from shutting it down.I've noticed little silicon cases available on Amazon for the Clip and I'm thinking of getting on, but I'm having a hard time figuring out if they are compatible with the Clip I own. I've read some comments saying that one was made for the first version of the Clip that had the power button on the side and none of the product descriptions I have read have mentioned exactly what version of the Clip their case was made for so I'm reluctant to order one.Overall, I believe the Clip is the best non-Apple player around and I didn't want to go the Apple route. I am thinking of picking up a Clip Zip -- the newest model, just so see if it is better about the moisture issue -- but again, just got to wait until I see one on sale.
summary: Great player for the gym, just beware of sweat!

reviewText: Owned and used for 3 weeksComputer/OS: Crunchbang (Debian and Linux based)Features I like:- Small, light, very portable- High-contrast display is easier to see than I expected- Decent battery life- OGG and FLAC support- FM radio- Ability to connect to PC as a usb flash drive (which means it is compatible with my Linux distro)Features I don't like:- Firmware (even the latest) is buggy (see write-up below), I fixed this by removing SanDisk firmware and using Rockbox (rockbox.org)- When running, I clip it to the bottom of my shirt, upside-down and it eventually will come loose and fall off. So I have to find a way to clip it to something right side up.- Confusing battery charging indicatorThe firmware on the device has some issues. It garbled my song's ID3 tag information so navigating my library by Genre, Artist, Album, etc. was not possible (I could still play all of my music, it was just completely disorganized on the player which made navigation & song selection difficult). So I split my music collection up by genre and created a folder for each genre in the hopes of navigating by folder. This worked ok but not without problems. I had a folder titled "Folk" and another "Folk Metal" in the clip's memory; when I tried to navigate to the "Folk" folder on the device, it would not display, then I noticed that all my "Folk" songs where displaying in my "Folk Metal" folder. I connected the clip to my computer to see if I had copied them over to the device wrong; when viewing the contents of the clip on my computer, there was clearly a separate "Folk" and "Folk Metal" folder each containing the correct songs, but when you try to navigate to the folders on the clip (ie, I want to play a song from my "Folk" folder) the "Folk" folder does not exist and the clip lumps all of my "Folk" songs in the "Folk Metal" folder.To remedy the inherent problems and limitations of the clip's firmware, I simply used the open-source Rockbox firmware (rockbox.org) and it works flawlessly with more features, options, and navigation capabilities than the stock firmware ever provided.Overall, if you are tech-savvy and can comfortably replace the firmware, it's a good lower cost alternative to an ipod nano that is compatible with more advanced operating systems (such as Linux).
summary: Buggy firmware, rockbox to the rescue

The headphones & this mp3 player are just the thing to motivate you kick up the workouts a notch.The player has a clip built into the back of it which is great!
