reviewText: I've owned 4 of these, two clips, and two clip+. Every single one has failed, each in its own way. The power button stopped working on one, another one the computer can't recognize when it gets plugged in, and the other two just froze, the screen froze, and the battery died and can be no longer be charged or turned on. None of them were dropped or damaged before they died, the just fritzed out for no discernible reason. The average life I would estimate at about 6-7 months, some died earlier some died later. I actually really like this player, that's why I keep buying it, I just cannot justify buying another one of these things, knowing that it will only last about half a year and die. It's a great little player, if it was reliable I would literally give it 5 stars. Sansa, PLEASE TAKE LONG TERM RELIABILITY SERIOUSLY, YOU ARE DOING IRREPARABLE DAMAGE TO YOUR BRAND.Edit: They released a firmware update a couple months ago which FIXED all four of my "broken" players. I have a suspicion that they were programmed to fail after a certain number of hours, and they changed their mind when everyone complained so they released a firmware fix to make the player work again. Upgraded from 1 to 2 stars.

This is a great player; but don't waste your time with the hard copy instructions. Go to the website for a comprehensive set. That's how I discovered the volume control button. It's tiny and set on the side out of sight, and appears like just another accessory port (you have to be under 40 to be able to see the '+' and '-' on it w/o glasses). Once you discover it, however, it works just fine and you'll discover a unit that can really pump out the sound, whether it's connected to ear buds or a car stereo's AUX port.

Warning! I left this device connected to my laptop to charge, over night. It charged to 75%, only. I attached it to a desktop for a couple of hours. It charged to 75%, only. The only button that worked, occasionally, was the on/off button. I sent this item back. Am waiting for a refund.
summary: I do not recommend this device.

reviewText: Well.....have to say that this little unit packs one heck of a punch for its size, let me tell ya ! Small, Compact, Light. Download simple as can be and the Sound is great to boot ! Best thing....did Not cost you a arm and a leg. If you are looking for a MP3 without a ton of bells and whistles....easy to set up with great sound.....for the price you can Not go wrong with this SanDisk ! I would Defintely Recomment this item to anyone out there in the hunt for a MP3.

I have had a couple of Sansa e2X0s and absolutely loved them. After many years of use the ON/OFF button started to fail so it was time to get a new one. With smart phones eating into the MP3 player market, the options were slim. I decided to try the clip, despite the very cheap price. I ended up returning the unit because it was defective. I put a 16 Gb micro card in and tried to sync 8 Gb of music to it through Windows Media Player. It failed multiple times. It also rebooted on me when I was playing it in my car (the battery was full). A good MP3 player for $30 was just too good to be true. I have joined the next generation and am using my smart phone now.

I lost my old MP3 player. I read reviews and shopped at stores. The reviews helped to convinced me as well as the SanDisk name. I was shocked to see how small it was. I like the 4GB size, my old one was only 1GB, so I can store a lot of music on this one. I works great.

I'm editing my review because after less than a month of very light use the device has stopped working. Won't power on. Won't charge up. Won't do anything. What a cheap POS. Very disappointing. Will never buy a SanDisk product again.
summary: A nifty little gadget - until it stopped working.

reviewText: Tried three different connectors -- earbuds, speakers, and auto MP3 cable. The unit was not able to hold them securely enough. Playback was very spotty with gaps in sound. Returned it.

The SanDisk Sansa Clip+ is a nice little music player. It is very small but the display is bright and easily readable.There is one BIG gotcha. It ships in "MTP" mode (it's default mode). Unfortunately in this mode it corrupts folder names (even though music plays just fine). It's an easy fix (if you know about it) to switch it to "MSC" mode *before* copying files to it.The included earbuds are fairly poor but they do work.Navigation is a bit clumsy but after a little familiarity it's not all that hard to use. It does take a lot more "clicks" to get to something than my Samsung player did.Battery life seems to be fairly decent, I've never come close to draining the battery.Update: It died! In the middle of playing music it just plain stopped and won't power on. Five weeks is not a long lifetime for an electronic device like this (considering I've got other music players which are over six years old and still working perfectly). So I've dropped my rating from four to two stars. I'd drop it to one star but I may buy another because I can't find any other device that is designed as nicely (including supporting the OGG format)

I was really disappointed with this product, especially with all the great reviews on amazon. I was not able to get the advertised battery life of 15hrs or even close to it. I initially thought it was due to a defective battery so I requested a replacement from Amazon. When I got the second one, same thing!The battery would not last for more than 5 hours max. I experimented with this to see if I could increase the life like turning down the brightness, only listening to the radio, etc., but that did not make much of a difference ... went from 4.5hrs to 5hrs max. Anyways after the second one had the same problem I ended up returning it too.

I did not realize that I was buying this wonderful little MP3 with a required membership or subscription for Rhapsody. Am I just missing other ways to use it or will it always die off without the Rhapsody subscription?

Not a bad product if you're willing to be without an mp3 player while it charges. I prefer a battery (alkaline) operated mp3 so I can always have it working when the charge goes dead (by replacing the battery).
summary: had to rewrite this review after I figured the thing out

reviewText: I got this because I've had to exchange two smartphones; I was keeping them in my pocket at the gym, and the cord was getting pushed/pulled against the jack, eventually causing the jack to short out. I figured something that could live outside of my pockets would fare much better.I was surprised by the sound quality, even plugged into my stereo. For smaller speakers, there's lots of EQ presets, or you can make your own. Klipsh S4's are my new fav headphones. Sounds perfect with the EQ turned off.The navigation is well thought out. Easy to jump around, and you can browse your library while songs are playing. You can browse by album/artist/song/genre, playlists, recently added, top rated, podcasts, audiobooks, recordings, or... folders! That's for those of you that're too lazy to properly tag your audio files. If your stuff is already organized in folders, just drag/drop those folders onto the player, and you can navigate/play by folder. Each folder has a "play all" option to play all of the albums underneath a particular folder.For those that do tag, google "mp3tag" for a great free app. I also have a new appreciation for Winamp. Create a new playlist based on what's currently playing, right-click, send-to-device, and done! Anything that's in an unsupported format (m4a, aac unfortunately) will get converted to an mp3 on the fly. Lots of other features and plugins for syncing, but that's mostly what I care about - finishing what I'm listening to at work during the commute.There's 8GB internal storage, and it takes up to 32GB external cards. Sadly, it takes a long time for the player to scan a new card, so you won't be swapping cards in and out a lot. I also hear that having a card drains the battery more quickly. Battery life is excellent, btw. Supposedly 15h of playability, or ~10h with a memory card inserted.PROS: Compared to a shuffle: this has a SCREEN, an FM radio (easy jump between presets), FM/Voice recording, and expandable memory. Compared to a nano: a fraction of the price, well laid out physical buttons that you can operate by feel, expandable memory, FM radio, FM/Voice recording.CONS: A big part of Sandisk's business is selling memory cards. Could that be why there's no locking cover for inserted memory cards? And why they're spring-loaded, so bumping them will cause them to eject? I'll never put more than a CHEAP 8GB card in this thing. And I won't buy it from Sandisk. So there.I haven't tried the audiobook or podcast features, but there's some options in the player UI for handling those.

For $30 this MP3 Player is a good value. What I don't like about it is the inability to easily organize songs. My old SanDisk Zen 5 player was great about this. It was easy to put songs in Album folders and organize them sensibly. The Sansa Clip makes it easy to create Playlists, but it simply refuses to recognize my album folders as such. So, good price and decent player, but not great interface-wise.

Wow, what a disappointment! I own a Sansa View player, that I absolutely love, and had picked up the Clip back in January to use as a tiny, lightweight player for my gym workouts.Barely outlived its 90-day warranty before refusing to charge or turn on (I switched out charging cables to make sure it was the player, not the cable, that was faulty.)The other thing I disliked about this player was that it could only connect to Windows 7 in a mode that apparently did not support transfer of playlists. I could sync music files just fine, but it never recognized any of the playlists I'd set up.I guess you get what you pay for, but 100 days? C'mon!
summary: Okay while it lasted...which was exactly 100 days

reviewText: As you may observe in another review, the dirt-cheap, cockroach-tough Coby MP301 is my favorite expendable MP3 music player. If I'm in the Boundary Waters or CAMBA, I just pop in another AAA battery (never littering) when the thing runs dry and continue beating it up! But let's face it, even at 256-320 kbps, MP3/AAC sound is a grainy caricature of the real thing.In the higher-priced, recharge-it-and-treat-it-kindly realm, the Sansa Clip+ is so good I've given away my iTunes-afflicted (okay, I actually used CopyTrans Manager as a sanity-saving substitute) Apple iThings. Good riddance. What's the deal?When I really want to listen to music, as opposed to having a background soundtrack for kicking-out-the-jams, LOSSLESS digital playback is the only way to go. The ill-fated Microsoft Zune allowed lossless WMA playback, albeit at a premium price. That was then, this is now. Behold the petite Sansa Clip+. It supports pristine, full-fidelity FLAC lossless playback. It does it incredibly well. And it does it at an incredible price point.As a bonus, the Clip+ also lets you instantly swap 16GB microSDHC cards, even with a protective rubber jacket. Don't try that with an Apple iThing.Because lossless files are easily inter-convertible, I simply transform the WMA files I ripped from CD (which, for quality reasons, is how I prefer to purchase music) to FLAC. Done and done.With exemplary headphones (e.g. Grado), the sound is absolutely top drawer and breathtakingly glorious. Get some!

I've had mine since September 2010. It's march 2011 now so it's been six months since I purchased it from Amazon. I got it to listen to audio books, and it worked beautifully for about 3 months. But one by one the buttons are not responding. I have to click the button 10 or more times in order to get a response. This has happened to the Pause, Home and fast forward buttons so far. Guess I'll have to check the warranty. Other than the button quality it has been great

The first one worked fine for about a week.Then it wouldn't hold a charge overnight. It would be fully charged when I went to sleep and dead in the morning. I made sure it was off before going to sleep.Now, after owning it for less than a month, it completely died.I returned it and Sandisk sent me a new one.The new one lasted about a week. It just suddenly died while I was running and wouldn't turn on.Now I get a 3rd one that should arrive today. Hopefully it won't quickly break like the other 2.I guess you get what you pay for.I don't think the unit is very durable. If you plan on exercising with it clipped to you, you should probably opt for something else.

This is a great little portable music player. So many more features, flexibility and storage capacity than the much more expensive one trick pony - the iPod Shuffle. I use it for workouts mainly, so I organize my music based on BMP/tempo. For example, all the 130-145 BPM songs are grouped into a single folder so when I go running, I will play music in that folder. I have another folder for slower walking music, etc. You basically drag and drop songs into the player. Very easy. No special software needed.I have never used the SD card so I taped the slot opening w/ a small piece of clear Scotch tape to seal it from dust.The only reason I took a star from the rating, is because it cannot read AAC/m4a files directly. Luckily my Windows 7 will automatically convert all of my m4a files into mp3, but doing so takes much longer time. If SanDisk updates this model w/ the m4a file support I will grab a new one without a second thought.Note: plug for the headset is very tight so I had to push hard to get a full contact. Once in it won't get loose so it's perfect for sport/workout use. I use my own Bose headset.UPDATE: If you want AAC/m4a file support out of the box, do not buy this product. Buy the Sansa Clip Zip instead. It's only slightly more expensive than this model. Or, you can replace the stock firmware with Rockbox and it supports AAC files plus other additional benefits.
summary: Excellent in everyway except no m4a (AAC) file support

reviewText: Packaging was terrible as it sealed the headset wire into the plastic, Leaving me with just the Clip and angry that I had to order another set to cover the loss. Other than poor packaging the Sansa clip itself is actually pretty awesome, easy to setup and put my songs into. Too bad the factory killed my review.

I followed the instructions that came with the player but could only get it to play the very first song I loaded on it and then only sporadically. I could never get anything on the menu screen except a set of headphones. No menu or anything. I spent over 4 hours trying to troubleshoot and get the thing to work. That's enough for me.Note that the earbuds that came with it are too big for my ears and so are uncomfortable. The earbuds that came with my Fuze were fine and I used them probably for a couple of years before I had to replace.Also, it seems like the plug for the earbuds sticks out too far, like it's ill fitting and when I tried using it while jogging, it wiggled and jiggled around and the sound went off and on with every step. I don't want to break the player by trying to force the plug in deeper because you can feel that there is quite a bit of resistance there so I'm not really sure what the problem is. Quite frankly, I don't want to deal with it.I have a Sandisk Fuze that never did hold a charge like it was supposed to that I was too lazy to send back and now I'm not particularly impressed with this Clip either. I think I'm pretty much done with SanDisk and will be trying my luck with something else.
summary: Can't Get Anything To Come Up On Screen/Plays Sporadically

reviewText: I purchased this player as a gift for my 7 year old grandson. The controls are very easy for him to use. Another plus was that no external software was required to add music. Just plug it in to any USB port, the computer recognizes the device and you can drag and drop music. The USB cord that it came with is a little short, but who doesn't have spare longer USB cords laying around? He is very happy with it.

I got this because of the good reviews, and because I thought I could use a smaller, cheaper music player with no fancy HD screen like I used to have. I was very shocked at how tiny it was when I got it. The buttons are very confusing, as there are no clear function buttons for things, you have to keep using the '<' and '>' for everything. Also, when I loaded about 6 CDs onto the player, and then started it to listen to the songs, the player would just skip right over about 20 songs, with no clear reason. It wasn't on shuffle, and all the songs were loaded the same way, all were mp3 files...I am disappointed, and it was also very annoying having to bypass the insane amount of Rhapsody spam and trying to get me to sign up through the site, saying the player wouldn't work unless I used that site/program for my music. Well, if that's why this player was screwed up, then I will go with a different brand now.

I had never had a mpg player before but since I was due to fly a great deal I decided to get this little inexpensive one that seemed to have good ratings. I actually gave it a 4 star because it does a good job and you can download a great deal of music on it very easily and also extend your music selection 4g more with a mini card.My main complaint is either the little guy is defective, or I am unable to find ear buds whose connector fits in properly enough that it doesn't keep cutting out every time it is jiggled a little....so much for clipping it to your shirt when you exercise or jog. I finally clipped it to the sun visor in my car and after going through several kinds of ear buds was able to find a pair that were secure enough (although they still cut out) that it plays pretty solid unless I accidently move the wire when adjusting sound, etc.I had tossed out all the paperwork and box so I was unable to return it so I can't say if this is a bug with all or just mine. As cheap as it was, it just wasn't worth the hassle. Sound is good, clear and can be turned up quite loudly.
summary: For the money, it is Okay

reviewText: We have been very pleased with the Sansa Clip+. Its size makes it easy to carry around, and the sound quality is nice, even when outside with ambient noises. Transfering music is quick and easy, and the menu is designed for easy access to albums, audiobooks, or customized playlists.The menu is easy to navigate, but it does have a tendency to freeze if skipping multiple songs in a playlist.Overall, this product has proven itself a great value for the price.

I needed something to replace my Sansa fuze. I've owned two Sansa Fuzes, and the second was not nearly as good as the first. It failed after six months, screen blanking out, ear phone plug in failing and freezing/turning itself off/ ect . . . you can read that review if you want. I have owned many Sansa MP3 players, and been very pleased. I would have purchased another Fuse, given it one more try, but its doubled in price! Litterally. And, since I use my players at work, I wanted something smaller that I could just hook to my clothes or badge. I was thinking I would have to buy something small but with a arm band or something, so when I saw the Sansa Clip, I thought my prayers had been answered.As I read in other reviews, the sound quality with this little guy is really good. Its better than my Sansa Fuse! The portability is great. I can just clip it to myself and leave it, walk around work, and not worry about it. The screen is wasy enough to read, if I hold it within a foot of my face (I could read my Fuse from further away). It has the features I used most in the Fuze, playing songs and audio books and listening to the radio. The first thing I noticed was I was unable to adjust the screen brightness as far down as I wanted. It saved a lot of battery life in my fuze when I cranked it way down. This may help explain my biggest disappointment with the Clip.The battery life is no where near what I saw advertised. I charged it when I got it, leaving it plugged into my computer for hours, and noticed the first day that the battery lost charge rapidly. After just 2.5 hours, I was down to half. So, the next night, I left it charging in my computer for four hours. The next day, it seemed to be better. I got through 5 hours, and it still read a little over half full. I forgot to charge last night, and today, I only got 2 hours out of it before it shut itself down. I had just looked at the screen a few seconds before it died to change the volume, and saw that I still had half a charge left. The battery icon was only half gone. Now, I haven't been using up the battery by lighting up the screen. I haven't been changing songs or volume or stopping and starting. I have been listening to an audio book, just putting in my head phones and letting it run. So, I got maybe half the hours advertised. I feel jipped. I just hate it when I purchase something, spend money on something (i'm on a budget, so fifty dollars isn't something I can easily spare) and have it not work as advertised. I can't plug in USB anything to my work computer, so can't charge that way at work. I ordered a wall charger, and I hope that will solve this problem. \I also had problems with my 2G SD card and my audio books in general. I had to clear, format and reinstall my SD card twice before the Clip seemed to "take" it. It wouldn't display everything I had saved on the card. It seemed to have a problem especially with my audiobooks. I took all the audio books off, put only music on the SD card, and all the songs SEEM to have installed, but I can't be positive. In addition, the audio book playback is not always easy and smooth. Sometimes, I try to play them, and the Clip does this weird skipping thing. It won't play the sudio book, skips to the next one. When I go back and try again to play the audio book, it then skips ahead two books, and so on until none of them will play. The first time this happened was when they audio books were on the SD card, and taking them off and putting them on the internal hard drive seemed to fix it. But, then it happened again, and I had to format and re-install, and now they seem to be working. So I hope I won't have that problem anymore, but I can't be sure since the first thing I did was format when i got it, and I had problems. Also, when playing the audio books, sometimes they skip. Its only happened a handful of times, and it only skips a few seconds, and if I miss anything important, I can rewind and it plays through the second time, but its really annoying. I shouldn't have to do that! It should play these things just fine!Honestly, I regret my purchase. I hope the last fuse I had and this Clip aren't an indication of future Sansa quality because I've owned Sansa's for YEARS and always been loyal because of their durability and quality. I won't be purchasing another Clip. I may try a Fuze again if this one doesn't work out, but I am about out of hopeful chances . . .
summary: Doesn't live up to advertised features

reviewText: Today my sansa clip died without warning, after 16 months of light use. The player won't power on and charging it via USB through a computer or plug did nothing to it other than making it hot to touch.Pros:1. Play with folder view, instead of by album or artists.2. Small (could be a con-may lose it easily).3. Good sound quality.4.Micro SD slot support upto 32gb (does NOT support 64 gb sdxc-tried already, so there is no doubt)5. Has a radio and voice recorder.Cons:1. will randomly change my file names and adding meaningless ".SID" extension files. This is very annoying.2. Battery not removable, so if the battery is dead, you are out of luck.2. Won't last long--USA has 1 yr warranty and Europe has 2yrs, why is the discrimination toward US costumers? Now my player is dead after 16 months and I'm out of warranty. Have to throw it to the trash, what a shame.Other thought, maybe wait until I get a Samgung galaxy S4 and it supports 64 micro SD card and use my phone as a mp3 player.

reviewText: This one doesn't recognize my sd card more than half the time. Died once and finally later came back to life. Died again and hasn't returned. May go for warranty. Battery life was excellent. Sounded good.

I've had a similar, older model of this product which broke after using it several times, so i was skeptic about the quality i would get. All i can say is that the product has delivered everything it promised, and then some. The main feature that i was looking for was the battery life, which i have to say that it really is close to 15 hours, even at close to maximum volume. It also has a lot of nice features that very basic mp3 players in this price range normally don't have - like the ability to delete a song, to select an album, an artist, to create a playlist, etc. I can't speak for the recording quality or the radio as i've only been using it to listen to music and podcasts. I want to mention for those that feel the volume is too low that it has a power saving setting in audio options which toggles from normal volume to loud, which still gives great battery life. I wish the clip would have a bit more strength to it so that the mp3 would stay clipped even if it brushes against something, but that is something very minor which is not worth taking away a star for. The 4 gb memory is decent and i was able to put a good amount of music on there. If that is not enough, you can easily buy a micro SD card - which are very cheap - and quickly increase the storage size. After using this product, i don't know why anyone would pay more for an mp3 player, when this one does just about anything you can ask of it.
This MP3 player is very tiny, So if the small size is what you wantthis is adequate as a budget size item.
summary: This MP3 player is very tiny...

reviewText: Amazon was quick to refund my money. But I was disappointed. I have purchased 3 SanDisk Sansa Clip players in the past 2 years. The first one failed after a year. The second one works well and I've had it for 2 years. I like the player. It's easy to use and the clip is conveinent. The audio port on the indigo player was defective. Production quality control is lacking big time! I won't try another one.

I have had this device for a few months now and when I wasn't using it regularly I was very happy with it. However, I've started using it more and have found the battery life to be extremely disappointing. I almost wouldn't mind that the battery life is short if it would TELL ME. It has several bars to notify you, once it is 1/2 full....that means its about to die at any moment. Sometimes I'll turn it on and it will say the battery is almost full (one sliver missing) and then it will die within a couple hours of play. I've gone out for a run multiple times and had it die mid run which is extremely frustrating.I've tried plugging it into my car and if you do that with the volume up high the battery life is absolutely terrible. Using it in this capacity will drain that battery within a couple of 30 minute car rides.The next problem with the battery is that it takes hours to charge back up....so after it suddenly shuts down on you you have to wait half a day before its charged up again. UGG.I understand it was a cheap device, and I would be ok with a short battery life if it could convey itself to me accurately. I don't feel like I can trust it to work when I need it to.....so ultimately it's going to need to be replaced.UPDATE 7/24: It just officially died for no reason -it won't charge or turn on. After <7 months of light use it is completely dead. I am extremely unhappy with this product at this point as you can imagine.

2nd one, first one started giving garbled audio then would not power up.2nd one Used less than 6 hours, gave a error that more memory was needed for the database even with only the original songs. Now won't power up.
summary: Would be great if the thing worked more than 6 hours. 2nd one with problems.

reviewText: This is a great little MP3 Player. Light and sounds great. I upgraded the ear plugs since I didn't care for the set that came with the player. The price is more than reasonable considering the prices for other MP 3 Players.

Love the size of this device and it has worked well in the cold which is one key thing I was looking for. I wish that it had a clock/stopwatch function and I wish it was more intuitive to create/manage playlists. I realize that music can be managed through Windows Media Player, but I have my MP3 collection organized in iTunes, so this is just one more complicating step. Not the end of the world and I'd purchase this again.
summary: Device is very good; management of music content is just OK.

reviewText: It worked for a few weeks. Wont turn on,even if plugged into computer. I had one several years ago and that one had a battery that wouldn't hold a charge. I thought I'd give it another try... You'd be better off buying something else

with only a $30 price tag ($20 if you can find a good deal on the web). Its perfect. Light weight. And if it gets destroyed you don't care as much if it were an IPOD. Out fit it with the $8 Sony earphones and its a match made in heaven. I have 4 of these. Buy them when you can get a good deal. Work every penny.
summary: perfect mp3 player for the gym

reviewText: This is Mac compatible, but you can only load songs like adding files to a flash drive, no song lists without Windows software included. It is probably fine for Windows, but I'd rather by another Ipod Shuffle for the money and my Mac.
Ordered this to use with FLAC Files. Try as I did, I could not get a peep out of this tiny player.

This Sansa MP3 player lasted only a month for me and it died suddenly. Otherwise I would have giving it a lot more stares.OTOH I have an older Sansa ExpressTM MP3 Player 2GB, still going strong after 2 years of regular usage.I did like the newer Sansa for the short time it worked, mainly because it could FastForward much, much quicker than my older one.If you buy this one, save your sales order/receipt for credit or return in case it suddenly dies on you. It might not be as rugged as the earlier-designed Sansa players.
summary: Good, but didn't last long for me

reviewText: I now have bought 3 of these. 2 that are 4GB & 1 that is 8GB. Be aware that the ones with the circle "button", on the front, are the older models. I liked the way it lighted up around the circle, but it does not have the memory card slot or the "folder" option. On the newer ones, the "folder" option allows you to see & play all of one artist's songs or albums.At first, I did not think that I could delete songs, then I studied the instructions, and realized how simple it is. Not sure why, but when I connected the Sansa player to my desktop computer, I was able to see a list of what songs are on the player and delete from there. When I connected it to my laptop, I was unable to see any lists.I love that it is so small and portable, and that it has that clip feature! It is 1 of the top 5 MP3 players!For Christmas presents, I intend to send the 4 GB ones, with a set up of my friend's special songs & albums, that I have collected on my computer. One friend is a walker and she will now have lots of "walking songs". WOW, will she like how light & convenient, this Sansa is!
I really like this gadget it's a nifty little player and I'm looking forward to listening to many of my CD's while attending to other task ...
summary: I love this thing it's super

reviewText: hard to use, controls are confusing and this thing quit working all together after a few months. Buy something else

Pros:- cheap and lightCons:- Takes forever to transfer songs to- Horrible music management. Tried all methods to sync itunes playlists or WMP or even Winamp but all didn't success..Bottom line, don't buy this product. it doesn't worth the time or a single penny on it.

I ordered this item because I wanted to run with something small and my ipod was too big. I was so excited to get this cute little Sansa clip, and used it nearly every day for almost one year. About a month ago things weren't quite right. The clip said that I didn't have enough storage for my mp3 list which was actually just a fraction of the full size of the clip. I removed some items, recharged and off we went for another 2 weeks. The same message popped up again, but as long as I pressed the middle button and the >>> button, all was well. This past week, in addition to the "not enough storage" message, a new message started popping up when I turned the clip on. "Refreshing Your media". That didn't seem too bad as it seemed to refresh (at this point however I was much more worried). Today the death knell. The "Refreshing your Media" message will not go off no matter how I try to turn the clip off. I even tried to reformat with paperclip to the back side, but alas nothing changes. I have plugged the clip into my computer, but it makes no difference. I fear this little clip is dead and it makes me very sad. Buy another???? Sigh. I just don't know. Oh Yes I do!After thinking about my Sansa clip, I decided to change the stars from 3-1. I am furious at my Sansa clip because it led me to believe that it had overcome the itunes issues, could be formatted with Mp3's and that I would have a trusting relationship with it for longer than just 11 months. Why should you waste even $40 on something that betrays you. I did not get it wet, I kept it in my jacket pocket or running pants pocket. I did not charge it unless the battery had been "low". I never dropped it or abused it in anyway. I put great African songs on it. It is dead for sure, and I have to say, "DO NOT BUY THIS ITEM". Spend more if you have to and get a product that doesn't die in less than a year.

I am returning two of my most recent purchases of the sensa mp3 player. Not all were made the same. The first two I purchased were very very good. I used them for a long time. Everyday use. Wow. Now, I just purchased two new ones, and they were DEFECTIVE. Oh, my. Maybe they are making them from cheap parts, maybe they went under a MANGNET before arriving to me. Do not know. But, both were bad. The music skipped and skipped and skipped some more.
summary: My most recent purchases were DEFECTIVE, but read on

reviewText: So far so good. This was a presemt for my wife. She has a nice I-pod classic but it does not have FM radio built in. The FM is needed at the gym so she can watch the various televisions while working out. The gym broadcasts the audio on various FM frequencies.Very light weight and battery life is excellent.I was surprised to learn though that the organization of music is very limited.

This was my second SanDisk Sansa Clip+. The first was 4 Gig, the second, 8 Gig . Neither lasted more than 6 months. I think I was pretty gentle with both. The worst thing I did to it was run the battery down to the nub a few times. (Most rechargeables last longer if you recharge before they are empty.) My 8G died this morning after about 2 songs. I thought maybe the battery had run down, but my USB charger at work wouldn't "wake it up" (the device seems to come on when you plug it in).Previously, I was able to recover from this by connecting it to my home computer, but that did work this time. It's basically a sealed unit so it looks like this is my second little Sansa brick (or maybe a Lego is more appropriate). Maybe that's just the lifespan of these guys since both lasted about as long. I'm not convinced it's the battery alone as it was routinely holding a charge for more than a week running it 45 minute each way on the train.Not sure I'm going to try another Sansa. I've grappled with whether, given my needs, it is worth dropping $100 or more. On the other hand, I've spent nearly $100 on 2 Sansas and got less than a year in total. I wonder if I'd get a couple of years out of a Nano- which would make it a better price-performer.While it worked, by the way, I thought it was a nice little unit- good sound and battery life, and easy to use.
summary: Not Very Durable In My Experience

reviewText: If you're looking for something to play MP3's but not video you don't need to look any further. These Sansa Clip+ devices are perfect and, unlike most players, allows you to expand your storage (and keep extra with you) with the use of a MicroSD card. In addition to the performance, the ease of use, and everything else that is great about them they use Mini USB connectors to both charge and load your media so it'll work with cables that most people already have. There is no need to worry about software compatibility because they will function as a USB drive and all you need to do is copy your media over to it and it will do the rest.

I purchased this with Super Saver shipping and it arrived yesterday. Today was the first real "field test", taking it out into the world with me. I tried both the FM Radio and the MP3 player functionality.The bass is a little shallow on the earbuds, but what do you expect for something that comes for free with a $35 player? They serve me well enough.The FM Radio works about as well as it can be expected to work with such a small form factor. My older (much larger) sports radio that I used to carry in my briefcase actually can't compare to the Sansa here, so as for this aspect the parts are definitely of very good quality.My one gripe - and it's a major one - is that .m3u functionality is very borked on this player. I have been using computers for almost 2 decades and I am definitely of the "tinkerer" mindset, and I could not for the life of me get .m3u or .pls playlists to work across directories. (So for example, if you have songs sorted by band in folders and you have a playlist trying to access songs in both folders, the playlist will just show up as empty.) This is a MAJOR flaw in the MP3 player in my opinion. The only real solution is to dump all of your MP3s into one directory and make playlists from there.If they fixed this it would have been a 5/5, but considering how this product is a fair bit older I doubt it will happen. Oh well.
summary: Good for the price, with one glaring flaw.

reviewText: I really like this player. Great sound. Easy to download to. Can have tons of memory with a 32gb MICRO SD card. I just like their older models better. They were larger so it was easier to keep track of where it was and it used a wheel on the front. Not these push buttons arranged in a circular fashion. Please bring back the older style player.

The whole reason I got this MP3 player was for the audiobook feature. But none of the books I have downloaded will go into the audiobook section. I finally manually moved them using a windows program, after being told repeatedly that it was unable to move them via some error message.Nothing I have downloaded went where it was supposed to go either. I copied an audiobook (cd's) into a playlist to ensure they were in the right order and when I loaded it into the sansa, it rearranged it based on author, so it was 1) not in the 'playlist' section and 2) the sections were no longer in order, which made it worthless.It is nice and small, but even the navigation is bizzare. I am happier with my sony walkman and should have just bought one of those and dedicated it to only audiobooks. At least it is expandable I guess, so if I can ever get the books to go on correctly I can fit a few more in there.
summary: Not all that happy with Sansa

reviewText: I bought one of these as a gift for my grandmother. Packed it with songs she loves and at least managed to get her away from trying to find tape players everywhere now. Anyway, the thing is a bit too small to be friendly. While I'm sure it's size makes it perfect for runners, the average user won't write home about its size. The menus are simple enough to navigate, and the screen isn't difficult to read; even with its small size. It does what it's supposed to do, and has yet to break. But that's pretty much where the pros stop. The included headphones are not great. No charging outlet came with it (just the cable for charging purposes). Options are supremely limited with regard to docking to an external sound source. And the battery dies in a matter of hours from full charge. So the product works, is easy to navigate, and isn't priced too high like other MP3 players you'll find. But there's still much to be desired by the average user.
summary: Decent, but I wouldn't buy another

reviewText: I take this to the beach this is great you can load you music on a empty disk and this takes up little space in the beach bag

Worked fine for a couple of weeks; then it started not powering up, even when attached to computer. Then for a while it would; then for a while it wouldn't. Just too much aggravation. Price was good, especially if it would've worked reliably. Oh, well.

This was a Birthday gift to my son. It was a lot smaller than I had anticipated, but it was a good price. It was easy to load songs to it and it did not take long for him to figure out how things work once we figured out how to change it from French to English (can be a challenge when you do not read or speak French).

I want to listen to MP3s. I don't want to pay a fortune to do that. I don't need to look at pictures of an album cover, I don't need to take pictures while I'm listening, I don't need GPS to tell me where I am, I don't need anything -- I just want to listen to MP3s. I just want a simple, durable, reliable little device to play MP3s.So, after looking at my options, I chose this. This does work, and it has been pretty reliable. So when I gave mine to a friend, I replaced it with...another one of these. I just don't think there's another device that is (a) "good enough" and (b) not too expensive.The good things are that it has a rechargable battery that lasts plenty long, and it recharges whenever it's attached to my computer. It's small and very lightweight. It has been rugged and durable enough. It comes in very pretty colors.The bad thing is the interface. There are just lots of annoyances. Nothing fatal or deal-breaking. Just annoying. If you put a folder of music onto this, often it will put some random characters in front of the folder name. So when you're going through the folders, trying to find the one you want to listen to, instead of looking at the end of the list for "ZZ Top", you might need to look at the top of the list, for "B2GHKZZ Top". And the screen is small, so all you'll see is "B2GHKZ". It's just annoying.And what I mostly use this for is listening to baseball games. I'll record the radio broadcast with my computer at night, and then listen to the game the next day. So it's a 3+ hour MP3. The buttons are...fiddly. Let's say you want to fast forward 2 minutes, to skip the commercials between innings. Ok, press and hold the fast forward button for about 4 seconds. But...sometimes the button gets confused, and it thinks you tapped it, instead of holding it. If you tap a fast forward button, what happens? It goes to the next track! Ugh. So now you have to go back to the baseball game MP3, and hold the fast forward button to get back to where you were. Oh, you don't know where you were??? You had been listening to the game for a while, and you know you're at the end of the 4th inning. Ok, so how far should you fast forward? 50 minutes? 70? 30? As you maybe can imagine, it's very annoying. Fast forward some, listen to see if you already heard it, then fast forward some more, listen to see if you already heard it, fast forward some more, now you're too far and you have to go back... Don't blame the user. There are a lot of devices in the world with fast forward buttons, and I don't have this problem with any of them. Just this MP3 player. And it's not THIS specific player. I've owned two of these, and they both did this.Also, I listen to a lot of BBC radio shows on this. They're usually around 30 minutes long. Sometimes I'll stop in the middle of one. Sometimes the player will remember where I stopped, and sometimes it won't. It's just annoying.So it gets 3 stars. And more importantly, yes, I would buy another one of these if I lost the one I have now. It's really annoying, but a better-working MP3 player would cost a lot more. Getting rid of the annoyances is not worth the extra money.
summary: I hate it, but I bought another, so I guess I don't really hate it.

reviewText: I bought this to replace my beloved old Sansa E140 MP3 player(which still works fine) as I wanted more memory capacity. My needs are simple: to play MP3 files while working out at the gym.The 8 MB Clip + fulfills the basic requirements. It's easy to load files (just drag and drop on your PC) and straightforward to operate. There are a couple of nice features such as several "equalizer" settings, the ability to create playlists, plug-in module capability and an FM tuner (don't count on good reception for anything but the strongest local signals. This is not the MP3 to buy if FM listening is a priority for you).The clip (much maligned on the original model) seems OK but its just plastic, after all. Be gentle. I was surprised at how tiny this player is - about half the size of an old-fashioned Zippo cigarette lighter.I have the following criticisms:a. Battery issues (docked 1 star). The Clip + has a rechargeable and NONREPLACEABLE battery (apparently the norm now). When the battery fails to hold a charge, as it inevitably will eventually, you chuck the whole MP3 player. Right now (near new), it holds enough charge for a weeks' worth of my gym workouts but the jury's still out on this.It takes a GOOD two hours to completely recharge on my computer's USB port. The display has a battery charge level icon but it doesn't appear to be very linear and, of course, when it decides the battery is too low, it abruptly shuts off.Another quirk: When I disconnect the unit from my computer's USB port, the display goes dark. Silly me: the first time I assumed the player was therefore off. Not so. You must still push the power off button to actually shut it down; otherwise, it remains in play mode.b. Useless earpieces (docked 1/2 star). I admit I'm not a fan of "in ear" earpieces (I prefer over-the-ear headphones). But the supplied earpieces I found to be particularly worthless. Even sitting at a desk, I couldn't get them to stay in my ears longer than about five seconds. Totally useless for gym workouts. Figure on buying your own earphones/headphones.c. Poor documentation (docked 1/2 star). The unit comes only with a single sheet "quick start" instruction page - which doesn't even contain enough information to quick start. To get the full instruction manual, you must go to the Sandisk website (the quick start sheet had the wrong web address) and download it. Call me old fashioned, but it pisses me off to burn up half an inkjet cartridge printing the instructions out. Even my cheapo Casio watch came with a complete (if miniature) manual. Sandisk could sharpen up it's technical writing on the instructions, too.Other things to know: Before using the unit, go to the Sandisk website and download/install the latest firmware updates. Also, my player came with preloaded "sample music" that you'll want to delete before adding your own.JUNE 2012 UPDATE: Well, My Clip+ has failed in less than two years. The problem is not the battery as I would have expected: it is repeated freeze-ups of the firmware. I have the latest firmware update installed and only about half the memory capacity used - nonetheless it freezes up every five minutes or so of use. Performing the "master reset" unfreezes it but the problem just recurs. Even removed and reinstalled my MP3 files - no effect. My conclusion is that Sansa MP3 players work well - WHILE THEY WORK. But if you're gonna buy one, consider it to be a short-term throwaway item and make sure your files are backed up somewhere. Maybe I'll try an iPod Nano....

After a few dozen uses the headphone jack input started losing contact. This resulted in losing audio to one earphone. Within a few weeks after this the sansa clip stopped taking a charge, now its on the way to the trash can.

I bought another make the first time (Hipster). Sandisc Sansa Clip for the extra cost is very superior. MP3s and technology is new to me, but I can manage to work it quite well. I like using it if I can't sleep in the middle of the night. I like to use it with padded headphones.I can find the buttons in the dark quite easily. It is very intuitive....easy to use. I bought one for winter home and ordered another one for permanent home.

Since I received the Sansa Clip. I've had nothing but issues trying to get it to sync to Windows Media Player. It will show up in Windows Media Player trying to sync, and just as quickly, disappear. If I'm lucky, after 30 minutes of watching this dance of showing up, and disappearing, it'll finally sync to where I can download music to it.I've gone through this routine several times and I'm over it. It has nothing to do with Windows Media Player, because since purchasing the Sansa Clip and becoming beyond frustrated with it, I purchased a Sony Walkman MP3 player and it has no issues with syncing up to Windows Media Player.Other than the Clip not syncing, it seems to work flawlessly and has no issues being recognized and playing through my car USB.The Sansa Clip would have been all I needed in an MP3 player, but alas, it wasn't meant to be.
summary: Not thrilled with the Sansa Clip

reviewText: This is the third Sansa MP3 player I've owned. The Clip this replaced was very good but had one major annoying factor. It took a while to boot up. After I updated the software it would index all the songs each time it was turned on before you could play any music.I've got a 16 gig card in my new Clip Plus 8 gig. It boots up quickly, in seconds unlike maybe a minute like my old Clip. Be warned that it will a while to index the songs when you add music, mine took maybe 5-10 minutes but then I do have like 3000 songs. Each time you add a song it will re-index when you turn it on. But if you are just turning it on without adding anything to it, it's fast!Like everyone else, I think it has great sound and is to small you almost worry about losing it. I just wrap the earplug cord around it, using the clip to secure it and pop it in my pocket.There is one annoying thing and maybe I'm doing something wrong but the memory in the clip and the card are treated as two different memories when hooked up to Windows Media Player. This means that you just can't add 20 gig of music to the Clip despite your 24 gig (16 gig card and 8 gig memory). You have to put some on the card and some on the built in memory. Just a pain but at least it all acts as one memory for playing songs.

I bought this at the very beginning of September 2011 and I've been really happy with it defects and all until it died on me two days ago. It's really dissappointing because I took very good care for it but after reading the other reviews, I see I might not be the only one having a similar problem, which there are tons of reviews on. It suddenly stopped playing one day, didn't drop it at all! I tried to plug it into a usb adapter to charge it, but it hasn't turning on. I figured, I got what I paid for at $22 -- I got it off a Woot! deal. I probably won't invest in another one of these and attempt to keep looking for an Apple mp3 player alternative, but will that ever be the case? There were other problems prior to it also; for one thing, it can't play high quality mp3 files or handle a complex file very well. So this will make the battery drain faster, i.e. you might have charged it last night, but it could die well within 3-4 hours of continuous play. In order to make it last longer, you'd have to bring the quality of your mp3s down. Which sucks during long commutes on public transportation. You also shouldn't use the equalizer too much either since the "added" features drain the batteries too. The filing system can get rather messy, but it's so tiny and functional, this didn't bother me too much unless I had to have things playing in a specific order. And my last gripe is the audio was a bit low, but I could just be going deaf...Some things I did like about it:-the fact that you could turn it from a 4gb to a 32 gb mp3 player with the miniSD card.-If I had audio books, it would have been really useful because it leaves off where you stop/pause by going to another folder.-It was small and cute, extremely portable, would have been perfect for exercising.-really inexpensive mp3 playerWell, I suppose it was a good 4 months, but that'll be all it will be now. Sigh... off to find a better brand and maybe not be so cheap.

I like my Sandisk. I download songs and audio books on this player. It is very small and I just clip it onto my shirt. I work outside in the yard a lot and because I can clip it out of the way, it doesn't get hung up on plants and other grabbing things. It has good volume, it picks up on the stories where I left off and it is convenient. It does Mr have bookmarking, but it does resume where I left off. I cannot use it with audible also.I have a Creative Zen, but it is bulky to use outside. It also gets locked up and I have to fiddle with it to get it to shut off. I have none of those problems with the Scandisk.. It was VERY reasonably priced and I am pleased with the value.

In an age of high-end, expensive tech and MP3 players, people like me always got lost in the dust... that is, people like me who don't necessarily have $100 or more to spend on a good, name-brand MP3 player just so they can listen to music.But I found the SanDisk Sansa Clip+ 8 GM MP3 Player a good compromise and a decent "budget MP3 player."For it's relatively low price (clocking in at less than half the cost of most other bigger-brand MP3 players I browsed through), it's of a very good quality. The product itself is very small and compact, but easy to use and navigate. It does feel a tad on the brittle side, but still more-or-less sturdy.The sound quality for its price is fantastic, even using the cheap ear-buds that came for free with the player. And I was able to very easily dump about 6 gigs of music onto the player by plugging it into my computer. The battery does seem to wear down a bit on the quick side (generally lasting 1.5-3 hours depending on how often I use it, how much I press the buttons or change the volume, etc.), but I can forgive this since I don't usually use it for more than an hour at a time.I have heard complaints that these players sometimes stop working after a few months, but in all honesty, for the price, I don't see that as too big of an issue for me. It'd be easier for me to replace one of these than an iPod.The only other real issues is that it is hard plugging in headphones and then unplugging them- the headphone jack is a bit on the snug side, meaning you have to be quite firm, which I found awkward. But that's not too big of a detractor for me.

SanDisk Sansa Clip+ 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)I bought this to give to my brother who loves to listen to music. The computer detected the player initially. So, I started to load it with music; I spent several hours doing it. When I was done, I wanted to try it. I hooked it up to my earphones, but it wouldn't even turn on! No matter what I did, it wouldn't work. I've had one Sansa MP3 player before that gave me many hours of enjoyment, so I didn't have any apprehensions buying this one. But this was a total disappointment. Not recommended.

The problem is that these simply do not last;I have purchased several due to the size and excellent sound quality for the price but just expect to replace them every 5012 months because they don't last.But this LAST one only worked for over a month and died on me.Not sure I will buy the same model again.
summary: Lasted for all of 6 weeks before started to malfunction

reviewText: I'm on my third Sansa clip in 6 months, they all work fine for a month or so, and then freeze and won't boot up. I am thoroughly disgusted, and am moving on to a different brand, too bad because the clip is the perfect size for an mp3 player. My guess is that at some point some genius at Sansa made a design change that allowed for clips to be manufactured at a lesser cost, as the older ones seemed to work just fine. DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME.

Update: The original one of these that I bought is (so far) still working like a champ. However, the next 3 I bought have all died -- the last 2 within a week or two of receiving them. I noticed that they felt cheaper, for instance, when I plugged into the audio jack and when I plugged into the USB jack. It is like they are using really cheap parts or something. The symptom? They play for a while, and then they make a loud pop and quit playing and the screen goes dead. I am giving Amazon one more try to give me a unit of the same quality of the original one I bought. If it works, I'll try to report that here. If not, then I'm probably going to give up on this player. What a pity. It was a lot of functionality for a very cheap price, but if it doesn't work, it's not worth any price.Original post:The single thing that adds the most value to this player is the HCSD slot in the side. As far as I'm aware, you can put any capacity card in this slot. This essentially turns a 4GB player into a 20GB or 36GB player (maybe more?), depending on the card. Plus, if you have a pocket full of HDSC cards, you can swap out your music "instantly" without having to have a PC handy.I say, "instantly," because it takes between a few seconds and a few minutes for the player to scan in the titles off your media, when you change out songs (regardless of how it is done), depending on how many songs you loaded.One other feature that is very valuable to me with this player (besides the fact that it can also RECORD as well as play), is the fast-forwad feature. I listen to a lot of voice recordings, and the ability to fast-forward/fast-rewind to catch technical details is a huge time-saver.I have found that the player sometimes doesn't know what to do with MP3 files I load on it, until I play with putting them in various folders. It was a little non-intuitive that my Clark Howard podcasts would have to go under the "Music" folder, but once I figured it out, it hasn't been a problem. Not sure what that is all about, and I haven't found any documentation on the rationale and rules behind where to put stuff. Whatever -- it works.The other thing that took me quite a while to figure out is the order that this thing plays the MP3s. It seems to sort solely by the track name. For instance, I had some Alexander Scourby CDs that I ripped to MP3 so I could listen to them while I exercised/commuted. It wanted to play all the track-1 files first, then all the track-2 files, etc. I had to find some free software (SimpleTag GUI for Mac OS-X, and Audacity for Windows) that allowed me to hand-edit the track numbers so all the books and chapters would line up properly. For over 1000 MP3 files, that took a while! You can use Mutagen Python library, or if you Google "Dive Into Python" "Chapter 5" and maybe a few other key words, you should be able to find some Python instructions that you can use to do all the edits automagically a whole lot faster than hand-editing, but that approach is not for everybody. =)This little player is almost like an audio Swiss army knife! Fantastic job, SanDisk!!! Keep it up!

Sansa this is for free, please listen: Love the Micro SD addition to the Clip+. it makes the cheapest 16GB+ player in the market and sound quality is as good as the original. The Bad: The turn on/off mechanism is a disgrace. I know adding the SD took away some real estate from the unit, but, the on/off mechanism is cheap and a disaster I go over 3 units to prove it). Please replace with something similar to the original a solid big slider. Battery duration, I dont know if it is because all my music comes from the SD unit, but Battery time is reduces to 1/3 of the original unit. One charge would be good for 15 hours in the original clip. One charge in the Clip+ is only about 5 hours... so there, I'm ready for the Clip++. Best regards.. Me.
summary: Time for a revised version Clip++

reviewText: I love this little player. I have an older Sansa player that I purchased years ago and it has held up well but only has a small amount of memory. I had a Sony and it died after a couple of years and it was much more expensive that the clip. The other thing I love about the clip is the memory card slot. I installed an 8G card in mine because I already had it as a spare for another device. With the installed 4g that gives me 12G which so far has been enough. It will hold up to 32G, which I am seriously considering. As for reliability it has held up very well. However, it has locked up on me twice. All you have to do when that occurs is reset it by depressing and holding the power button for 20 seconds.As a general recommendation to folks, I do all my playing via playlists. It makes it much easier to load and play the songs I want in the order I want. Some of the reviewers have complained about the memory slot not having a cover to keep out dust. I purchased a neoprene cover for mine that fits the bill for that and doesn't interfere with using the buttons. They are available right here on Amazon and they are cheaper than dirt.

Purchased after I lost my Ipod Nano. Overall I'm satisfied, please see what I like and what I don't.Pros:1. Very good for audiobooks, incomparable with Ipod nano, keeps bookamarks for several books at once.2. Practically unlimited memory. You can use as many inexpensive 8 or 16 gb cards as you want.Actually,if to use memory cards, you can purchase device with 4 gb internal memory and save some money.3. Convenient clip and device attached strong enough.4. Easy to transfer files from computer to the player, much more convenient than to create I-tune playlists and to transfer files to Ipod.5.Good battery life.5.Very reasonable price.Cons:1.Not user friendly navigation.2.Dipsplay quality is not the best, difficult to read file names.3.Takes time to find the proper files, because all the time you have to pass through many options - radio, recordings, podcasts, etc, etc.4.Too short USB cable.In spite of some negative things I like this player and recommend it.However, if Ipod nano would cost the same price I would take Ipod due to easier navigation and better display.
summary: Excellent for audiobooks, practically unlimited memory

reviewText: This is great for audiobooks. There is plenty of room to get 5 or 6 (probably even more) titles on and its controls are much easier to use than the Samsung players that I've had in the past. Sound is very good and there is enough volume to overcome exercise equipment using Sony on ear headphones. I just hope that the headphone jack holds out, that's what did in both of the Samsungs.

Updated on 12/2/2013SanDisk saw my post and offered a solution to the problem that I had with the pops in the FM recordings. That is really great customer service. I've upgraded my rating accordingly (4 stars from 3. If the problem never happened,it would be 5 stars. :)Original post below:Pros:Easy to transfer recordings to/from the Sansa using the USB cable.Glad it uses a standard mini USB cable.Voice recordings work wellFM recordings work ok as long as the FM signal is strong... see Cons below.Cons:When recording on an FM signal that is not full strength, the recording process introduces a click or pop about every 1/3 second that is very annoying. It is strange because when listening to the FM broadcast direct through the headphones while recording, the sound is fine. You don't hear the clicks until playback. I think it is a flaw in the recording algorithm. I have had to use aftermarket recording filters to try and remove the clicks.
summary: Good for playing music. Recording problem resolved

reviewText: I've had this player for less than a year. It was great while it lasted. But now it will charge up on the computer but it won't turn on.

I received this item yesterday. I read and reread the minimal instructions, and charged the unit. After playing with it for several minutes, I realized there was a piece of plastic covering the screen, which had to be removed. Nowhere in the instructions was that noted. I downloaded some CD's from my computer, and attempted to hook it up to a small portable speaker. It would not work, although we have used other MP3 players on it. I then tried it on another speaker. It worked, but only if I held it in my hand, not allowing the plug in the player to move. Finally, I tried the include ear buds. They worked fine. By this time, I was totally fed up with the unit. After posting my review, I read a comment from Sandisk that the earbud jack may be very tight when new, and to force the jack in. It worked! Now I only semi-dislike the unit.

I'm trying to learn Turkish. I've down loaded every language disk I can find to this and then I've recorded a bunch of stuff off You Tube on the voice recorder. This thing works flawlessly. This thing quit on me within a few weeks of normal operation. It simply won't turn on anymore, Wish I'd gotten something else.

I copied a folder containing 766 files of various sizes and total 20.4 GB onto the card. That took 40 minutes and 59 seconds --> average 8.5 MB/sec. Then I copied 355 files (9.4 GB). That took 18 minutes and 8 seconds --> average 8.9 MB/sec. So in both tests the write speed is a little bit shy from the nominal 10 MB/sec but not too much off. Reading back and binary comparing with the original files from the first test took 28 minutes and 21 seconds. So the reading speed is 12.3 MB/sec.

reviewText: This card has, over the past three weeks, performed flawlessly with my Nikon D7000, which I have used to take and transfer both photos and 1080p video. Otherwise, imho this card is plenty capable of handling most people's burst needs.Slightly off topic, but as a sub-rating, I gave this card three stars for "storage capacity" because it has a truly "average" amount of capacity...as compared to other 32 GB cards. What a silly thing to rate -- two years ago, this capacity would have been thought gigantic, and two years from now, it will be small. There is a separate rating for "value for money," which takes into account the capacity vs. price. So I'm not sure why Amazon is asking reviewers to rate "storage capacity" as an attribute. Anyone?

reviewText: I don't usually write negative reviews because whining goes against my nature. But I feel an obligation to share my bad experience. I bought this card along with a Canon EOS Rebel 4ti. Checked the card, checked the "Safe" tab, put it in 2 different card readers on 2 different PCs. Only contained photos that had been taken the first week.I am an IT person and have software to recover deleted and lost data. I do it for people often. But there was nothing to be found on this card but a dozen old photos and two dozen deleted photos. After accepting that they were gone forever, I tried formatting the card in the camera and on my PC. It would not format. Still contained the original dozen photos.Maybe I got a bad one and this was a fluke. But I'll stick with SanDisk from now on.

reviewText: In fairness I have to say I've used Transcend cards over the years without incident or problems.However based on some of the reviews here - I think it's fair to say the class 10 really does have a speed rate of a class 6 according to clocking by any number of sources. When the card arrived it took multiple efforts to format - as I dug deeper into the reviews albeit most are positive the complaints were pretty much all the same:* Trouble formatting* Cameras not turning off* Distortion and surprisingly slow rendering time for a class 10My first inclination was that the problem was within the cameras card reader so I placed a call to Panasonic Pro cam support. The feedback I received was in a nut shell to stick with Sandisc as they've had numerous calls regarding problems with the Transcend cards.Bottom line - these cards may be less expensive but cheaper of course never means better. I think for certain applications Transcend is still a find choice for low to mid level cameras and camcorders. However as the tech I spoke with put it - when you've spent 2 grand on a camera - don't skimp on the memory cards.

I recently purchased a Canon SX40 camera and this card along with it. I have never had a memory card error before, but there's a first time for everything. It didn't start right away. I took about 70 pictures and 2 videos before things started to slowly crumble. On a couple of photos, the camera could not view them and called them "unidentified images". When uploaded to a computer, those photos did transfer, but strangely only 1/2 the picture showed up. Then the total breakdown occurred when the camera simply told me "memory card error". I couldn't view any images, nor upload any that hadn't been. I originally put the blame on the camera, which was clearly wrong. Camera's fine. Couldn't be better actually, now that that card is out.I contacted Transcend and they directed me to their website where they have a lost data recovery program for download called "RecoveRx". I downloaded it and gave it a try and it did recover most of my photos. It took the program about 9 hours of running time to do this btw. Unfortunately, not all pics were recovered and definitely not the videos (which were the most important things on the card!). I sent the card in to Transcend and they are in the process of sending me a new card...which will work this time...right? The only way one can professionally have their memory card resurrected would be to send it overseas to the tune of 3 months processing time plus who knows how much $. I weighed the cost and time to the need to get those videos back and it just didn't add up. So I cut my losses and am getting a new card. I am certainly gun shy at this point though in shooting photos. I'm sure things will turn out fine in the end, but I'm longing for the days when the only way you could lose your photos was to open the back of your camera by accident!Best of luck to other Transcend card users out there, of which there must be quite a few.

A quick look at the frequency response graphs at Innerfidelity or Goldenears backs this up. Mids are recessed and vocals are difficult to make out especially when mixed in with complex music. The highs are decent but can be a little shrill with some recordings. After equing (dropping the bass, increasing the mids and dealing with hump in the highs) the sound improved significantly. The bass was tighter and more complex, vocals stood out more and the sometimes shrill highs disappeared. The overall clarity of the sound improved. After equing, did they match my more expensive IEMS (GR07 BE)? NO (not even close) but they did sound a lot better.Overall: Definitely worth $5-6 and even more so when equed.

reviewText: This thumb drive lasted less than a year of daily use. I used a USB port extender cable to try to lessen the wear-and-tear on the drive's USB interface. After days of no problems in use and being frequently transferred between computers, I ejected the drive using the Windows Explorer eject function. No computer would read the drive after that. No green light, no mounting sound, nothing. The one thing that that was different was that I was using a new work lap top for the first time, As noted, it functioned fine when mounted to the computer and ejected properly, but would not work again in any computer after that, including the one it had just been ejected from.Because I regularly backed up the drive to an external hard drive at home, and synced the most used files to another location at work using a free Microsoft utility called Sync Toy 2.1, I lost no critical data and have decided that I will not pursue recovering data from the device. Still, the failure of the drive was inconvenient and annoying. Most users of these drives know that they do not last forever, but my prior ones have lasted much longer than a year. Viewing flash memory drives as (un)reliable as old school spinning drives is the best policy. It could fail today, it could fail in five years, but it will fail.My new thumb drive is from Iogear. It is different in that it is a card reader for a variety of SD cards. My hope is that having the flash memory on a removable card will reduce the vulnerability of my data to hardware failures. Instead of having to toss out the whole drive, I will hopefully be able to move the SD card to a new reader and keep on going.

I've bought dozens of these Kingston flash drives over the years. Loved them. They were reliable, the flashing LED was bright enough to be seen through the plastic handle, and the folding clasp is a great idea.I just bought six more, of a couple of different sizes (16 GB and 32 GB), and at first I thought they must all be defective: none of them flashed to show that the drive was in use.I broke one open and they are completely different on the inside to the ones I've bought previously. Instead of a small circuit board with a tiny LED, there is nothing. The memory chip is now small enough to be almost entirely located in the plug itself: the handle of the drive is just empty space (hold it up to the light and you can see right through it).The memory chip is housed in a plastic clip that holds it in place in the plug. However, the plastic clip has a prominent hole right where an LED would need to go to be where the LED used to be in the old model, and, clearly visible in the hole, at the top end of the memory chip, are a couple of gold connection points. My two guesses are: 1) Toshiba (the chip manufacturer) intended an LED to be attached there; and 2) Kingstone just couldn't be bothered to do so.With these drives, then, you have *no idea* when your computer has finally emptied its buffer to the drive. You can no-longer just wait for the flashing to stop then remove it from the USB port; you have to keep trying to "safely eject" it until you are no-longer told the drive is in use.Well, that and when I have a row of flash drives in my USB hub, the flashing was the only way I could tell which was the one I was saving data to...If you use your flash drives for semi-permanent storage, I suppose the lack of a data transfer indicator may not be a deal breaker. For the rest of us, though, these things are no-longer top-of-the-line flash drives. They are just junk.

reviewText: Worked good for writing and reading files fast but the case is flimsy plastic and broke off in my computer. I will by Kingston again but only f they offer a metal case. I will not buy plastic again. Price was good so another instance of getting what you pay for.

I bought this thumb drive from Amazon for $38.68 (Currently 39.75 ... the price changes) and used a free utility that I downloaded from the Internet (H2TESTW.EXE ver 1.4) that will display read/write speeds in addition to capacity. This device (USING THE AFOREMENTIONED UTILITY ... OTHER UTILITIES WILL PROBABLY YIELD DIFFERENT RESULTS) yielded 58.1GB TOTAL space with speeds of 4.15MBytes/Sec Writing and 16.00MBytes/Sec while Reading.Conversely, the SanDisk Ultra 64GB microSDXC Class 10 Memory Card (that requires an adapter (which it comes with) and a reader (which is an additional expenese, typically less than $5.00) to fit in a USB port cost me $58.96 (Currently $49.53 ... the price changes) (again from Amazon ASIN B009QZH6JS), and using the same utility yielded 59.4GB TOTAL space with speeds of 8.76MBytes/Sec Writing and 24.6MB/Sec Reading.NOTE: ALL chips will yield slightly different TOTAL space available, as they will inevitably have a different number of "Bad Sectors" crop up when formatting.NOTE: H2TESTW.EXE ONLY writes a bunch of SMALL files. If it wrote LARGE files, it would in all likelihood yield faster results.NOTE: this data comes from an Intel based desktop computer (DELL VOSTRO 200 ... good machine that's lasted for years) running Windows XP. XP requires these high capacity chips to be formatted using the exFAT format in order to make use of all available space ... yah, yah, i know it's old as the hills, but it STILL runs fine ... gimma a break.So Kingston vs SanDiskKingston> Cheaper> a TINY bit less TOTAL space available> only runs about half the speed as the SanDisk chip> has a light indicating Read/WriteSanDisk> More expensive> a TINY bit more TOTAL space> runs twice (about) as fast> NO light> requires an adapter & reader to fit into a USB portThere are a LOT of chips/Drives out there ... do your research ... and then YOU decide what's most important to you in the Cost/Size/Speed arena.
summary: Cheaper, but Less Capacity and Slower Than a SanDisk uSDXC memory chip

I have always been told that Kingston was tops, and in the past I've been very happy with their products, epecially the old Data Traveler, which had you put the cap on the opposite end when you opened it. No more lost caps! The entire line has been redesigned to this new style of metal top. So far I've had two. I did a lot of research on indoor TV antennas. This one was the highest rated.At one point it picked up 50 stations, great, except all of them were the upper channels.22-70. There's not a lot I want to watch up there.I want the broadcast VHF, you know, NBC, ABC, FOX, CBS.I wanted to watch football when the game is on locally.I'm 16 miles from the transmitter according to the charts.I can't get any of those reliably. Maybe if I move it around, it works for a couple hours,then it breaks up. My living room is on the wrong side of the house, away from the antennas.The problem is my (Samsung) TV doesn't allow you to "add channels". You have to search again.I'd love if it had a "signal strength" meter, like my Sharp Aquos, but no. It will be hunt and peck.The design and workmanship is top notch. Even the cable is nicely finished. The amplifier is powered by myUSB port on the TV so I don't need to plug it in (ac)Sunday, I'll try it again or compare with my huge and awkward Terk rabbit ears.UPDATE:Well, I held the antenna in my hand and tried several locations. Here's the problem.Your body makes a difference. The best signal was when I stood in the LR holding the antenna over my head like the statue of liberty.Obviously, that wasn't a solution, so I tried on the wall, but good spots broke up when I walked away.Also, make sure you don't touch the metal connector because that will make your body part of the antenna. (It gets better)Nothing was perfect for all channels, but oddly, the best compromise was placing the antenna flat on top of a lamp in the corner.That's where it remains today. I watched Fox football and later NBC Sunday night without touching the antenna.Now, Mohu has jacked up the price by $6. Jeez, this thing is getting too expensive, I need another for the bedroom TV now.Maybe I'll try the Amazon for half the cost. I tried Wal*Mart's $10 rabbit ears in the bedroom, and they sucked. No VHF.With modern TV's you can't tune to a channel and play with the rabbit ears. You won't see the channel unless it's decent enough toscan in. So moving the antenna requires another scan.
