reviewText: This antenna works surprisingly well for such a thin little thing! It actually picked up more channels than a heavier-duty version we purchased locally. We found that we received the same number of channels whether we placed it in the window or on a wall so we have ours on the wall behind some books - you can't even see it! Great buy!

I had this for about a month now. It is true that it needs to be in a sweet spot for more channels. And after moving it all around my living room in every direction possible, I could only get 18 channels at the most. And out of those also, the receptions is very pulsating. If the weather is cloudy, 3-5 channels are lost. And if there is wind, all video channels have trouble keeping up with the minimum signal strength and start showing "Now tuning" text on the screen. The most interesting part is, I loose reception of the channels who have transmitting towers within 10 mile radius.The three starts are for its portability, ease of erection and having a good quality reception (when it works) . I need to add, it is not true that this is a multi - directional antenna. When I change the directions, the channels do change.
summary: Not as good as the claims

reviewText: I've been without cable for a couple of years now, and was very excited about the possibility of receiving a couple of local channels. Unfortunately, I tried several locations around my television room, and was unable to pickup any channels.I emailed customer service, and had a response back in about an hour. They sent me a report showing that even though stations were well within range, the terrain in my area negatively impacted reception. They had me try the antenna with no amplifier, still to no avail. A second email was also answered quickly.Customer service was outstanding, but unfortunately the antenna didn't work for me.
summary: Great service, but didn't work for me

reviewText: This indoor antenna is great! It's not the powered version, but my previous antenna was powered and included an 'External Antenna In' coaxial plug. I just plugged this antenna into my previous one and now all our channels are perfect. My other antenna was really crappy, but it was powered, this basically replaced the antenna portion, juiced it up a notch and now we get channels that we didn't even know were available.I would say that if you purchase this antenna for indoor use, either upgrade to the powered model or do what I did. It doesn't work the best if you can't amplify the signal, in-fact, it's probably not a good idea to use this unpowered unless you can put it really high, and most likely that would be outdoors, which this isn't rated for.I also liked the fact that it's white on one side and black on the other, and should be able to fit most people's decor.

I was hoping to pull in more channels and this antenna did not really do that. I agree with the reviewer who said the higher the antenna is placed, the better. If you are using it on the inner walls with some house interference and far distance from the towers, I think the only solution is to get an "ugly" outdoor antenna.
summary: Pretty solid indoor tv antenna but not without negatives.

reviewText: I had a directional antenna from winegard for a while which I loved but kept on tripping over wires. I then purchased this little beauty. I actually almost purchased the Winegard equivalent until I realized that the cable was built in. I have had very bad luck with cables and I wanted to make sure that if I needed a longer cable, I could always buy one. This antenna is at least as strong as my directional one but is omnidirectional which is very nice. It means that I get to hang this and watch most of the TV stations without worrying about moving the antenna to the best position. I found a place where I get between 95-100 signal strength for almost all of my channels which was as good as the directional when facing the right way. The really nice thing about this is that it is light and it has two holes which is big enough for some picture wire. It is now hanging on a wall, out of the way, and I didn't need to get a longer cable. The cable it comes with is really short though. I needed this on an outward facing wall in an old house. I was really hoping the cable would be long enough and it was, though just barely. A 25ft would have been very nice. Also the cable is very high quality and claims to conform to UL standards. It is an rc59 thin coax which is fine for the length. I wouldn't attach this to a wall directly though. I liked hanging it from the crown molding to keep it about 2in away from the wall. Placing it up against the wall actually caused a significant loss of signal. Anyway, just a great buy. I get a few of the channels listed on the website but that is because I live in a very hilly region and I get the same channels as before, with better strength, and I don't have to move it. A very good antenna and possibly the best one you can get without going roof mounted.
summary: I bought this as a replacement for a directional indoor antenna

reviewText: Before I start my review, I should inform everyone I live in a big city in a rowhome and this antenna is set up in my basement right next to my window. If this affects reception, one should take note.Unboxing this thing I noticed it really is super light and almost feels like poster board between clear contact paper. Which I guess is a good thing. But it's perplexing why the the velcro stickers that the antenna came with can't seem to support the weight of this super light antenna. It kept falling down and was a nightmare to keep mounted. I eventually had to run out to an arts and crafts supplier to buy more velcro supports for it, and since then, havent had a major problem.Anyway, about the antenna and it's reception, it's good. Not great. Not excellent. But good. My first night I took it home and it actually stayed mounted for 12 whole hours, I was able to scan lots of channels and get reception in this room I never got before. If I did this review that night I would have given it 4 or 5 stars because I was happy in that moment. But this picks up ZERO VHF channels. Which in my area means no ABC and no PBS. May not seem like a big deal to you, but considering the $8 antenna I had before could at least pick up these channels if I am in perfect conditions, it's a knock against the $40 product. However, the channels I do get are mostly clear with fairly good signals. Of course, if it's even remotely cloudy outside the reception gets a little spotty, but I guess if I'm being realistic I can't expect an indoor antenna to be 100% clear in less than perfect weather conditions. Still, I somewhat expected more considering the stellar reviews this thing got. Maybe it's my fault for getting my hopes up.I'm giving it 3 stars because no other antenna gave me this many channels on my HDTV. So that's a good thing. But those channels it picks up come in and out depending on the weather. And it does cost $40 so it's not cheap and it has less than stellar reception. So keep in mind this is not a bad review. If you are in an upstairs bedroom or apartment I can imagine this being a great antenna for you if you can mount it next to a window.. In my situation, it's not great. This room got horrible reception on my $8 antenna so this is an improvement. I'm not regretting buying it but I'm not blown away either, and I think 3 stars is more than fair in this situation.
summary: It's o.k. but not the best

reviewText: I bought this with the hope of cutting cable at my parents' house and saving myself $120/mo. My dad is retired and he likes to watch NY-1 (Time Warner's New York 24-hr news and weather channel), sports from time to time, and some other channels. I also have a supplementary foreign language package that includes 4 extra channels. 3 of them are free and available over the air in our area, so I figured he really wouldn't miss that 1 channel. Well, when I plugged this in and got all the channels set up, with a look of extreme dissatisfaction he promptly pronounced the Mohu as "useless". My 3 star rating is not a reflection of the product's quality. It is very easy to set up and the channels that were available came in crisp and clear. My problem was the assortment.Make sure you use the zipcode locator on Mohu's site before buying so you know what channels to expect. As they say, you get what you pay for and a lot of the free channels are language specific (Spanish, Korean, Hindi, Chinese) and only of interest if you happen to understand that language. In NYC, I can get 60 channels, but most of them are useless to me (HSN, audio channels, infomercials, Telemundo/Univision (Spanish), religious).So, in the end, I returned this and kept cable.

reviewText: I fell for the fancy advertisement and honestly thought this device would not look awkward. In the end, it's just another eye sore in the TV room. It looks and feels incredibly cheap, but it seems to do its job reasonably well. I purchased the Leaf to replace a $10 antenna I got from Walmart a few years ago. I thought going with one that has so many high ratings and reviews would be better. In a way it was, but it's not much of an upgrade in my opinion.The $10 unit receives more channels (we're talking ~23 channels with the Leaf and ~40 with the $10 unit).The Leaf seems to have much better video/audio quality on the channels it does receive.It seems to cut out the weak signals and really improve on the stronger signals (where the $10 unit just displays pixelated images on more channels).I'll be surprised if the thing lasts more than a couple months with how flimsy/cheap it feels.Ultimately it does what I was looking for, but not in the way I expected. It reduced the amount of noise/interference on several channels...by removing them completely. It did improve the quality on the channels it works with. It's less bulky that the $10 unit and it doesn't require external power so there's less mess and less chance for the kids to fiddle with it. So I am happy that it works, but quite disappointed overall...I guess I just expected more from all the great reviews I saw.

reviewText: I live in Seattle, Washington, and we have many local TV stations. I ran the antenna cable upstairs and put the antenna in a window in a direct line of sight with the TV transmission towers, which were about 5 miles away. I also had the amplifier on it. You'd THINK the reception would come in fabulous!!! The local stations are 3,4,5,7 and 9. Well, 3, 5 and 7 did, but not 4. Then when I messed around with it and slightly changed the position, I did get channel 4 --- but not Channel 7! I have one "must-see" show on each local channel. But about 90% of my programs are on Channel 9 (PBS), which comes from Tacoma, WA, about 45 miles away. It wouldn't come on at all! FINALLY, with much tinkering, I did get Channel 9. But I record EVERYTHING, to watch later. And as soon as I turn on the VHS/DVD recorder: PFFT! most of the channels disappear. I got some of them to work, but NOT Channel 9, the absolutely most important one. Nova, Nature, American Experience, American Masters, Masterpiece Theater...I am totally addicted to Channel 9! No Channel 9? DEAL-BREAKER! So with sadness I had to send the antenna back. The ads for it say that it'll pick up stations about 50 miles away, EVEN WAY INSIDE THE HOUSE! Well, that is simply not true. Otherwise it's a nice design. Wish it had worked.

reviewText: Like everyone in these reviews, the Leaf is phenomenal. Some specifics (what I found generally lacking in these otherwise great reviews). I live in a 9th floor apt in Falls Church, VA. I have a Vizio M470SL (47 inch flat screen). I read here that for the Leaf to work my TV had to be "digital ready." I went to every online source I could find - but couldn't find that phrase anywhere. (Lots of refs to HDMI on the Vizio, but none to "digital ready.") The Leaf arrived, I pulled it from its packaging, amazed by its wafer thin size. I screwed the coax adapter into the back of my flat screen, hung the Leaf next to the window to my balcony, eventually found autoscan on my Vizio TV, hit the button and watched the TV find about 52 stations. Amazing. Not all of them are crystal clear, but about a dozen are HD, over the air. Incredible. So clear that I can see where talk-show guests are wearing too much make-up. Hope the above is helpful.
But you can spend about half on the Amazon basics version and get the same thing. I did and got the same amount of channels and clarity.
reception; could not pull in but 5 channels. We bought another type for a few dollars more and doubled the channels received. You won't know till you try it...everyone's reception range is different.

We inconsistently get 15-25 channels with this on our first floor TV, but the major networks (NBC, CBS, FOX, WPHL) would get pixelated or blue-screen frequently enough it was not tolerable. We live about 15 miles from Philly, so the distance might be the issue. However, I made a Gray-Hoverman antenna using foam board and copper tape, and we get 25 channels, all crystal clear. So I probably wouldn't recommend this if you don't live in or close to the city. The Mohu Leaf is obviously very cosmetically pleasing and easy to hide, especially compared to a foam board, but just didn't work at all for us.

I live less than thirty miles from the needed towers but this antenna was not able to pick up any channels for me in the room/space needed.Unfortunately the device did not work for me, but great customer service from Mohu; I contacted them by email when I could not get any channels with the device and they promptly replied issuing a RMA number with return instructions. No hassles on the return/refund.Update March 01,2012: after much trial and error I was able to use Winegard antenna to get a few channels of service: with theWinegard FreeVision FV-30BB HDTV AntennaI was able to get at least one network (CBS) and one local channel. A recommended option.

Better than rabbit ears in every way. Not only are they somewhat stronger, but they look so much better. Rabbit ears are such an eyesore. I'd strongly recommend going to Mohu's website before buying because you can enter your location and it will show you on a map where it expects to reach. So for all these people complaining that it doesn't work any better than their rabbit ears, that may be true because they simply live too far from where certain stations broadcast from, but don't blame it on the Leaf.

The product is simply awful. The reception was very poor and even when I twisted myself into a pretzel to receive some channel, the reception was low quality.The thing that bugged me the most was that the antenna was very directional. It would work only in one orientation. I have a built-in entertainment corner and I couldn't find any mounting scheme that allowed reception. Forget about putting it on the inside wall of the cabinet, somehow 1/2" of particle board is sufficient to block all signal.After a frustrating afternoon, returned it promptly.Went to Costco and bought a tabletop wire-mesh antenna. It's bigger, and somewhat unsightly but damn it works. I am getting over 60 channels, many of them in spectacular full HD. It looks great on my 120Hz LED TV.
summary: Not worth the money or time

reviewText: This allows me to tune into all the local broadcast stations in Seattle without difficulty. The antenna is located inside my home but it has no trouble picking up local signals. I'm using it in conjunction with a Sony 55 inch HDTV, the picture is great

reviewText: Bought this for my mother who doesn't have cable. Improves the reception over the Terk antenna she had before and is more easily located in different parts of her viewing room than the Terk.

The first time I had tried an antenna at my apartment, I got very poor results. I purchased an antenna from Walmart made by Phillips/Magnavox I think. I could only get one major local hd channel (channel 7.1, ABC), and several SD channels. This was about 3.5 years ago when I first moved into my apartment. I discovered that Comcast was broadcasting ClearQAM channels on the cable for my internet, and have been relying on that ever since.Three days ago I woke up to all my ClearQAM channels (channels broadcast in the clear (not encrypted) on the cable I get my internet connection by) were encrypted by Comcast. All I needed was my local channels...everything else I get online in some form or another. So, I decided to try an antenna again. I tried the Leaf this time, after reading some positive reviews and seeing that it had been bundled with the Simple.TV on Kickstarter with some of the reward teirs (I purchased a Simple.TV via Kickstarter, but did not get tier which included a Leaf). I was pleasantly surprised to get nearly all of the channels I got before with ClearQAM. 39 digital channels and 1 analog channel according to my TV. The only major local HD channel I can't receive is channel 2.1, CBS...which I can certainly live without. So I am extremely happy with my Mohu Leaf. I may try a couple different positionings with the Leaf to see if I can bring in that last HD channel. I highly recommend the Leaf from the results I got. I love it!Oh and on positioning...the Leaf is positioned about a foot higher (in the same window) than the original antenna I used. It has virtually the same view out of the window as the original antenna, and I highly doubt moving that antenna to where the leaf is now would help it receive more channels. I think it was just a very poorly made HDTV antenna.
summary: Comcast Encrypted...so I switched to OTA with the Leaf...with great success!

reviewText: has great reception for such a small foot print.I didn't placing it on the wall, there were a few stations I needed to tweak the position of the Antenna. reviewText: We live in a fairly remote area with stations as far as 35-50 mi away. We currently use an amplified indoor antenna that has rabbit ears and a central UHF receiver. When the rabbit ears are positioned at a certain angle, we received a total of 5 digital channels and 2 analog channels (Yes! There are some local ones still transmitting in analog). The Mohu leaf Ultimate receives 11 digital and 2 analog channels. How's that for making a difference? (See more details below).The Mohu antenna is ultra light and surprisingly thin (like a cereal box cardboard). The antenna comes with a 16 ft coax cable and an usb powered amplifier. An AC adapter is also included in case your TV's USB port is not available. The thin ultralight nature of the antenna enables positioning anywhere with just a couple of pins (there are mounting holes in the antenna leaf) or velcro dots (pins and velcro dots are provided). This also make it easy to move the antenna around during initial set-up.The leaf is black on one side and white on the other. Flipping it does not affect performance. So I guess this is just for aesthetics. You can use whichever side that suits your wall paint color.Note: You do need to find a good spot that works for all the channels you want to receive. For example, if I place this antenna in the basement, we receive only 3-4 more channels than the existing antenna. When used upstairs (mezzanine level), our current antenna makes no difference, but Mohu gets all the additional channels.Overall, a very nice looking, light weight antenna that really works.
summary: Light-weight, ultra thin and works great!

This rating is based on what (or rather what was not delivered) was delivered compared to other antennae. The $12 RCA unit was able to deliver all local stations without the need to be moved to receive all channels. I live in the city in a one story home - not in some far out location. It is based on observation and in comparison to other antennae - at least one of which is clearly superior and has a cost of about one third that of the Leaf. I appreciate the reviews on Amazon because they are extremely helpful in making wise decisions when purchasing products.

First off, a disclaimer: everyone's reception situation is different. What works for one person may not work for another, and what fails for one person might be a stunning success for another. An antenna review can only describe the observations of a person in a given place.My setting is suburban, perhaps 15-20 miles from my stations, but also hampered somewhat by a nearby airport. I have experimented with a dozen antennas over the years. The most successful for me has been theTerk HDTVa Indoor Amplified Antenna, but I have also had good success with theRCA Basic Indoor Antennaand theRadioShack Indoor HDTV Antenna 15-246 Radio Shack.The Leaf, in my experience, fell somewhere in the middle-upper range among the antennas I tested. My reigning champ is still the Terk (which is connected to my living room HDTV), and the Leaf could not get better signals in that room, despite the different locations I put it in. (I even experimented with the Terk's amp booster with the Leaf, which did help some, although not to the degree as it did the Terk.) In most cases, I found the Leaf to be a notch better than the basic RCA and comparable to the Radio Shack antenna.It was a different story altogether in the basement. I have a TV downstairs that I prefer to have its own dedicated antenna, as there is too much loss in the signal going downstairs. I tested the Leaf down there, and its ability to be mounted on the wall was the difference-maker; it was able to access stations down there that none of my other antennas could, and is now a permanent fixture in the downstairs TV.If you're looking for a good indoor antenna, the Leaf is a bit of a risk, as it is not as cost-effective to return as a box store antenna. Still, if you're desperate for options and don't mind risking some money, it is worth a look.
summary: A solid antenna that may be useful for certain situations

reviewText: I do not have cable so I needed to replace my old rabbit ear antenna that was bent. I've had okay luck with rabbit ears but usually I have to move the antenna every which way to get reception. Also depending on the channel, the rabbit ears had to be stationed and moved to a different location just to get reception. Therefore, even though I had 41 channels available to me, I could only get about 10 channels (most of them were Korean channels) without repositioning everything. In addition, there were about 10 channels I could barely get or not get at all.This Mohu is incredible and way beyond what I expected from an antenna. I now get the same 41 channels (in northwestern NJ) and about 25 of those channels come in clear without interference or without positioning the antenna. I still do have some channels that just won't come in even though they scan as available. However, this is a tremendous improvement over my rabbit ears. Also, the picture is extremely vibrant -- way better than I've had before.In addition, I love that the antenna is like a flat piece of cardboard which I can tape up. In my case I hid it behind my furniture. I tried hanging it on the wall near the ceiling right by a window but since I didn't get any better reception, I figured I'd leave it behind my furniture.Installation was so simple. I connected the coax cable provided to the antenna and the Leaf Ultimate Amplifier. I then connected the amplifier into the antenna port on the back of my VCR/DVD. The amplifier needs power to work. Therefore, since my TV does not have a USB port, I connected the USB cable coming from the amplifier to the included wall adapter which I then plugged into an outlet behind the TV.Since the coax cable is very long, I was able to run the cable down and across the wall behind the TV, then behind a picture and up and over to the other side of my armoire. There are now no visible cables and nothing for my cats to play with.There is only one slight negative that I noticed. When changing channels, the picture takes a few seconds longer to come in but when it does, the results are clear and the picture colors supremely vibrant.I am as pleased as if I had purchased this myself. Had I purchased this, I would have considered this a great buy.May 21, 2013 Update: Below is an inventory of the channels I get in my area with this new antenna. As a result of this inventory, I actually found out that I have 36 channels that come in clear, 1 that is slighty fuzzy, and 4 that don't come in at all.These are the channels that come in clearly2-1 (English, American TV)2-2 (English, American TV)4-1 (English, American TV)4-2 (English, American TV)5-1 (English, American TV)5-2 (English, American TV -- movies coming soon) (no picture yet)7-1 (English, American TV)7-2 (English, American TV)7-3 (English, American TV)9-2 (comes in a little pixel-ly or fuzzy)13-1 (English, American TV)13-2 (English, American TV)13-3 (English, American TV)41-1 (Spanish)41-2 (Spanish)47-1 (Spanish)47-2 (Spanish)50-1 (English, American TV)50-3 (audio)63-1(English, American TV)63-2 (Korean)63-3 (Chinese)63-4 (Chinese)63-5 (Chinese)63-6 (Spanish)63-7 (Spanish)63-8 (audio Spanish)63-9 (Korean talk radio)66-1 (audio Religion)66-2 (audio Religion)66-3 (family radio)66-4 (Mind TV media independent)66-5 (Foreign Taiwan radio)66-6 (Taiwan radio)66-7 (NOAA weather audio)68-1 (Spanish)68-2 (Spanish)These are the channels that scanned as available but do not come in on my TV at all:11-1 (English, American TV)11-2 (English, American TV)11-3 (English, American TV)47-3 (Spanish)

reviewText: This didn't work very well for me. Many of the reviews didn't actually agree with my experience with this product.

We took it out, placed it at the top of the window.Ran the scanner on our $2k Sony HDTV and...It picked up 2 channels.Compared to our outdoor antenna that picks up 26 channels. I have another indoor antenna with fins on it that picks up 8 channels.Very displeased with this "miracle" antenna.

Here's an extract from the Amazon product description of this thing:"Based on discrete mudflap antenna designed for the U.S. Military"Well, in my opinion, this thing makes a much better mudflap than a TV antenna, and a pretty expensive mudflap at that. I can get better digital TV reception using an inexpensive UHF loop antenna than with this thing, despite being well within the 35-mile reception range quoted.Mine is going back to Amazon tomorrow, even though a spare mudflap might come in handy in case I ever get a military transport vehicle someday.

This antenna works, but it won't suddenly give you good reception if you've had trouble with other antennas. With this antenna I receive about half the channels that are available compared to my roof-mounted antenna. I didn't expect it to suddenly pick up all the signals at 100%, but honestly, it doesn't perform any better than the rabbit-ears we were using before.
If the US military uses this thing for anything then our military is in bad shape. Nothing, nada, no signal at all, not even a ghost.

This overpriced piece of laminated construction paper doesn't work. It is worse than the 15-year old rabbit ear antenna (with one ear broken) which it replaced. I don't understand all the rave reviews about this. Must all be from people who work for the company.I live in Portland in a normal residential area. No tall buildings or trees in the vicinity. I've tried moving the antenna everywhere. High, low, in the window, on the wall, on the TV, on the floor, in my hand - doesn't matter. Choppy, un-watchable reception on basic channels no matter what I do.I should have kept my old rabbit ears around until I made sure this works. At least I can still watch TV online.

It works for most stations but it's not a miracle cure. Placement of the antenna and your location in relation to the transmitters will be critical in how many stations you receive. Even after careful adjustments, i wasn't able to get all my stations. On the positive side, it is easy to install. I think it is a bit overpriced.
This antenna does not work any better than the cheap bunny ears bought from wal mart,or Ebay.Save your money and don't buy this.
Useless.

Disppointed in this antennae. I live 7 miles due east of Dallas. I can even see the skyline of buildings from my house. This antennae did not pick up a single VHF (channels 2-13) station. It can only pick up the UHF channels.

I think this product may work well for some people but not for me. The house where I used the Mohu antenna is about 25 miles from the mast. I got one or two stations but they were scratchy. You really need to work this out before buying an internal antenna or you will be disapointed.

With all of the fantastic reviews I thought 'hey this is just what I need!' Turned out to be nothing more than fancy trash. I only got 1 station in with this thing and I don't even live in the middle of nowhere. I got 4 channels with the cheapie ugly set of bunny ears at Walmart.

Since we're getting ready to cut the cable and going back to antenna tv with an internet tv box we had to get well.... a new antenna. I bought a few from Walmart and they didn't work at all. At best we only got 7 channels. I was a little skeptical on this antenna but I figured since it had so many good reviews it was worth giving it a try. Much to my surprise this antenna is absolutely amazing! It really is paper thin and blends in well on our white walls. It looks as if it's just a sheet of paper, lamintated, with a cord hanging out the bottom but it is certainly much more than that. We were able to pull in 17 OTA channels which the Walmart antennae couldn't even come close!The OTA HD channels look just as good as the cable channels and the Mrs. is happy we have at least CBS, NBC, and ABC channels. None the Walmart antennae were capable of pulling in ABC and only 1 pulled in CBS.If you're looking for a great indoor antenna, I don't think you can get better than this!
summary: Forget the cheap antennae this is the one!

reviewText: My dream of cutting the cable cord is gone. I ordered this product. We are in a major city and very close to a major cable hub (within 2 miles, huge satellites receivers on ground). We got about 4 channels (they did look great) we actually watched and a bunch of channels such as china news we don't need. All in all it is a not a solution for us.
Could not even pick up ABC HD so we could watch scandal even though I live right here in San Antonio, TX. Picked up FOX and CBS though. We ended up just getting DirecTV instead.

I don't know about anyone else.....but I would be happy to go back to the dark ages and TV the way we used it get receive it! We have 2 TV's on a dish and 2 small TV's we have tried, with not a lot of success, to get 'free TV". Apparently we live on the periphery of signals. I hooked up the LEAF.........and can't believe it! I get many more than a couple of stations , depending on how hard the wind is blowing. I'm very happy with it and will order another. For me, it's important to get local TV when we are having serious storms and I think this will fit the bill.

I lived in the bay area and wanted to try out this hdtv indoor antenna. I was surprised I was able to pick up about 20 local channels. I picked up 4 Vietnamese channels, 3 Chinese channels, 4 Hispanic channels, 4 PBS channels, plus some random others.Unfortunately, I was not able to pick up CBS, NBC and KTSF.This is a good start to "cut the cord" from Cable.

I've tried a bunch of times & locations to tune in our local NBC station (which is less than 20 miles from my home). Don't know if downtown is getting in the way or not, but that channel just won't come in 100% of the time. All other major networks work great plus all the other digital junk floating around out there. Giving this to my brother-in-law who lives upstairs as he doesn't mind missing out on one channel, but I'm ordering the souped-up version. This works well!

I think we watch TV too much, but I haven't gotten rid of the cable box yet. However, when we move to another state in a few weeks, I will not order cable. Having said that this antenna was easy to put together and the quality of the picture is good.As long as we can get a few channels, I'm happy. DOes what it is supposed to do.
Once I cut the cable and got a digital converter box, I needed a good antenna the rabit ears worked fine but I wanted more channels I purchased 2 of these and they work great!

After reading all the gushing reviews of the Mohu Leaf I thought I would give it a try. I have been less than impressed with the Leaf. I had hoped to mount it on a wall near my HDTV but could not get good reception. I tried several locations but none worked satisfactorily. In fact, it performed more poorly than the $10 RCA "rabbit ears" style from Walmart.I moved the Leaf to our sunroom (large open room with large windows). I thought maybe it would work better out there. Nope. I even mounted it right up against a window and it would pick up only 3-5 channels. Finally I got several channels (but not as many as I should) by hanging the Leaf about 7' in the air and about 6' from a wall. I will try some other locations and see what I can come up with. I will probably keep probably keep it to use with a small more portable TV we have.The antenna that works the best for me is theEagle Aspen Dtv2Buhf Directv 2-Bay Uhf Antenna. I ordered it from Amazon also. I have it in a closet and it still picks up more than twice the channels I could pick up with the Leaf. If you don't mind the appearance I would recommend the Eagle Aspen over the Mohu Leaf.
summary: Others work better and are much less expensive

reviewText: i had high hopes, but this did not work. if i left it in the open, it seemed ok, but if i tried to hide it as it's made for, no signal.

I first want to mention I am not an expert on these things, so my experience could just be a lack of understanding how to use this properly. But maybe that is what most of us here are, and this review might be helpful for you.So I got this thing out of the package, and my TV is in a corner. There is a window on each side of the corner, so I simply place the antenna on the window with some tape and perform the auto program on the TV. I get 8 digital channels and 0 analog channels. So I decide to take it off that window and place it on the other window. It is about 4 feet away from the other window. Next I do the auto program on the TV, and this time I get 9 channels. BUT, they are almost all different channels. For example, on the second window I get ABC, on the first channel I got NBC.So I am giving this thing 4 stars. It definitely works and the picture quality is super. But I really wish it could be less finicky about which direction it was facing if possible. Makes you wonder if I got two of these things, placed one on the first window and another one on the second window then had them each connect into one line and fed that line into the tv what would happen.

I have my Mohu mounted on my bedroom wall. The sticky strips they provided didnt hold, but my own double stick tape works great. I got this on sale for 25 bucks. I get about 25 channels in HD, though sometimes i get some interference, but rarely. I really only watch the local channels because the rest of them dont really show anything that anyone under 90 watches. Though a few spanish channels do come in as well. I watch most of my fav shows online, and my smart tv gets hulu and netflix, so I cut the cable chord. I do like having the local channels to watch the news and late night without paying the cable company, so it's a win.I would recommend the Mohu, but make sure you check your area for a good tv signal. My home is in the green zone, so I was good.UPDATE: 6-12-14I have a standard Mohu leaf in my bedroom & it works perfectly. But the same mohu leaf, will not work in my living room. (Barely get 3 channels). I bought the "mohu 50" amplified for 68 bucks to use on my living room tv, and that one struggled too. Returned it and looking at other options now. What I'm saying is, 1 room and a different wall can be the difference between free tv and no tv. However, being only 30 feet away, and using the amplified version that's 2 times the price (tried in over 20 different spots) should have worked. Lowered to 3 stars. Amazon took it back for a full refund! Thank you.

Reading from the description, it seems to be an awesome product. However, some of the times the amplifier antenna would looses the signal. And for the price, I believe that it is not worth it. My recommendation is to get something that is alike but cheap to try it out first.

I'm not sure how this "antenna" got all those five-star reviews. I live in downtown Boston only 1/2 mile from the transmitters for most of the TV stations yet no matter where I placed this antenna I got ZERO stations when auto-tuning. Everything was set properly (tuner set to "antenna" not "cable") and the cable was snug.Returned to Amazon today.
summary: DOESN'T WORK: Receives ZERO Channels in Downtown Boston

reviewText: I've been trying to find a discreet antenna to get reception about 40 miles from the antenna location. This doesn't do the trick.

I am moderately pleased with this antenna. Having dropped satellite a while back I wanted an antenna that would still let me watch all my local channels. When I first hooked it up there were a couple channels that weren't coming in very well but they were ones that I didn't watch that frequently anyway so it didn't bother me. After having it a while one of the channels that carries a lot of my shows stopped getting good reception. It's supposed to be multi-directional so moving it around doesn't do a lot of good. Maybe weather conditions affect it but I didn't think anything affected digital signals. I think a decent pair of rabbit ears would work just as well.

Apparently this item is very dependent upon where you live. I currently have a Terk HDTV amplified Antenna Pro. And when the unit is positioned correctly, it brings in fantastic picture and sound. However, recently I purchased a TabloTV OTA DVR and I found that having a directional antenna was not convenient when you wanted to record multiple programs from different stations. So I figured I would get an omni-directional unit.This one had been reviewed very positive, so I decided to try it out. I was very disappointed. I hung the unit up and had the Tablo scan for channels. The Terk pulled in about 20 channels and most were extremely strong signals. The Lead pulled in maybe 10, and only one or two were strong signals. When I went to watch live TV, I could not get a consistent signal for more than 10 seconds. I tried positioning the unit in different places with no luck. I am returning it.I am sure this works great, but it very much depends on where you live. My other antenna works great, so I will just have to plan ahead when I want to record something, or go all-in and get a rooftop unit.

I bought this for my spare bedroom and it barely worked there, despite it being upstairs and free of obstruction. When my parents moved into a nearby apartment building and found out that the cable would not be available for 30 days, I brought it over. It worked amazingly well there, less than a mile from my home. They were able to pull all types of extra stations in addition to the networks. Strange thing was, one of the networks ( I forget which one) did not come in at all. But that was easily overlooked as the quality on the rest of the stations was awesome. I had seen mixed reviews and I think it is strictly due to location. I bought it at a reasonable price and was willing to risk it. Good luck!
summary: When it works, it is awesome!

reviewText: I went on a search for indoor antennas because I recently moved to Colorado and tried to get satellite for my apartment. Unfortunately, with the way my apartment was facing, there would have been no way I was able to get signal according to the technician so I had to cancel.After browsing around and doing my research, I found this antenna. I am surprised at the clarity and the amount of channels I receive off of this. A lot of the mainstream channels like ABC, FOX, NBC, etc. are really clear and in HD. It also receives a lot of random channels that I didn't expect. Overall, after scanning, I received about 50 different channels. It pretty much is paper thin as advertised. It seems like a piece of paper that has been laminated. One side is black while the other is white. You can easily hang it on the wall with a thumb tack.Overall, I am very satisfied with this antenna. It is just funny that this receives such great signal while satellite fails to get any signal. It also saved me a monthly payment for TV. I highly recommend for people who want to save money and also only needs the basic channels.

It works better than you'd expect for something with such a small footprint. 40 years of experience with rabbit ears and all kinds of fancy antennae that don't work had me set with pretty low expectations, so I was really pleasantly surprised that we started getting all manner of channels that we didn't even know existed once we switched to this one.

It's easy to install - you just stick it to a wall. It blends in very well with the room decor. I get CBS and ABC very well, and no NBC or FOX. But the signal is pretty good, and for the money it's a good value.

I'm naturally a skeptical person, but given the glowing reviews, I decided to try this relatively inexpensive inside antenna in lieu of buying a more expensive outside antenna. I'm using this in a somewhat remote part of the state, and had my doubts. I'm about 700 feet above sea level. No mountains or significant hills, but quite a few trees. Anyway, this worked fantastically well. My location has DirecTV, but it is notorious for going out during bad (and not so bad) storms, when I when you really need to stay informed. This antenna is a backup and allows me to get local stations during such times. I thought I'd get maybe 8 or 10 of the regional channels, but I got 22 channels, some from 200 miles away. You will not regret this purchase.
summary: WOW! The stellar reviews are true!

reviewText: I was hoping to get rid of cable. I checked the government website and saw a good HDTV signal in my area but not a great one. The device is easy to install but does not pick up anything but noise. I don't know if that means this device doesn't work well, or there is a lack of signal in my area. I don't know anyone else in the area that has tried to use over the air so it is impossible to tell. What I can say is that this antenna did not work at all...not even a little bit.
summary: Does not work well in my area

reviewText: I bought this for my parents RV in Socal. Basically if you don't have line of sight to a tower it won't work (direct quote from support at Mohu) It probably works well in a city but for RV use in mountainous areas you'll need to find something else.
summary: Don't buy it in Southern California

reviewText: I installed this in second floor bedroom and it outperformed an RCA amplified antenna. A good deal for the money.

Great antenna! I wasn't sure what to expect since this antenna is cheaper than some others but we've gotten great results. We were able to find many local channels with amazing HD quality with this thing. The cable is long enough for adjustments to get the best position. Fantastic antenna for the price.

We live in Alaska and I cannot even get 4 stations with this and this is with still having to get up and move it depending on what station you want to see. I am sure this works well in other parts of the country ie..the lower 48 but just not good for the direction of the horizon up here.

I know that some of the reviews were in question, but I gambled anyway and so far 5 months... have liked it. We cut cable 8 months ago and wanted a better way to view the news and such. This product works very well for us. We live no further than 30 miles from most TV stations in columbus Ohio area. Every once and awhile it will have some delays but most of the time there are no issues. Cable that came with it was nice and long.
summary: Mohu Leaf Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna

reviewText: I got the leaf antenna for my daughter who was having difficulty pulling in channels on her new TV.With the Leaf, reception occasionally falters, but it pulls in several more channels than she received previously and the quality of reception is more consistent.My daughter is pleased!!! So is dad!

Well, with digital signals, it works or it doesn't. You get some of that "scrambling" with a weak signal, but for the most part it works or it doesn't.The antenna is pretty good. I hung it behind a picture - the coax cable makes it protrude from the wall, not the flat antenna. It catches just about everything, but weather does affect it.My wife says it would be nice to just have a signal that works all the time, which is a good point. But when you have a good HD signal (for FREE), with 5.1 sound, it's pretty great.

The manufacturer claims that this is the most powerful high def antennae on the market. It isn't. But the ones that are involve ornate combinations of rabbit ears and complex extensions. What this Mohu antenna is is the simplest antenna on the market. Instead of contorting your antenna in more and more complex configurations in an attempt to pick up just one more station, these rest in a single place. If they aren't the most complex antenna, they are definitely the least obtrusive.There are always going to be some who will learn for a minutely improved performance to appearance, but I like how they manage to stay out of the way. A couple of small tacks and they are part of your wall. I also like that each side provides a sharply contrasting appearance, either matte black or matte white.For most users of antenna these are going to represent the best the alternative. Definitely one of more interesting options on the market.
summary: Not the most powerful HD antennae on the market, but perhaps the most fashionable

reviewText: I purchased the amplified Leaf and the standard Leaf as I have two TV's currently using a provider that is choking me for $110 a month. I chose the amplified because I have one TV in a basement. I happen to live in Albuquerque and there are many antennas on the Sandia mountains but the signal from channel 4 is always an issue (so everyone tells me). The amplified Leaf was worse than the standard Leaf in signal strength and picture quality everywhere I used it (upstairs and down). It appears to be influenced by any electrical signals like the TV itself. It comes with some special C123 cable that s thinner but I could not get several channels. The standard Leaf with the RG6U cable worked extremely well. I was not able to get the channel 4 in the basement but I got all of the others. Based on what I am seeing I would buy the standard Leaf and save some money. I also found that one has to try moving the Leaf around several times and monitor the signal strength for all of the channels and find the best average for the channels you watch most. Oh, I changed the amplified to a standard and used it without the amplifier. I also switched back to RG6U cable and it worked much better.
summary: Amplified what - not the signal coming in.

reviewText: We use a 23" HD TV that doubles as a computer monitor in the study. I tried this antenna because my wife was annoyed by the ugly rabbit ears sitting on top of the computer hutch.With the Mohu hidden behind a picture that is above my filing cabinet, I now get 23 channels. That is six more channels than I got with amplified rabbit ears. Only one of the 23 channels is not as good as the attic antenna with an amplifier that serves the big TV in the family room. The Mohu is about 10 feet lower than the attic antenna and is surrounded by walls and electronic equipment.I have not tried an amplifier with the Mohu yet.Not everyone will get 23 channels over the air. My area is an ideal environment for broadcast TV, but this antenna is the best I have found, and it is NOT made in China!Packaging was perfect. A pizza-style box with two sheets of bubble wrap protecting the antenna. Easy to open and 100% recyclable and/or reusable.
My husband bought this because we live so close to the Canadian Border (he wanted to pick up hockey being broadcast over there). It works well!

I went from getting 3 very obscure channels to getting about 9, only 5 of which are basic broadcast channels (2,4,9.1, 9.2, 9.3). I still don't get 5,7 or 11 which really should be coming in... In any case, perhaps it's the way my home is set up and the fact that there are no windows facing the direction of the broadcast. I've moved it around and it picks up more channels but then loses the other ones so I have not been able to find a place where it picks up all the channels available to me. I thought this was a multidirectional so I'm not clear as to why that happens.
very thin, like a letter sized paper.Connected to my tv, scanned and got a 70 signal strength. not bad. Picture quality is very good.Long Island City, Queens, 4th floor.
When reading reviews it showed I would be able to at least pick up 8 channels in my area. When it was set up, it showed I picked up 8 channels but only have 1 channel that I can actually see.

Got my Mohu this morning (got my mohu working? lol) Anyway hooked it up right away and sorry to say I was disappointed, most places I tried it I only got 14 channels, Putting it in a few "inconvenient/eyesore" type places I was able to get 23 channels.I have been using an older version of the Clearstream 2 antenna (see separate review on Amazon) and the Clearstream 2 is the clear winner hands down, it pulls in at the minimum 46 channels, it's only weakness is VHF which I learned has since been addressed with a new model (Clearstream 2V) or as an accessory purchase.The only advantage for the Mohu was those VHF channels and it is much smaller and lighter, it looks cool but the Clearstream 2 is built for indoor or outdoor which could account for added size and bulk.. Plus as I mentioned the Clearstream has been updated, I have an older UHF only model (and it still gets two VHF channels).The Mohu was slightly better than a cheap $14 RCA model I started with a few years ago when I gave up on satallite and cable/Uverse.Some notes on these new digital antennas if you have not tried one, weather and placement of antennas make a huge difference as can the time of day. Weaker channel reception is mercurial and fleeting..each time you do a channel scan you can add some channels but lose some as well. On the plus side the digital antennas give you a pure HD picture and sound, not the compressed signal you are getting from cable or Uverse (it has been years since I had Directv so not fair to compare). I bet if I place the Clearstream outdoors it would perform even better. If you are in a city close to transmitters and or have a small apartment the Mohu may suit your needs adequately but to really pull in channels from everywhere it is the Clearstream that gets the job done.In closing, for me the Clearstream is the clear winner. I am in the Northern suburbs of Atlanta, so lots to pick from channel wise in a 50 mile radius but lots of trees/hills etc to affect signal as well. Think the Mohu says it has a 35 mile range, the Clearstream says 50 miles plus

I bought this antenna in the hopes that I was going to rid myself of my frightfully expensive monthly cable bill. Much to my disappointment, no matter where I placed the antenna I could not get a signal. I either got a defect antenna or the hills surrounding my house are blocking all the local signals.
This item does not work at all. I bought a regular antenna and that one works better than this. I should have read all the reviews including the 1 stars, so buyers beware.

I found that like with the old-fashioned rabbit ears, I still need to move this antenna to get the best service for certain tv stations. So attaching "permanently" to the wall isn't an option. I wish that the antenna came with a stand that would allow me to set it down and tilt or rotate it to get the best reception.
summary: Wish it came with a stand

reviewText: Works much better than the old rabbit ears but I still cannot get all local channels (I was never able to get them with any antenna). Those that come in are clearer than the old systems, and there is no adjustment knob that has to be messed with. This was really easy to install, no tools or technical ability required. Plug it in, a few buttons on your TV remote control and it works. Much easier than messing with rooftop antenna too.The flat profile is nice, and it is relatively unobtrusive on the wall behind the TV. You will need something to keep it stuck to the wall, especially if you have to move it after you use up the Velcro it comes with.Don't forget, some old TV's will still need a tuner that is separate. This still worked with an old TV that needed a tuner, so no real issues there, but it may not work "out of the box" for every TV.

I have the original Leaf. The 2 big differences are: 1) longer coax cable from the antenna. 2) The USB power-able amp.I left the Ultimate in the product case and dug out the amp and attached it to my set.No, I don't get more channels (YMMV). Yes, it helped with some really weak signal for me (PBS). Went from 0-1 bar to 2-3 bar.FYI I went to 'used' under Amazon Warehouse and saved a bundle. RF is a tricky deal. This may or may not work for you.The product itself is excellent. And it cannot change the laws of physics.Yes, even small changes can make a big difference. I found a position that gets everything I can get, without moving things around. Very Very happy.
No signal. May be my area or may be the product, but I had no luck with this product at all. Others in my area say their antenna pick up stations just fine.

Update, beware of all the FAKE reviews that say it is the best thing since cable for TV._____________________________________________________________________I so wanted this to work. I cut the cable "umbilical cord" three years ago, and am happy. I would like to get my locals for certain sporting events that they broadcast.I read all the reviews, both good and bad, and made what I thought was an informed decision to purchase this antenna. After wasting over three hours locating the "leaf" here and there, I have found that it is no better than the antenna I had purchased three years ago at a much lesser price. I also went to their website, entered my zip, and it gave me a list of "lots" of channels that this antenna would pick up in my area. I had to chuckle.One plus, and this is the only one, is the mobility of the "leaf". The extra long cable is also a plus, so I guess that is two pluses. ;)I have my wall marked for each channel I wish to watch, and I will have to move it each time I want to watch that channel. This alone would not be too much of a problem, but here's the catch: you have to waste an additional 20 minutes waiting for your TV to rescan for channels each time you move the leaf. Actually, if you touch it, it will lose it's signal and you will have to rescan!If you are looking for an indoor antenna that will pick up all of your locals, look further, as this is no different than the others, and often there are CHEAPER antennas out there.I found a good youtube video that shows how to build an outside HDTV antenna. I think I will go that route as it will only cost me my time, which I have already wasted and the cost for all components will be under $20, including the coaxial cable needed.

Review from Southern California. Solved my problem of having to often reposition my rabbit-ears when I changed a channel. I also pick up channels that were not previously available or "stable." Proably has a lot to do with being able to readily elevate the antenaa.

I live in Los Angeles and there are a lot of great OTA channels here (and in HD)! This is the first antenna that I've owned that's so aesthetically pleasing. However, it doesn't do a great job of picking up all the signals properly. I'm looking into better performing antennas now.
summary: Great form factor, but doesn't pick all channels well.

reviewText: Did I get a dud? I had a broken set of rabbit ears hooked to my brand new 55" LED TV and could pick up some channels perfectly. I got this because on windy/stormy days I had issues and I wanted to get more channels. I hooked it up per the instructions along with the power USB cable and I got exactly zero channels. Yes, I went through the channel scan on my TV. I consider myself tech savvy and fiddled with this thing for way too long. Maybe I have a unique situation or my unit was defective. Either way, I gotta calls it like I sees it.

In order to get 1-min. straight of reception, I had to hold the antenna in the middle of my living room by a window. I'm only 20 mi. away from downtown Atlanta and both units I tried would not pickup anything reliably. It was like satellite TV not getting reception. What a joke... why can't they make these things have some power?!

reviewText: I received this antenna just a few days ago having ordered it directly from the MOHU Web Site on the Internet (free shipping same price).Already an owner of the TERK antenna mentioned in the title above (see my review) and purchased from Amazon.com in early July 2011, I was very curious about how these two antennas would compare head-to-head when combined with my brand new 47" Toshiba Passive 3D TV.In short, both antennas can tune in about the same number of channels when properly positioned (30 - 40 range with some unusable, many Spanish language and some duplicate - 20 or so usable channels are left in the end). Both antennas can access all the local affiliates of the major networks plus FOX, with one exception: The MOHU - for some unknown reason - cannot access the local NBC affiliate; the TERK can. This is VHF channel 3 here where I live. However, other VHF channels - namely 5, 8, 10 & 13 - are tuned in by the MOHU without any problems whatsoever.Why no channel 3 via MOHU? I really did try tweaking its location to the nth degree. It shouldn't be the distance to the transmission tower since out of the 5 VHF stations mentioned above channel 3 is closest to my home (13 miles away - the remaining stations are all 18-23 miles distant).If this were due to an unknown peculiarity related to my specific location, then the TERK antenna shouldn't be able to receive this station either, but it does.Nevertheless, for all of the channels tuned in by both antennas (VHF & UHF), the signal strength/quality is notably better overall with the MOHU Leaf (not just subjectively, but also objectively as confirmed by the TV's signal reception display/meter), despite the fact that the TERK has a built-in signal amplifier and the MOHU's supposedly being optimized for UHF reception.If I had to choose one of the two antennas, it would be the MOHU Leaf, because of its better overall performance with regard to signal strength and resulting picture quality. The Leaf is also smaller/thinner and thus much more convenient and flexible in its placement options. I give it 4 out of 5 stars, because of the one important station (local NBC affiliate) that it fails to find.Overall, this is a quality product with impressive technology in a very small footprint - definitely a worthwhile purchase for cutting the cable/dish cord. The MOHU Leaf is definitely not just blowing the wind!

This is a review of theSeagate ST2000DM001 Barracuda 7200RPM 2 TB SATA 6 GB/s NCQ 64 MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive(ST500DM001)This is part of the "Barracuda" series, and not a Green drive. According to the manufacturer specs, this 7200 rpm drive has a 64MB cache, advanced format 4K sectors, 6GB/s interface. I cannot find any information regarding the warranty, but my experience with Seagate warranty has been pretty good.From what I've seen with this drive, I would not hesitate to use it as a performance or data drive. It is fast enough to run the OS, and large enough to store tons of data files. In fact, I will be replacing my WD Raptor (10K rpm) drive with this one because this Barracuda outperformed the Raptor in ALL of my benchmark and real-world testings. (For detailed specs, see below).Overall, highly recommended.(Warning: Geek alert!!!)Seagate has implemented the 1TB-per-Disk technology on its Barracuda drives, but some sites have reported that this 2TB model has three disks instead of two. This drive boasts low power consumption, and complies with the RoHS directive on hazardous materials and volunatarily restrict halogen compounds. So it is as green as possible with minimal sacrifice on performance. These are very good drives that balance performance, reliability, and capacity. I've tested this drive as a boot drive and for data storage, and so far it has exceeded my expectations and performed with high marks.I asked for an OEM drive, and not a retail package (boxed with cables, screws, etc.). I tested one of these drives on a desktop PC. I really did not know what to expect because it is a relatively new drive. First thing I did was format it to NTFS using PartedMagic (multiple partitions).Using CDM 3.0.1 and HD Tach as benchmarking tools, I got the following specs:Average Read - 249 MB/sSequential Read - 258 MB/sAveage Write - 126 MB/sSequential Write - 136 MB/sClearly, these benchmark numbers are impressive. The benchmark numbers for this drive are a bit more impressive than the WD Black 2TB model, and it may have to do with the fast 6GBps interface (SATA3), the larger cache (64MB), or the advanced format 4K sector.Using real files, I calculated the transfer to and from an SSD drive. I transferred an 8.5 GB folder containing 1GB files. Using Windows, I clocked an average 52 MBps read and 24 MBps write. In a Mac (OS X), the same files transferred were 61 MBps read and 37 MBps write. The folder took under three minutes to transfer over!!! Very impressive numbers.I did not find this drive to be particularly noisy. My Hitachi 1TB 7200 and my WD Raptor are louder (though this is obvious). On my PC, the boot drive (Raptor) is noisier because it is a 10K rpm drive. However, this Seagate drive is noisier than my 5400 and 5900 rpm drives (not surprising). I've never tried this drive on a RAID configuration (having only one). I may try it in my NAS box if I feel adventurous, but I don't really want to fuss around with non-matching drives for RAID arrays (just a personal preference).After seeing the performance of this drive in benchmark and real-world files, I would use this drive for a boot drive and for backups. Only time will tell how reliable they are.Highly recommended!!!Disclaimer: I received this product through the Vine program in exchange for an objective review. I do not receive monetary compensation from Amazon or its affiliates. I spent my own free and valuable time testing and trying out this product and providing this objective review.

reviewText: Very convenient for Seagate considering the 12 month warranty. My last two drive failures have been Seagates.. I'll stick with Western Digital from now on. Thanks for nothing, Seagate!

Seagate is widely regarded for making sub-par hard drives overall which it dismisses when you call them because they have a "1% failure rate", but when you look at the reviews of those that actually bothered to update them after initially booting up the disk then you see a very different story. Most comment on a 30-50% failure rate, one I can attest to with me having used about 15 of these 3tb drives in the past 1.5 years and 8 of them have failed.If you're going to order these things order them in groups of 3 because most likely 1 will be dead on arrival or going to die. Out of my last 3 HDDs I ordered 2 weeks ago (because I had yet ANOTHER failure), one arrived that failed the smart tests immediately with all sorts of bad sectors popping up during a surface scan and deemed "going to die soon". Another had numerous slow response sectors (over 50,000) which is most likely an indication of a drive that'll last less than a year under more than normal duress but was still usable so I kept it. I'm afraid to even get a replacement drive directly from Seagate because the one that failed was a replacement drive that I just got a few months ago which replaced another replacement drive from Seagate which was DOA.NONE of my drives have lasted longer than ONE YEAR so far. These things are advertised to be high performance, I have them in a would be high performance computer that is rarely used as more than a Youtube watching machine. The horrible Seagate rep suggested I buy enterprise level drives which cost at least 3X more! Then, they totally dismiss my claims because they have a "1% failure rate." Some engineers have even posted in-depth reviews of their supposed enterprise "raid drives" which claim that those special "raid drives" are actually horrible for raid setups because that low, constant spindle speed causes some drives not to boot up when needed which causes data loss among other things such as setting off raid alarms because the drives drop out of the arrays when they don't spin up.I used to work as a lead engineer at Aon Hewitt, a very large billion dollar corporation with over 65k employees worldwide. We ordered over 25,000 laptops, a good majority of which had Seagate drives in them. 40% of those drives failed within the first few months of us deploying those laptops which we brought up with Lenovo (who was supposed to reach out to Seagate). It was chalked up to a "bad batch of hard drives". When a company generating $16 billion a year on the same level of Seagate has 40% of it's hard drives failing then I would say that definitely says something about the quality of the drives. Those drives reflected bad upon my entire department with all the downtime and lost data and we devoted a lot of time trying to get to the bottom of the bluescreens and failures only to find out it was just "bad drives."The 3TB drives also take up a lot of resources when writing to for some odd reason. 32gb of RAM, an 8-core processor, the latest graphics card, and an OS loaded onto an SSD doesn't stop my system from hiccuping when writing mere 500mb files to these drives.Yet, Seagate continues to claim they have a "1% failure rate" and dismiss every negative review. The manager of the reps said that "If you release the perfect product, there's always going to be someone that complains." He left no room for improvement upon his own product and suggested Seagate drives were perfect!People, update your reviews to reflect your true experience with these drives after months of usage. Let Seagate know the exact quality of these drives so they can't continue to live in their fantasy realm where they don't suck. No wonder Seagate and other HDD manufacturers got destroyed when SSDs were released, I'm surprised they're even still in business. WD has a lower failure rate and their black series 3tb has faster read/write speeds so they're the better deal. When I get the chance I'm selling all these drives and buying all WD drives (unless 4TB SSDs drop down to a reasonable price.)

reviewText: Summary: This Seagate Desktop HDD 4 TB SATA 6Gb/s NCQ 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive ST4000DM000 performs pretty much as expected from the specifications. But, because of 1) how Amazon shipped it to me, 2) some problems I had with it in my drive enclosures, and 3) its inability to come anywhere close to SATA 6 Gb/s speeds, I'm rating it merely at an OK 3 stars out of 5.Supporting Details:First of all, my environment: I'm running Windows 8 (64-bit) on anASUS P8Z77-V PRO LGA 1155 Intel Z77 HDMI SATA 6Gb/s USB 3.0 ATX Intel Motherboardusing anIntel 520 Series Solid-State Drive 240 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch - SSDSC2CW240A3K5 (Reseller Kit)as my primary disk.Next, the shipping: Amazon sent this bare drive to me packed in LOOSE bubble-wrap (a layer on the bottom of the box, the bare drive, and another layer on top of the drive. Normally, I've received bare drives wrapped TIGHTLY in bubble wrap (all sides) and taped shut. I could hear the drive rattling in the box before opening it.Now, the tests: I'd liked to have tested this drive using myStarTech.com SuperSpeed USB 3.0 to Dual 2.5/3.5in SATA Hard Drive Docking Station. But, unfortunately, Windows 8 only recognizes this docking station as USB 2.0 (not 3.0) on every USB port on my system. So, I really couldn't test with that (though I did power up the drive that way and initialize with a GUID Partition Table in Windows' Disk Management).Then, I tried my old Icy Dock MB559US-1S External 3.5" eSATA/USB 2.0 Hard Drive Enclosure connected to the eSATA port. But, the drive wouldn't even spin up when connected that way. Ditto for myThermaltake St0005u Blacx Esata&Usb-Sata; Hdd Docking Station Windows&Mac; Os Compatible: the drive failed to spin up. Since the drive did spin up in the StarTech dock (though slowly), I have no idea if this is an incompatibility between those older docks and the new SATA 6 Gb/s drive or if the drive has problems.I finally took my computer apart enough for me to connect the drive to an Intel Z77 SATA 6 Gb/s port on my motherboard and ran these tests that way (obviously, the drive did spin up with that). Because of space constraints, I had to leave the computer open with the drive outside the case. In this configuration, I could hear the drive spinning, seeking, and accessing. It all sounded fairly quiet and smooth. So, I assume that inside a closed case, it would probably sound pretty good. Regarding temperatures, the disk stayed pretty cool throughout the testing (about 34 degrees Centigrade). Remember, though, this is outside the computer case (no airflow over the drive, but no airflow restrictions or waste heat from other components).I double-checked in Disk Management that the drive was still a GPT one and noted the usable space of 3725.90 GB. I then ran HD Tune on it. Oddly, HD Tune saw the drive as only being 2199 GB. I assume that's an issue with the very large size (i.e., greater than 2 GB) of the drive. I don't know how valid the test results are because of that, but I've included a screenshot of the benchmark results up on the product page. Here's a text version:HD Tune: ST4000DM000-1F21 BenchmarkTransfer Rate Minimum : 131.7 MB/secTransfer Rate Maximum : 189.3 MB/secTransfer Rate Average : 160.5 MB/secAccess Time : 14.1 msBurst Rate : 263.7 MB/secCPU Usage : 3.4%I'd like to point out that the average transfer rate that HD Tune finds works out to just 1.2 Gb/sec. This doesn't come anywhere near the theoretical transfer rate of the SATA 6 Gb/s connection. As expected, the physics of accessing a spinning set of platters far outweighs the theoretical transfer rate.I then started up Western Digital's DLGDIAG on the drive. Nothing bad showed up in the drive's SMART data. I then ran Quick Test and it passed. So, again, I have no idea what to think of the drive not powering up in those two docks.Moving away from formal benchmarks, I tried copying data to/from the drive. I started with a single 2.8 GB .ISO file. According to Windows, that file transferred from my SSD to the Seagate at about 145 MB/s. Copying it back, it transferred at about 210 MB/s. I've run across this discrepancy in transfer speed before and assume it's an artifact either of Windows 8 or the drive caching the transfers or of the SSD compressing/decompressing files in the background. But, the 145 MB/s seems to agree with what HD Tune came up with. Working with many smaller files, I copied my pictures (4,420 files in 452 folders totaling 3.42 GB) to the drive at about 108 MB/s and back again at about 130 MB/s.

I picked up the Seagate Barracuda 2TB internal hard drive a few weeks ago on Amazon. I think I've "broken it in" enough now to write a fair and honest review on this hard drive. Before picking this up, I was looking at three Western Digital models (the black/cavier, green, and blue editions), as well as various Samsung models and a Toshiba model of the same disc space size. After looking at various benchmarks, articles, and stats, I decided to pick up the Seagate Barracuda. on benchmarks, the speed of the Barracuda was just better. Not as eco-friendly as the Western Digital green but often "eco" comes at the cost of performance so I decided to go with this over the WD. Among this, I own an external Seagate Free Agent 500GB hard drive and it has been very reliable over the years, so I trusted them to deliver the same quality with an internal hard drive. As with last time, Seagate once again delivered a quality product! Anyway, here's a breakdown.PROS- Very fast, first load in on many games, transfer speeds are excellent- Lots of space at 2TB, no more deleting files!- Runs cool at 30C staying at the ambient temperature of my case- Smokes my old Sony and Western Digital hard drives that I replaced with this- Delivered in air sealed, anti-static bag in mint condition (as expected for a new product)CONS- Missing about 200GB of space (SEE BELOW)- Didn't include a manual, CDs, or SATA cable, just the plain old hard drive (not that I need all this crap but some people might)- Hard drive transfer utility from Seagate's websites did not work (SEE BELOW)CON - APPROX. 200GB MISSING SPACEI already knew about this going in but it still bothers me to an extent. For those that do not understand computer terminology, 1 (one) Terabyte is equal to exactly 1024 (one-thousand-twenty-four) Gigabytes of memory. But pretty much all hard drive manufacturers do not go by odd numbers when producing hard drives. They go by a "decimal gigabyte", meaning to them 1,000 Gigabytes is 1 Terabyte. Operating systems like Windows, however, still calculate the space on the drive by the "binary gigabyte" of 1024 Gigabytes. This means when you install your 2TB hard drive you are only getting about 1.81GB of hard drive space instead of 2TB because the hard drive doesn't actually have 2TB to the binary Gigabyte of space. To do this calculation yourself you can calculated what 93% of your hard drive space is, ex:2,000GB * .93 = 1,860GB (1.8TB)Now I already knew about this but I thought I would share this with newcomers to this hard drive. Personally I think it's getting kind of ridiculous. The bigger the hard drive you get, the more space you lose because of this discrepancy between the manufacturer and the way the Operate System properly calculates hard drive space. 200GB is alot of space to give up over this which is why I am knocking off a star for this product. Blame who you want. Some will blame Microsoft/Windows, others will blame with Hard Drive manufacturer. Hypothetically if Microsoft would go by decimal Gigabyte, we wouldn't lose that space. But shouldn't the manufacturer go by the mathematically correct measurement of hard drive space? I think further down the road there is going to have to be addressed by both the OS and hard drive manufacturers. Think about it, if you bought a 10TB hard drive years from now you would lose about 700GB of space! I used to not mind this difference in space but it's getting quiet ridiculous these days.CON - HARD DRIVE TRANSFER UTILITY DOESN'T WORKSeagate's official website offers a download for a utility to transfer files from an old drive to a new one. This utility did not work for me, however i have my own unique way of transferring files. I just copy everything over and then rename the disk to the same drive letter as the previous and reboot. If Windows is not running from that hard drive you can easily get away with this. Some programs, however, that have security and/or registry entries may not transfer correctly. Just be aware that their software is not the best and if you are doing a transfer with a hard drive that has Windows on it there are a few more steps involved in doing this properly.SOME PRO TIPS- When you first get this drive, before doing anything with it you should absolutely UPDATE THE FIRMWARE. Seagate's website has an official link to download firmware. Burn it to a bootable CD, run it, and you should be good to go! This was relatively painless and it's a good idea to do with internal hardware like this so you don't have issues down the road and you get the most out of your hard drive.- After updating the firmware, format and partition the drive and you should be good to go!- To get the full 6GB/s transfer speeds you should have a compatible motherboard and SATA cable that supports the high transfer speeds. Most new SATA cables natively support this speed. You are NOT required, however, to have SATA III 6GB/speeds to use this drive. Heck it would probably work in a Windows 95 computer as SATA is usually backwards compatible!- Make sure you do not touch the circuit board with your fingers on the bottom and avoid using magnetized screwdrivers whenever working with it in the computer. Also make sure the drive is properly mounted secure and level inside the computer.Final thoughts, great hard drive, good price. It's not as fun as buying an awesome new graphics card but it was a necessity. As for me, I'm a professional website developer/programmer self-employed. I work from home and go to college online as well so my computer is important to me. I wouldn't have bought this hard drive if I didn't think it was "good". I read some of the other reviews on here (Seagate haters) and some complaints about what manufacturer the drive comes from (eg. China, Taiwain, etc.). Honestly that's just overlooking it. Pretty much all computer products come from over seas these days. There is little to no difference between them and no matter which one it comes from, that doesn't mean theres going to be a flop in one of them. If you get a defunct hard drive return it to Amazon. They are usually pretty good with returns/exchanges. I would recommend this to anyone whether you're a die hard PC junkie or a casual user. Segate is a great, reputable hard drive company and I'm proud to own two of their hard drive products.
