reviewText: For those of you who are not aware of it, this drive has some kind of firmware problem that makes the drive chirp from time to time. Whatever the problem it, Seagate fixed it with a firmware update recently. In order to update the firmware, you need to set your hard drive mode in BIOS to IDE (not AHCI), then download the bootable iso version (I don't trust microsoft to get in between me and my firmware updates). Boot from the cd the iso created, select "d" for download new firmware. Wait 20 seconds or so. When it says it's done, turn off your computer. At bootup, enter BIOS and switch back to AHCI. You are done. I haven't had any chirping or any other problems with this drive.It's 3 platters only, with 1TB each. This means is consumes less power than its brethren with more platters, and the performance is good. I have it hooked to a 6.0 GbPS SATA port. Runs great, quiet, etc.In the past I've always bought Western Digital drives but in the wake of the flood, WD appears to be keeping its prices way high for a long time. even on their wimpy green drives. I mean, it was like 10 months ago or something, people! Good reason to switch to Seagate. Seagate, on the other hand, has lowered prices to something in the same ballpark as pre-flood levels--though they haven't progressed past where they were at the time.Anyway, I have a 1 TB version of this drive in my main computer (the firmware update said it didn't need updating) and a 3 TB version (which I updated myself) in my home fileserver.What I want to know is when is Seagate going to use these great 1TB platters in a 4 and 5 platter configuration. I already have a 4TB seagate drives (barricuda XT) that I pulled out of an external enclosure (for some reason they never sold the 4 TB version as a bare drive). It has 5 platters. Why not make 4 or 5 platter Barricudas using the 1Tb platters? It has to be trivial. I could use the space on my fileserver.By the way at the time I bought this you could get the same drive in an external enclosure for $10 less. I was very tempted to buy that and then rip it out of the enclosure, as I did my Barricuda XT, but I decided $10 was enough to pay for a valid warranty and the option of returning it if it didn't work right away. Didn't end up needing that, but better safe than sorry.I will check back in and mark it down if the drive goes down or misbehaves any time soon. If you don't see that, it's still working like a champ.
summary: Great drive. Firmware update was easy.

I received this drive under Amazon's "Amazon Vine" program where they ship customers consumer products for free in exchange for a review. The device arrived via US Postal non-functional, and I was unable to return the drive to Amazon or exchange it through Seagate. This review documented my experience, but admittedly, isn't a review about a functional drive. If you're still interested, read on...Amazon shipped the bare drive (in a static bag only) via USPS using a plain manila envelope. There was absolutely no padding in the envelope. I removed the drive from the envelop and plugged it into myStartech eSATA USB to SATA Hard Drive Docking Station for Dual 2.5 or 3.5-Inch HDD SATADOCK22UE. Once powered up, the drive made a series of loud clicking sounds, and then spun down. After some quick troubleshooting, I determined that the drive was broken. The product warranty printed on the drive's label says it's covered up to 350 G's. I can't imagine that USPS subjected the drive to this level of torment during shipping. I immediately went to Seagate's site to open a warranty ticket. They had a slick online RMA tool, but it was unable to process the defunct drive's serial number. The site quickly routed me to Seagate's warranty number at 1-800-SEAGATE. I called the number and received a message that support was closed (during lunch hours). I called back at 1pm CT; selected option 3 for "Warranty Repairs" and was quickly greeted by a friendly customer service rep. It took 30 seconds from dialing the phone to talking to a live human being - practically unprecedented in today's America. The service rep was located in the U.S., and was extremely smart and professional. Because the drive was sent to me from Amazon Vine to review, Amazon doesn't process returns nor would Seagate provide a warranty on CDUs (Consumer Demonstration Units). I explained to Seagate that I would be writing a review on the drive, but they were unable to replace it.Naturally, my review isn't glowing. The proprietary date code printed on the drive's cover was 12076. A quick search on Google returned [...] which deciphered the date code as August 18th, 2011 - so the drive was essentially brand new, but likely built and shipped to the U.S. before the Thai flooding. The drive I received was manufactured in China.Overall I'd give Seagate (+1) star for friendly customer service, (-1) star for not replacing the brand new drive, and (-1) star for the drive's condition (but as I indicated earlier, the problem might have resulted from shipping it bare in a manila envelope).Would I purchase this drive? Yes. I'm a huge fan of Western Digital but Seagate has been releasing great products since the mid-2000's. I reviewed theSeagate Barracuda XT 2000 GB 7200RPM 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Bare Drive - ST32000641ASin February 2010 and found it to be an excellent drive with solid performance and quiet operation - the drive is still functioning today in one of our NAS servers. We also use theSeagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 4 TB (2 x 2 TB) Network Attached Storage ST340005LSA10G-RK, which is an exceptional NAS that consumes very little electricity.A case can be made that without actually using a functioning version of the drive, I can't give it one star; but with the drive arriving non-functional, and Seagate not honoring a warranty on a drive that was manufactured two months earlier, how would you rate it? Had Seagate replaced the drive, I would have omitted the drive's original non-functional condition from my final review.

reviewText: In order to avoid parallels to the common SATA II misnomer, the SATA-IO has compiled a set of marketing guidelines for the new specification. The specification should be called Serial ATA International Organization: Serial ATA Revision 3.0, and the technology itself is to be referred to as SATA 6 Gbit/s. A product using this standard should be called the SATA 6 Gbit/s [product name]. The terms SATA III or SATA 3.0, which are considered to cause confusion among consumers, must not be used. The standard was designed for SSDs but has been implemented for HDDs as well.Currently there's not much real world difference between SATA 3 and 6 for hard drives. SATA 6 was designed for SSDs but even those are not fast enough to take advantage of it yet.With 3.5in drives offering capacities exponentially higher than similarly-priced solid state counterparts, they're very far from dead. Considering the largest SSD size that's even remotely affordable is 256GB, those with lots of data will still want a magnetic hard drive. This drive can hold huge amounts of audio, video and picture data.If your computer only has a SATA 3GB interface you can still use 6Gb drives so long as the cable is less than a meter (most are much shorter).The free Seagate DiskWizard software allows you to install 3TB and 4TB hard drives in Windows, including XP, without UEFI BIOS but I wouldn't recommend going that route.In my opinion unless you have a cutting edge system, with the UEFI bios you may want to stick to smaller external drives as add-ons.

reviewText: I've ordered and used many Seagate (and other brand) drives over the years and have never experienced a problem until this one. It was completely unusable out of the box. It took 5 - 6 power cycles just to get the drive to initialize completely and be detected by the the BIOS. Once detected by bios and booted into Windows, as soon as Disk manager attempted to initialize the drive it began throwing I/O errors and hanging the system. From there it was hit or miss on whether it would detect at all, hang the system, blue screen the system, etc. This was on a very new system with an Asus mainboard, windows 7 ultimate, the latest BIOS, INF's and RST Drivers; plus other 3 TB's drive have worked fine in it so I'm almost certain its not the system.Maybe this was just an anomaly but it makes me think that maybe some of these other negative reviews aren't so far fetched -- re: getting multiple DOA drives in a batch, etc. Maybe there really is a QA problem post flooding last year. Will update after I receive a replacement.

I have ordered over 18 of these drives now and all are still performing great. The drives were not all ordered at the same time with the most recent set being ordered about a year ago now. I have had no drive failures and have been very happy with their performance.The only con would be Amazon's packaging which has changed recently. The hard drive used to fit very tightly in the plain generic box with no shifting, sliding or any movement at all. The boxes are now larger and the plastic holders that secure the drive inside do not hold it securely in place. When you pick up the box, you can actually feel the drive shifting around inside the box now. One star lost because of this new packaging.

I've got 7 of these drives, one of which failed out of warranty (just a couple of months ... thanks Seagate). The good thing is that it's a 7200rpm drive, the bad news is that depending on the firmware, your drive can chirp (aggressive head parking).Also according to a recent article on ars, Backblaze tested a lot of drives and found that Seagate's annual failure rate can be as high as 25% for some drives, around 9% for this drive. Not great considering the Hitachi drives are under 2%.Since I'm stuck with these drives and not exactly thrilled with that, I thought I'd share my recent findings. Thankfully I have a RAID 6 setup so I can weather a few drive failures. Just wish I knew beforehand how poor the reliability of these drives are. 1 out of 5 drives failed after 2 years, hopefully the other drives will fare better

reviewText: I am using this to occasionally control a PC in a bedroom hooked up to a 32" tv. We use it as a server, and doesn't get daily use. reviewText: I bought this to use with my 7000 series Samsung SMART TV and it is absolutely wonderful. Slightly smaller that a full size key board, so it doesn't take up much room on the coffee table. The receiver is in a USB port on the front of the PC, and I'm sitting about 12 feet away. No complaints there.One great feature is the addition of a left-mouse button on the upper left corner of the keyboard. Very thoughtful; really comes in handy. Another plus is the on-off switch that keeps me from inadvertently waking the PC.My only complaint is the over-sensitivity of the touchpad. I have to use a very light touch or the slightest movement will be interpreted as a click which usually provides unwanted results.This was not the first keyboard/mouse device I tried with my setup, but it's the one I'm sticking with. It's official. I have bought every full-sized (or nearly full-sized) couch keyboard on the market. This is not an exaggeration, I actually am not aware of another unit available to buy that I have not bought and hated.Every single one of them is AWFUL and I don't just *dislike* them, I actively hate them. Seriously we can put a man on the (expletive) moon and we can't make a couch keyboard that isn't terrible?So, what makes THIS couch keyboard terrible?No scroll wheel (or scrolly edge of trackpad), no ambidextrous clicking, and over-eager tap/click sensitivity on the trackpad.So, all of the keyboards that have "left mouse buttons" on both the left and right of the keyboard AND good range AND a decent pointing device, have utterly unusable latency and drop key input. Or as it would look if I were typing this on one of those, "hveu rly una y late anddpk eynpt"All of the keyboards that have decent range and don't drop key input constantly, have crap pointing devices. That would be the category this Logitech K400 falls in.I'm genuinely infuriated by the market's inability to produce a single (more expletives) couch keyboard that isn't awful and miserable. I'm going to return this Logitech because it sucks and it's still within its return period. Clearly nobody at Logitech has ever personally tried to actually sit on a couch and use a keyboard to control a computer.Edit: It's obvious that it *really* rustles peoples' jimmies when I write an unfavorable review of a product they like. OH NO I TOLD YOU MY HONEST OPINION IN A PRODUCT REVIEW, I MUST BE AN A-HOLE!... yeah whatever. If you don't want honest reviews don't read any of mine - it's no sweat off my coin purse.

I bought this for regular use at a computer. I want to be able to write documents and email and code software using it. It's not for light-duty use controlling an HTPC or the like in my situation. If that's not your situation, this review probably doesn't interest you.I want to use this as a primary keyboard on a crowded desk. I prefer compact keyboards with short key travel (like a great laptop keyboard), and am trying to cut down on wire clutter.A quick rundown, with more elaboration afterward.PROS* Installed without a hitch on Windows 7. I inserted the dongle, and everything just worked. This is quite nice.* The trackpad feel is nice. (Buttons are another story) Features like two-finger scroll and tap-to-click worked great, out of the box.* It's attractive.CONS* Keyboard feel is awful.* Trackpad buttons have the feel and finish of a mid-70s Pinto. They're loose and imprecise.* The keyboard layout is odd even by laptop standards.What I found with the keyboard is that the feel is absolutely awful. The keys have a good bit of side-to-side travel, and only the faintest of tactile feedback when the key is depressed. Thus, I found myself pressing really hard (to bottom out the key), and that really tires my hands. It's also quite unsatisfying. I type fast, and blasting out error-free text on a good keyboard is one of life's little pleasures.Worse, the key layout is more unstandard than most. Note that Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down overlay the cursor keypad, requiring use of a modifier key to scroll up and down within a word processor document or editor window. Yuck. Insert and Delete are just above Backspace, where you'll find yourself occasionally changing from insert-mode to overtype-mode if you miss the backspace key.The other layout sin is that the cursor keypad intrudes into the row with the shift key, such that up arrow sits between right-shift and the question mark. Sorry, but my hands expect question mark to be immediately next to shift. I wish I had noticed this in the photos.The trackpad buttons are loose and rattle-y, with a lot of travel. Tap-to-click on the trackpad obviates the need for the buttons most of the time, but I do use the buttons here and there. Every time I pressed them, I couldn't help but think, "these feel like junk."In the end, I give three stars because the unit does work without incident. However, for the typical price, I expected better from a brand like Logitech. I'll be returning this one.

I initially hooked up my laptop to my flatscreen and needed a way of controlling it from the couch. This little keyboard was the perfect solution. Small enough to be unobtrusive, yet large enough to allow for easy QWERTY typing. As another user said, I wouldn't write a paper with it, but it's comfortable enough to enter passwords/URL's without any problem. Has dedicated keys for Mute, Vol Up, Vol Down and Home. It also sports an additional button which acts as a left mouse click on the upper left side of the keyboard, allowing for easy navigation when being held "steering wheel" style.Using Logitech's SetPoint software, it allows for you to adjust mouse sensitivity, mouse acceleration, and turning on/off "tap-to-click". The touchpad also supports multi-finger scrolling, but I did not see a way to disable this if the need arose.As of this writing, you can customize 11 available F-keys to do the following Windows commands (F12 is reserved for Scroll Lock):Application switcherBackCalculatorCalendarCloseControl PanelCopyCutDocument FlipDocumentsEject DriveE-mailFavoritesForwardGadgetsGeneric ButtonHelpInternet RefreshInternet StopKeystroke AssignmentLaunch ProgramLock PCMaximizeMedia PlayerMessengerMinimize all windowsMuteMy ComputerMy DocumentsMy HomeMy MusicMy PicturesMy VideosNewNextOne-Touch SearchOpen fileOpen folderOpen Web pagePage DownPage UpPastePlay/PausePresentationPreviousPrintRecordRedoReplyRestore All WindowsRotate LeftRotate RightSaveSearch for filesShow DesktopShuffleSleepSpreadsheetsStopUndoVolume UpVolume DownZoom inZoom outZoom resetThe keyboard also has an on/off switch located on the top right edge to help save battery life. Overall it's about the size of a loaf of bread and very light. My only two criticisms are 1) that it doesn't have a dedicated Sleep key which would be ideal for an HTPC and 2) the right Shift key was cut in half to make room for the up arrow key (see product picture for detail). Because of this, every time I attempt to capitalize a left-handed letter, I move my cursor up one line. Very small quibbles though. Overall a great keyboard to use from the couch.

The first thing is petty but what is with the lines? The real problem is that there is no scroll line. You have to use two fingers to scroll. Now normally that might not be a big deal but try to scroll with two fingers while holding on to the keyboard with both hands. Even if it was a tad longer would not have caused it any harm. As it is, it is un-usable. Keep looking for a better keyboard. reviewText: As a 3/4 size keyboard I find this keyboard just too cramped to properly type on. This probably would have been fine if it wasn't for the addition of arrow keys wedged in under the Enter key. The Enter key is less than half size, but the real killer for me is the right-shift. The damn thing is the same size as a regular key (less than half of what a regular shift key is) and has the up-arrow right goddamn next to it. I can't even count the number of times just typing this review that I went to hit shift and ended up moving up a line instead. I've tried... I just cannot get used to this keyboard layout. I considered just changing the keymapping so that the arrow was another shift button, but the whole board is still too small to be comfortable to me. I'll keep it as a spare though... the cost to return it is about 1/3rd the price of the keyboard.The case is a light plastic. It feels cheap, like the battery cover plate is going to eventually break off. It does have a nice feeling keystroke, the range and accuracy of the wireless seems excellent, and the touchpad (the reason I bought this model vs. others) responds nicely. However the keys themselves are labeled with what appears to be just wet-transfer decals (like the ones you get in a model airplane kit) which will undoubtedly rub off with use.This would probably do well as an HTPC keyboard where very little typing is intended. (No emails, no replying to forums while browing on the TV) but is otherwise not going to work as a desktop keyboard.No me gusta.
summary: Small, with a bad key layout...

reviewText: I purchased this keyboard because of size and the built-in mouse/touch-pad. The size is perfect, exactly what I wanted. As soon as I pulled this keyboard out of the box, I immediately noticed two things. First, which is more minor: the F-keys (F1-F12) are super small, yet there is a TON of dead space on the keyboard that could have easily accommodated normal sized F-keys or additional media buttons (more on this later). Second: there is little difference between the height and feeling of the "mouse" keys for left and right clicks and the height of the touchpad. I've been using (and frustrated) with the keyboard included with the Logitech Revue Google TV debacle for a year now, and its keyboard had the same problem as this keyboard.Why Logitech doesn't put some kind of tactile feel on the left and right click buttons on keyboards like this is beyond me. For example, most keyboards have small nubs or bevels on the "F" and "J" keys that make it easier to know where your fingers are on the keyboard without looking down. Why not on the left and right click buttons? They are especially needed when the height difference between them and the keyboard and the touchpad are all very similar. I've been trying to use this keyboard for a few weeks, and just like my Revue keyboard that I've had for a year, I am pressing down on the touchpad at times thinking I am on the left-click button.This keyboard also doesn't have media keys other than for volume and mute. Many keyboards, including most others from Logitech, have keys for playing music and video for functions like Previous, Next, Play, Stop, etc. There are none on this keyboard. Even if the keyboard required something like Logitech's SetPoint software installed in order to use keys like this, that would be fine. But the keys simply don't exist, even though there is so much empty space on the keyboard.I'm not digging this product.

reviewText: I bought this to use as a controller for my htpc running xbmc. I had been previously been using a gyration air remote that gaveme nothing but headaches (missing keys I needed having lots I didn't).The touchpad works pretty well, I only have windows7 so I didn't really test the multitouch gestures.The keyboard itself seems ok, not too cheap feeling. Logitech seems to want to create a device that is small enough as a home-theater PC remote but still big enough as a regular PC keyboard & mouse. Does cutting it both ways work for Logitech? This is currently the #1 best-selling keyboard at Amazon, so maybe it does.Most people would likely use Logitech K400 as a HTPC remote to be used on the living-room couch. A HTPC remote differs from a regular remote in that it is more "PC-centric". It is made for computer users who want to view their media on their HDTVs and sound systems, while still sticking to their favorite Windows or Mac interface.The K400 is light, weighing only 1.1 lbs, lighter than an iPad, so it should be couch-friendly. Its wireless range is good, as I have no connection problem within 20 feet away from the PC.The touchpad is fine for basic mouse clicks and navigation. It has no scroll zones, and it doesn't support a lot of gestures. You can single-tap for left mouse click, single-tap-and-hold for drag, and double-tap for scroll, and that's it. There is no gesture for right mouse click or middle mouse click (many laptops can do this). You cannot drag-lock, and that means when you drag something on the screen, your finger has to be always on the pad. To adjust the speed of the mouse movement, you can use your operating system's control panel or Logitech's Setpoint utility, which is not included in the package but can be downloaded at Logitech's website.You also cannot two-finger-pinch-zoom on the touchpad like you do on iOS devices, MacBook, or newer PC laptops. And that brings me to another topic.When you use the K400 on a couch looking at your TV screen, suddenly you realize you are not as close to your TV as you are to your PC, and you need to magnify the screen. Windows 7 and XP do have a built-in Magnifier utility (look under Accessories, Accessibility). But you have to run and control it manually with regular mouse clicks and drags and/or keyboard shortcuts. Fortunately, Logitech's Setpoint utility lets you launch a program with a hotkey, so at least you can launch the Magnifier utility with a touch of a button. I hope in future K400 models, Logitech would add a pinch-zoom gesture a la iPhone/iPad that would make magnifying easier.As a HTPC remote, this keyboard surely has far too few built-in media keys. It only has mute, volume up and down keys at the top. Obviously, you will have to rely on the hotkeys of your media applications to control playback. Logitech seems to believe that HTPC users may actually prefer to do that. In my case, they are right. I've been using PowerDVD on the PC for a long time and I'm very much used to just pressing F, B, N, P (hotkeys for forward, rewind, next chapter, previous chapter) instead of using dedicated media keys. There are also many special functions accessible only via hotkeys, such as Blu-ray's red, blue, green, and yellow buttons. So I'm very comfortable being without dedicated media keys. For those who are not used to media playback on a PC, this is not a convenience, and, thus, this keyboard is not made for them.Is this keyboard good for gaming on your HDTV? I have no problems playing Diablo III, adventure games, casual games, or any games that don't require precise mouse control. Playing first-person shooters that require accurate aiming, however, could be problematic, as K400's touchpad simply isn't as precise as a more sophisticated gaming mouse, such as my Logitech G5. You can get by with certain first-person games, like Portal 2, which is more forgiving to your aiming accuracy.Is this keyboard good for regular PC work? It feels more cramped than a laptop keyboard, mainly due to the much smaller Enter, right Shift, Backspace, and Control keys, which are the most used (that's why they are usually made wider). And the lack of a numeric pad, not even an Fn-extended numeric pad, would further hamper an office user. Other often-used keys like Home, End, PgUp, and PgDn also need to be Fn-extended (meaning you need to press the green Fn key plus another key). In short, if you do office work or need to do long periods of typing, pass this over and get a regular keyboard instead.For casual PC work on a couch, such as surfing the web, sending a few emails, shopping online, etc., this keyboard does fine.In short, the Logitech K400 is good as a HTPC keyboard for media playback and casual PC activities. I have been using it for just such purposes and have decided to keep it despite all the aforementioned shortcomings. I have tried alternative HTPC input devices and they have not worked out well. I've used iPhone apps such as the highly-touted "Mobile Mouse Pro" as well as hand-held mini HTPC keyboards, and found that I really needed a near-full-size keyboard that is also small and couch-friendly. The K400 seems to fit the bill.

Trying to find a good keyboard for an HTPC is hard and there are many considerations. Unfortunately, this one does not really live up to the cut for that purpose:1) Trackpad - it works, but it's not terribly responsive. Two finger scrolling works as does windows 8 gestures (swipe down, up, left, right from the edges), but again - not very responsively.2) Media Keys - Most of these are targeted at Windows 8 and mostly work fine in Linux (at least the volume and play/pause).3) Typing - For a media center, you really don't need to type tons; however, when you do you want to know you can semi-accurately type. The layout is slightly offset and the keys, mostly along the right side, are smaller than usual (right shift, arrows, etc). While somewhat frustrating, not a deal-breaker.4) Build Quality - The build quality is fairly poor. There is significant flex in the keyboard and it seems as though (conjecture only) it won't be terribly durable.5) Reception - The reception is good from 1' - ~10' (max) with line of sight. That works for many cases (mine included) for a smaller living room, but I get close to the edge of the range if I lay back on my couch with it.The description is actually focused on a mobile keyboard for use with a laptop, for that application it makes more sense (hence the 3 stars). The reception shouldn't really be an issue in that case, but I still wouldn't want to use the poorly implemented trackpad. I also wouldn't have lots of confidence in the build quality.Typically, I love logitech hardware and have always felt that they had quality products with actually useful features, but this one definitely is an anomaly in my experience with them. If you're looking for a HTPC keyboard, I would go for the IOGear GKM561R. Similar price-range, but great reception, features, implementation. If you're looking for something for your laptop to bring mobile, then I would probably go elsewhere if it were me.

As I am typically using this at night I can't really see it which makes typing something of a chore. But for the price it was worth it despite its lack of light. Not too small, not too big. I use it to control my HTPC and it's form factor is perfect. Not much to brag about, it's just a keyboard and touchpad that work as they should. The smaller size and integration make it just right for my living room in front of the TV.

Pros - excellent small size and no wires results in less clutter on the desk.Cons - Keyboard has been reduced in size so much that the PageUp, PageDown, Home and End keys require also pressing a function key at the same time which is awkward and annoying.Touchpad has almost no configuration options, no sensitivity setting, no scroll zones and verticle scrolling requires dragging two fingers up or down the middle of the touchpad and parallel with the sides. Since your hand and fingers are not typically positioned in a way that is also exactly parallel to the sides of the touchpad, scrolling can be inconsistent. Touch and drag almost never works.As a desktop replacement keyboard, this is not the greatest solution, but there are few products that include an integrated touchpad.As a remote control keyboard, perhaps to a laptop connected to a TV, this is an excellent choice.Note: I purchased this direct from Logitech since Amazon had a two month shipping delay.
summary: Not perfect, but fairly good - touchpad has been dumbed down

reviewText: I was putting together a second HTPC and needed a wireless keyboard. My other HTPC is equipped with an IOGEAR with the laser trackball, and it works quite well. Not thinking, I ordered this keyboard due to he Logitech name. The touchpad is the problem. The mouse buttons are unreliable, and I find the touchpad to be difficult to use. I wish I'd bought a second IOGEAR keyboard instead.UPDATE: 07/27/13Just received the IOGEAR cordless keyboard/trackball combination I ordered. This piece of junk Logitech is headed for the bin. The keyboard was okay, but the touchpad was a nightmare. I stuck with this frustrating piece of garbage for one year to try to get my money out of it, but I've had it. I've read the glowing reviews some people have given this thing, such as it works with any computer. What keyboard doesn't?Trust me, buy the IOGEAR Multimedia Keyboard with Laser Trackball and Scroll Wheel, 2.4GHz Wireless GKM561R (Black) by Iogear. It's MUCH better choice. I generally like Logitech equipment, but this keyboard was a huge disappointment.
Love the brand but absolutely hate this expecific keyboard due to its happier sensitivity to motion and poor assessment of actions
summary: I am not gonna lie, I hate this keyboard

reviewText: For a while now, I've been wanting to purchase a nice, portable keyboard that will allow me to use our nice laptop paired with our LCD television. I took a chance on this keyboard and, for the most part, am not disappointed whatsoever with it. In fact, I am typing this very review using this set-up, and it is working quite well for that purpose so far. It's not a perfect set-up, by any means, but it is a very satisfactory solution for these circumstances.The keyboard is quite small and light-weight, making for an ideal keyboard for portable, couch-surfing computer use. Its small size also makes it very easy to store the keyboard in a drawer when not in use, which I like because it keeps my home less cluttered. You have a little touchpad built-in, which is very convenient if you don't want to fiddle with a portable mouse and keyboard. There is a very nice button in the top left of the keyboard that acts as a second left-side mouse-button, so you can use your left thumb in combination with your right hand with smooth, intuitive results. It's great for that. The keyboard is clearly designed with this sort of set-up, that is to say, relaxed computer use on your TV, and it really fits the bill almost perfectly for it. The usb plug-in ranges from very small for your laptop, to normal usb keyboard plug-in size for your large desk-top. I use the smaller one and it works well and is hardly noticeable on my laptop. There's a switch to turn the keyboard off to conserve battery-life, and I really like that myself. It helps keep the already-decent battery life preserved even longer.It's not all perfect, however. For one, the connection can be a bit spotty. It seems that if there is anything in the way between the laptop and the keyboard, the signal is messed up and mouse movement and keyboard typing becomes erratic and virtually useless. This happens even if I'm less than five feet away from the laptop! Moving the keyboard a little bit to be more in line with the computer usually does the trick. The keyboard itself is fine, but will take some getting used to. To fit a full keyboard AND a touchpad on an already smaller-than-normal platform makes for a very cramp keyboard indeed. Having smaller-than-usual keys is tricky enough, but even keys such as shift and tab are a lot smaller, about the same size as normal letters, and this takes a lot of time adjusting to. It can be a real pain at first, trust me. There's no indicator on the keyboard that says whether caps-lock is on, or how much power is on, which is quite unfortunate.I've owned this keyboard for roughly 4-6 weeks now and have acclimated to using it fairly well by now. I waited this long so that I could write an honest assessment of the product without the blush of excitement of using my laptop comfortably on the TV, or the blush of irritation as I struggled to get used to it. Writing a review like this back then would have been nearly impossible due to the different size/set-up of a standard keyboard, but now it feels like second-nature. All-in-all, I'd definitely recommend this keyboard to all who are looking for a way to relax in the living room while using the computer, or who are looking for a convenient way to use your large-screen TV as your monitor. It's definitely a nice piece of tech to have. I hope this review was helpful. Thanks for reading. Toodles.
summary: Although not perfect, this keyboard fulfills its purpose well

reviewText: The range on this thing is great. I originally bought a cheap handheld device, whose ergonomics I preferred, but it died within 4 months and had no range. This device is a great size. It is not too large. It works without installing their Logitech software, but you will find that it accidentally clicks on things all the time as you move the cursor around. I installed the software and it works great now.

This is one of the best purchases I have ever made. This keyboard works very well. I use it on all of my computers, my tablet and my DVD Smart player. I have never had a connection error. I added a Cosmos skin and that gave the keys less slippery. The touch pad is not to sensitive and the keyboard has many setting to make it behave how you want it to. The keyboard layout is fantastic and also has some programmable buttons. If you are looking for a portable keyboard this is the one you need.
summary: The Only Keyboard You Will Ever Need

reviewText: Bought this to use with my Samsung Smart-TV. Works great, plug and play. Much easier than using the on-screen keyboard.

This keyboard really works. I am a big man with big hands and don't have any trouble with the size of the keys. This unit took the place of a big wireless Logitech keyboard and wireless mouse. I never had a good surface to run the mouse on and this unit works very well using the touch pad.Update 3/7/13 I just ordered my third K400 for a Windows 7 computer in the kitchen. Instead of the K400, I received a K400r from Amazon. Their product information didn't say K400r. The big difference between the two keyboards is that the volume up, volume down, and mute buttons aren't on the top left anymore. They are on the function keys instead. I have two other K400's that I use all the time but unfortunately this one is different. You can reprogram 3 of the 4 buttons on the top left but you can't reprogram the Home key. So I reprogrammed the volume up, volume down, and mute keys but the Home key changes the location of the volume up and volume down. The music key on the K400r has an indention just like the mute key on the K400.I don't like the K400r because it is different from my other two K400's. I think Amazon needs to identify this on their website selling this as the K400.I still like the K400 a lot for HTPC uses but I dropped my review mark because of Amazon's misleading information.

I ordered this for a relative for whom I was making an HTPC, and I liked it so much that I bought a second one for myself. The size and the integrated touchpad are really nice for driving an HDTV-connected PC from the cough or bed, and the wireless strength really surprised me. I'm using it at a distance of only about 15 feet, but it's GOING THROUGH A WALL and working fine!I'm using it with Ubuntu 12.04 without any trouble. Some people mentioned that the reliance on Windows Logitech drivers for configuring the touchpad speed was annoying, but that's not a feature that I'll miss. Touchpad tap-to-click (which I hate) can be disabled without any driver support by pressing Fn + Left Mouse Button. And the media keys worked out of the box.As for negatives, the media keys are quite limited. There is only volume up/down/mute and a browser home key. Play/pause/stop would have been nice. The button at the top-left that looks like a mouse is just a second left mouse button, which I think is a pretty dumb use of an extra key. The other thing I don't like so much is the key construction. I have gotten used to the "chiclet" style keyboards on modern laptops and this style feels a little clumsy by comparison. But ultimately, the form factor, integrated touchpad, and low price make for a good product for HTPCs.EDIT: After more usage, I discovered that the signal strength is pretty marginal after the loss caused by the wall, so if I'm on the other side of that room then it doesn't work well. I bought a 10-foot USB extension cable for the ridiculously low price of $1.74, ran that around the wall, and plugged the wireless receiver into that. Now it works great.
summary: Great value, only a couple flaws

reviewText: I bought this to use on my HTPC to control XBMC and it works great. My only complaint is the trackpad. It's bad. Usable, but bad. Often times moving the cursor will actually trigger a drag. There's also been some weird interference issues every now and then but I blame my house having lots of wireless devices.For the price you can't really go wrong though. There's other small keyboards out there but they're really terrible compared to this.
summary: A must have for your HTPC

reviewText: This integrated keyboard and touchpad is a great idea for a media TV, but the touchpad is awful. The touchpad's sensitivity sucks and the acceleration is too fast, regardless of the software settings. This results in an annoyingly slow curser most of the time followed by frustrating streaks of the mouse across the screen. Maybe the windows drivers are better, but I'm using mine on a linux/chrome os box.

I use this for my media PC connected to my TV to browse the Web, play music/video, etc. The keyboard is not very comfortable to type on and the keys are small. The touchpad leaves much to be desired. However, it works, and it's cheap.

I use this keyboard with an Ubuntu HTPC, and had tried it on an Android HDMI stick, and it worked there as well. It could be improved, however. The touchpad is tad too sensitive, and you wind up activating icons just trying to pass over them. Also, it should have LED backlight feature at this price, and finally a scrolling wheel or device would be nice. It's a bit of a pain using the touchpad to scroll, especially since it's so sensitive, you wind up tapping something when you have to remove your finger and start at the top of the pad again to scroll, etc.
summary: Works with Ubuntu and Android as well

reviewText: I just received the Logitech Wireless Touch Keyboard K400 with Built-In Multi-Touch Touchpad and have used it for about an hour.Pros: remarkably good packaging, easy installation, batteries included, touchpad works greatCon: it is not standard keyboard size. Perhaps I missed this in the product description, but the entire keyboard with touchpad is about five inches shorter than the keyboard I was previously using. The shift key is quite small (the size of the arrow button located just below it) so many typos, mistakes, and wrong lines have been my initial experience with actually using the keyboard.
summary: Great keyboard--but note it is "laptop size"

reviewText: OS: Ubuntu 12.04The touch pad is a little unresponsive for my tastes; however, this may be due to my OS. My main problem with this item is that it is very small. The description does not make mention that this keyboard is substantially smaller than a standard keyboard. I don't really expect to have to read the dimension of a keyboard.IMO the size should be denoted in the description. I'm going to keep it because I do like the fact that the mouse and keyboard are integrated. I guess I'll just use my wired keyboard when I plan on doing work on my computer.

I wouldn't recommend this drive just because it's ridiculously slow. I get write speeds of 3.5Mb/s which means a single 1Gb file can take well over a few minutes to get copied.It certainly looks very cute, it's about the size of your thumbnail - I mean literally that size, but I wish they'd given a lanyard or a small rope/thread to attach a key ring or something to it. It's so small that it would be quite possible to just lose it altogether. Think of it as a few nickels stacked on top of each other.Another problem is the small loop is so tiny that most off-the-shelf lanyards won't fit in it. It would allow just a single thread to pass through whereas all lanyards require you to put a loop through them.I bought it, and if I'd known how slow it was, I wouldn't have. I'm just going to keep it around in my camera bag to dump files on because it's small and light - apart from that, the slow write speed makes it non-worthy for any normal day to day use.
Slow on upload

Positives: Super-tiny and seems to work as well as other USB flash drivesNegatives: It didn't come with a strap. The metal loop is tiny and flimsy. I ran another thin metal loop through the flash drive's loop and my keychain. Within a week the loop on the flash drive had broken. I guess I needed a flexible strap instead of the metal loop. My bad.

Sandisk made a big mistake by making this a Fixed drive vs removable due to win 8 certification and not offering a flip bit utility like other MFGS. Can't be used as a bootable drive and this is a drive you don't pull out often due to the size which is good if you plan to keep in your usb slot.

I love these. They are exactly as described and fit into the laptop so that I can travel and not worry about breaking of my flash drive. These are much smaller than I envisioned though, so now I just need to worry about losing them.

Just got it today only to realize that it is defective.Write protected. Thought that there is a way to go around it. Googled and read forums for about an hour or so, with no luck. Called Sandisk Customer Support, was asked a lot of unnecessary questions before stating the reason for calling and getting a response that it is defective and they can't do anything about it. =/Kind of a bummer, since I was pretty excited about getting it today.
I ordered more than 2 and non of them working, and they can't be formatted. waste of money. this is the first time i buy a SanDisk product with such quality.
summary: I ordered more than 2 and non of them working

reviewText: This guy is tiny. I mean really small. So small you could almost swallow it. It is so small that it can be hard to pull out of the USB port. I wanted to tie a wire to it, but you need a really thin wire to fit into the hole they provide. IF this device was even an inch longer, it would be OK and a great bargain.Too small, is the final word. Don't buy it since you'll probably lose it, or be unable to stick in or pull it out of the USB port.
summary: Great to have a 32 gig USB Drive but...

reviewText: I am using this flash-drive in my car for music. So far, I disconnected from the slot to include more music on it and connected again with no problems at all.For those who complained about loosing or dropping it, you knew in advance that it was small. And that's why I bought it and that's why I love it.
I like the small size but with this new password protected encrypt private files software they don't work with Rhapsody. I used these for music to play in the car. I will try another brand.

I'm a photojournalist and often deliver photos to clients on flash drives. I was all set to buy a couple of dozen SanDisk Cruzer Fit 4GB USB 2.0 flash drives, but bought one first to give it a test. Glad I did!A cheap no-name flash drive from MicroCenter takes 5:15 to copy 2.90 GB of data.This stupid SanDisk Cruzer Fit 4GB took 11:47 to copy the same 2.90 GB of data. Over TWICE as slow!I used a direct USB 2.0 connection, not a hub.This flash drive is far too slow for professional work. Too bad this review will disappear among all these glowing reviews. I gave it two stars because: 1. it works, 2. it's pretty cute, 3. it's cheap. But fairly useless.
summary: Slow! Sickingly slow. Useless for professional work.

reviewText: The device itself if alright. But if You plan to attach it to your keychain, which is one of the only ways that you won't lose something so very, very small - BEWARE! The tiny metal ring attachment, in addition to being very hard to attach because it is so tiny, is extremely flimsy. After just a couple weeks on my keychain, the little ring attachment (the one built into the memory stick, such that it cannot be replaced with something stronger) simply broke. It's metal, but it is extremely thin; just barely thicket than a wire, and it just snapped. I was damn lucky I didn't loose the thing in that moment. Had it the circumstances been slightly different, I may have easily overlooked it.And NO, there was no "unusual use" that would have led to this; it was just a shoddy build quality, plain and simple. And NO, not all flash drives give you this problem. I had my last one on my keychain for years without it breaking off. It was just a slightly thicker metal loop - that's it. There's no reason that this one could not have been made more sturdily; it just simply was not.Such a simple thing, really, entirely defeating the purpose of the device. It could have been so easily avoided, yet they decided to save a few pennies... pennies that they saved which could easily lead to countless lost files and countless lost hours of your time. Shame on them.
summary: This purchase will end in tears

reviewText: I bought this to replace an older drive that I kept forgetting. I thought I would attach this one to my key chain so I would not forget it. This worked great for a while. The drive is plenty big enough in terms of data storage for my needs, and is physically small enough that it doesn't make my key chain too bulky. But there are a couple issues. First, the key chain attachment loop is on the drive itself, not the cover, so while I won't loose the drive, it is sometimes difficult to get it into a USB slot with my keys attached. I solved this with a quick detach key chain but that gets me back to the danger of forgetting the drive. The second problem is that the little metal loop on the drive where I attached my key chain broke off after about a month. Unfortunately that was pretty much the end of the usefulness for this product.
summary: Good Drive, bad key chain attachment

reviewText: I tend to misplace things fairly often. That made this a bad choice for me because it is so tiny. It's also dark in color, so not that easy to see. It's tiny enough for me to have misplaced it many times and then looked high and low for this little rascal. I will buy something larger next time.

I bought this for my wife to use with her new car stereo, as it has a USB input for mp3 playing. I have to say, when plugged in, you can hardly see this drive. It actually looks like a button on the stereo. You hardly notice it at all.As for usability: The drive's read and write speed are not lightning quick, but are fast enough for what we use it for. The stereo it's used in never has and read or loading problems, never had a glitch. This flash drive does have a very small yellow/orange LED on the back. For our particular use, it flashes when first plugged in or when the stereo is first turned on, but it does not flash or blink while it's in use or when every file is accessed. This is a good thing, as it would be pretty annoying to have an LED constantly blinking while you're driving, especially at night.The drive also has a small lanyard hole, but we're not using it. It's nearly microscopic, though. Also included is a small cover to keep the contacts protected when not plugged in. Finally, the file stability seems to be pretty good with this drive. We've not had a problem with corrupted or missing files.As another reviewer stated, this device is very small. It can easily be lost and is not intended to be constantly plugged in and removed. It's intended to be a semi-permanent emplacement.Overall, this USB drive has performed beyond expectations and met all my requirements. I would highly recommend.

This small powerful flash drive is great in my car. It takes up almost no room, but has lots of storage. With a lot of work, I was able to attach a wrist lanyard to the drive--to help me keep track of it. The connection for the lanyard is tiny, but it is possible to attach something to it if you are determined. Glad I got this.

After not being able to get it to work which should be as easy as plugging it in. I own lots of flash drives so was supprised that this did not work.I even went through Sandisk for help and they advised it was faulty and to return it for a refund. Only had it maybe 2 weeks. I returned it to the seller only for them to never refund my money. Have the seller listed in my information as someone not to buy from.

Didn't work. It took forever to arrive from China. I took a lose on the product. The seller said he would refund my money, if I first took back the negative feedback I gave them. They are in China , I'm in the U.S., I figured my chance of a refund was slim. I wasn't going to take back my feedback. If I save one person from such a negative experience, It would be worth my lose.

Super compact form factor makes it ideal for automobile use: rather than leaving an iPod or other device roasting in the car, I just fill up the SanDIsk with audio files, plug it into the car's USB port, and forget about it. The only downside? Painfully slow write times.
summary: Tiny Drive Good for Auto or Laptop Use, but Slow Write Speeds

reviewText: it's small which is an advantage, but you can easily lose the cap

reviewText: the key chain was low quality and it would fall off occasionally but thankfully always inside my pocket. Also after a couple months of being in my pocket, the small metal part on the usb end broke off but again, it was inside my pocket. So don't rely on that keychain to hold it, but now that it broke i don't know how to carry it around easily. Nice large storage for the small profile with very good price/gb, but it is slow, max speed of 5 MB/s.

I have a hard time keeping track of it. You need to buy the string to put on the loop. If you attach it directly to a key chain the loop breaks off and then you have to try and keep up with it. Works great - be sure to buy the string.

It is a great little product, surprisingly thumbnail small in size with a humongous storage capacity. I was very happy with it for the first two months but then a couple of days ago I plug it into my laptop and I get a "this device is write protected" message. Huh?! but I just used it last night and it worked fine. I did an extensive investigation on the internet, tried the DISKPART utility, tried low level formatting, tried changing permissions, even, with my heart palpitating in apprehension, tried modifying the registry. All to no avail. Even more weirdly I can't even make a proper backup of what is on the disk - I can read and copy some of the folders, the others I can't copy to my laptop hard drive. The general consensus on the internetz seems to be that this is caused by a bug in the software and there is no option other than to return it for a replacement. Of course, Amazon does not issues RMA for this item after a one month window, which means that I have to bear the loss. So, as they say, caveat emptor!
summary: Great for 2 months, then a bug caused "Write Protect" error

reviewText: Sometimes, size does matter, and in this case, this is too teeny. I have small hands, and yet, I have difficulty pulling this out of the USB slot. It's small size also makes it too easy to lose.

I bought two of these for my wife and I thinking that smaller is always better, but in this case that's not entirely true. I love the idea of a tiny flash drive, but these are so small that without some kind of lanyard or something to keep track of them with it would so incredibly easy to lose in a bag or a drawer. There is a small metal loop on the flash drive where you could attach a lanyard, but in my opinion that should have been included by the manufacturer. Plus, the loop is so tiny that it would be difficult to find a lanyard small enough and at the same time strong enough to be useful. That said, I love the convenience of having a super portable flash drive and the tiny design of this drive likely won't be an issue for someone that wants it to be as small as possible.
summary: I didn't think a flash drive could be too small, but ...

reviewText: This drive does not have the "removable" bit set in the firmware, so any computer will think it is a fixed disk, like a hard drive. Linux cannot transfer any files to it, because the firmware metadata is so screwed up. Could anything be easier than marking a removable disk as removable? What a total joke.
summary: SanDisk gets the easy things wrong

reviewText: The tiny SanDisk "Cruzer Fit" USB Flash Drives are the perfect solution to adding conveniently-removable storage space to your laptop without fear of the device becoming snagged or caught on nearby gear and/or clothing. The part that sticks out of the USB Port extends only ONE-QUARTER INCH beyond the surface -- it's actually kinda hard to remove, due to the tight fit and the small gripping area of the device -- BUT -- you can be sure the thing won't just FALL out when you're not looking.;>)The product illustration is ACTUAL SIZE of the Cruzer Fit 4GB. What you see is the COVER on the left, and the USB PLUG-IN on the right. The BLACK portion of the USB plug-in is the part that sticks out of the USB Port. It's practically snag-proof, and near-perfect for convenience and ease-of-use.I'm just wondering what to do with the "Cover" while the device is in use.There's a teeny-weeny, tiny-winey, teensy-weensy, little-bitty hole in the device -- presumably for a "carry-strap" -- but a piece of 10-lb.-test fishing line is about all I could get through the small, partially-obstructed hole.As they say, size matters -- and the device's conveniently-small size is kind of a penalty, since it's so small that it's hard to keep track of.I plan to leave mine plugged in to my PC, to be used as a Portable Family Photo Library.SanDisk quality and Amazon's low price made this a great deal !!

It's amazing how much memory they can get into such a small device. However, the small size is also a potential negative. As others have said, it would be easy to lose if you don't attach a lanyard to it ASAP. I used Nylon 10 lb. test fishing line. Seems to work OK.

PROS:- price- form factor, very low profile, creates an appealing flush result- reliability. have 2 or 3 of these and none have yet failedCONS:- speed. i won't get into read/write speeds as others have already done that. it isn't USB3 so don't expect that. Xbox 360 rates the drive as usable but under-performing.UPDATE:- lowering this review to 1 star until the abusive SPAM reply by SANDISK is removed. Product deserves 4/5 but their SPAM deserves punishment.

reviewText: This is really small. Great for laptops and tablets! It is so small that its hard to remove with my large hands. There is a spot to put a lanyard so thar helps

I bought this to supplement my Mac Air's limited hard drive space. My only problem with it, is that it seems to run slightly warmer than I am used to. I've noticed this in more than one laptop, and my desktop so it must be the device. No problems as of yet though.

So far this drive is just fine. The encryption software that comes with it is horribly slow, and includes no progress bar so you have no idea how long it will take. I deleted it and used safehouse instead.For a drive this impossibly small, Sandisk should include a small lanyard, period. Minus 1 star for sure for this oversight. Without a lanyard you have no way to secure this drive to a keychain or something else, and it's also hard to remove from the computer. This thing is small for sure, and without a lanyard it's very likely you will drop it and have a hard time finding it. Other drives I have purchased have had a small lanyard included in the package, for such a small drive this one should have had one too.The reason I debated giving only 3 stars is because I paid for a 32gb drive and got a drive with a capacity of 29.8. I deleted the pre-installed software, and reformatted the drive, still 29.8. Where is my extra 2.2 gig? That's actually a LOT of space in and of itself, and I think if it's advertised at 32gb, it should be at least pretty darn close (31.8 wouldn't have bothered me).In the end, 3 stars. If the advertised space matched the actual capacity it would have been 4.

I use small USB storage "drives" like this in my cars as music storage, where they have a front USB Connection. Previously I had been purchasing the HP USB storage, as this was the smallest I could find and only stuck out about a quarter inch, but after buying this, it sticks out just barely enough to get your fingers around it which I love - barely noticed, holds plenty of songs, and performance is as expected.

Don't get this or anything from SanDisk. I bought 2 of these flash drives and one of them came out as "read only". Really?There isn't a physical switch to remove the setting so I'm basically screwed.I got it in November 2013 and did not open it until now and the return window has expired.Not only did it not work, but the flash drives from SanDisk are slow. I should have learned the first time not to buy from this company but the prices are low and I thought I'd give them another shot. Fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice, shame on me. I'm done with this company.

I have to keep tweaking the registry in Windows 7 on one of my computers to get it to read this device. Not good. Not the Sandisk quality I expect. The only fix I could find was a registry tweak VID_780 is nonsense. Sandisk has no answer for this?Update: I found out that I had a defective drive and SANDISK contacted me after reading this review. Wow are they cool. Replacing it with a new one and their tech support and return policy is great. Will keep you posted on this when I get the new one at no cost. They even paid for the return shipping.
The title says it all. Thansfer speeds are 4MB/s or less so it takes a while to copy large files. Very small device though, designed to be plugged in and left there

While the price to performance / cost per GB is very good, the Sandisk Encryption software crashes PCs - both my lenovo and asus suffered blue screens - this kind of stuff scare me more. Rather be careful not losing it than having it encrypted and the SW thing crashing PCs.
Perfect for my car's USB port, I can store nearly my entire iTunes library on it and it's small enough not to be in the way and it's not even noticeable. Looking forward to the 128gb version!!!
I like a small thumb drive but this is so small it is hard to grasp it when removing it from my computer. I am sure it will get lost.

I bought these to copy mp3 files to play in my car. The USB socket in my car has a console door over it, and the door could not be closed with a larger flash drive in it. These are certainly small. That means that unfortunately they are easy to misplace. The real down side is that, in my car at least, I cannot remove the drive from the USB port with my fingers. There's very little to grab, and they are a really tight fit. I have to use needle-nose pliers to get them out of the port.
summary: Being small has pros and cons.

reviewText: This product is astoundingly cheap for how much storage it has, and it really is so small that I can just leave it plugged into my laptop and not have to worry about it getting bent or snapped off in my backpack. The only downside is the speed. With how large this is, I store larger file sizes on them, such as movies and whatnot. Transferring these files takes noticeably long, and some higher quality files can't even play from the flash drive because of how slow it is. Other than the speed though, the product has been reliable, small, and very convenient.

good USB for car use especially for Ford sync, very small and will fir perfectly on the USB slots, also very cheap per GByte of data

this is a quality product, but in my case I wanted one that I could link to my keychain so I would always have it and not lose it, as with thumb drives this small, very easy to lose, but SanDisk is great company

Really small USB, is perfect for the car radio, so you won't accidentally punch it, great capacity and 2.0 is fast enough for reading a lot of mp3. Recommended for car radios with USB input.

Works just like expected. Very small. Excellent for car radio's playing back MP3 files or movies.Big enough to be able to unplug it comfortably.Looks like SD card memory instead of flash memory at that size...Doesn't get hot.Hope it'll last.
I just dont like the bloatware, which is included too in my previous SanDisk, so i just erase itbut the speed is still good for R/W,

reviewText: I bought this to add supplemental storage to my Chromebook. The flash drive sticks out just a bit farther than I would like, but otherwise, it works fine.

product did not come with any way to attach to a keychain etc. metal loop on device was too small for the key ring or nylon loops I had. after getting on to a ring it broke off after less than a week in pocket. for something so easily lost its just not worth the hassle.

I love the Cruzer Fit for my Kia Sorento. The size factor of this thumb drive is spectacular...as long as you always remember where you put it. It's EXTREMELY small. This flash drive is Tiny! but it works great. I have a OTG Cable for my tablet, and I just leave this stuck in it all the time, just plugging it in when I need it.
the keyhole on the drive is too small for my key chain(a small one)... so, i have to use a wire to tie it to my key chain.... eventually, it's lost...

reviewText: I normally don't write reviews on products unless they really leave an impression with me. With that said, this tiny 32GB USB 2.0 flash drive is really slow. This flash drive is about the size of an adult thumbnail. Only a barely noticeable portion protrudes from the device it is plugged into. I use this in my Chevy Spark with the MyLink system. I picked this because it is short, it doesn't stick out and get in the way of the cupholders. No access issues as the car usb system recognizes it and plays all my music and videos that are stored on it.

Bought this drive to use in my Raspberry PI for hosting the operating system. It was small and compact just like the PI. Unfortunately it seems to be completely dead after only a few uses. I can't format it or do anything with it - just throws IO errors.
The size of this thing is amazingly small. The capacity choices are great also.My only problem is that it is also amazingly slow compared to other products in this category...
I like it but is a pain to store any large file in it. It just takes too long. The size is OK but I will recommend to attach it to something being so small is likely to be lost very easy.

The portability of the flash drive is great. But once the tiny loop breaks, its just a matter of time before the flash drive becomes missing and never found.
don't waste the $10-15 i did to get this if you think it's a cheap way to possibly get some extra storage. way too slow to run any iphoto or itunes library.

reviewText: This simply has to be the worst product that Sandisk has released. I needed a some extra GB since I switched to a smaller SSD drive. The Cruzer seems to work well. It is easy to leave in my Ultrabook. The only problem is that when I do need to take it out, it is a little hard to remove since in does not hang out very far.

reviewText: I love this little thing. I use it where space is an issue and a semi=-permenant installation is prefered. Inexpensive.

reviewText: Yes, there is always a 'but'. I bought 3 of these drives mainly because I was getting tired of using external hard drives that required their own power supply, and like the idea of a portable, USB powered backup.I've had WD drives before and not experienced any issues with them (I've got a couple of their 'powered' drives). But these little buggers have been frustrating!ALL 3 WORK independently. No issues there. The trouble begins when you try to daisy chain and use more than one at a time! A single 2TB drive was not going to be enough, so the plan was to link these together using a powered hub.My system: HP 19" laptop, running windows 7, 64 bit. 4 GB RAMHow I prepared and set up the drives:1 - The drives are ready to go out of the box. The cables that come with them are PATHETICALLY SHORT. About a foot long.2 - For each drive, I plugged them in one at a time and went into the properties to give them a unique drive name as to not confuse the computer, and keep them straight in windows explorer. To keep it easy, I named them "My Passport 1", "My Passport 2", and "My Passport 3". (I get the same problem I am about to describe if I have spaces in the name, or not)3 - To link them together, I made use of the following:a - HDE 2 Port USB 3.0 54mm Express CardB0046XUMDWb - Anker USB 3.0 7-Port Hub with 36W Power AdapterB006TT91TWc - AmazonBasics USB 3.0 A-Male to A-Female Extension CableB008EQYRRY4 - I tested the cable (3c Above) first by plugging each drive into the female end, and the male end into the express card (3a above). the drive spun up, computer recognized it with no issues. All 3 drives checked out OK.5 - I then tested the powered hub (3b above). Plugged it into the Express Card (3a above) directly, the other end into an outlet. I plugged in each drive one at a time (tested individually)... no issues. all drives recognized.6 - next, I tested the hub WITH the cable. I plugged the cable (3c) into the express card (3a), then the Hub (3b) into the cable (3c), AC adapter into the outlet. The PC recognized the hub with no issues.This is where it gets puzzling:7 - I plugged "My Passport 1" into the Hub (3b). Little blue light on the hub came on. The hard drive started to flicker, computer made the 'discovery' sound, and windows explorer opened showing the new drive, and it appeared as 'My Passport 1" in the directory tree. could access the drive with no issues.8 - I plugged "My Passport 2" into the Hub (3b). Little blue light on the hub came on. The hard drive started to flicker, computer made the 'discovery' sound, and windows explorer opened showing the new drive, and it appeared as 'My Passport 2" in the directory tree. could access the drive with no issues.9 - I plugged "My Passport 3" into the Hub (3b). Little blue light on the hub came on. The hard drive started to flicker, computer made the 'discovery' sound, AND THAT WAS IT. windows explorer would not see the 3rd drive, yet the computer must, because you get the audio tone as you did with the first 2. I clicked on the properties for the drivers; on 'manage'; checked in 'device manager' - no way on earth to get to the 3rd drive. yet you can pick it up and feel it is running.I installed the software that came with the hub, rebooted after installing each drive, nothing seems to work.10 - I ruled out a bad drive by repeating the procedures above, but changing the order of the drives being connected to the hub. I started with 'my passport 3' - fired up, recognized no problems (yet in #9 - the computer would see it based on the sound, but that was it). plugged in 'my passport 1'. it also fired up, computer recognized - windows explorer opened - good to go. plugged 'my passport 2' into the hub, behavior was similar to #9.things I have not tried yet: 2 drives in the Express card and one drive into the onboard USB2 port, but what sense would THAT make? all 3 USB 3.0 drives will boot individually with the hub, but no more than 2 of them.ANYONE else had this problem or have a solution? you should be able to plug all 3 drives into the 7 port hub with no issues. I can plug 2 drives into the hub, and then plug an older USB 2.0 drive into the hub, 2 thumbnail drives - all work in harmony. but 3 WD 2TB drives? haven't figured that one out yet

reviewText: I recently purchased this drive and was so disappointed with its performance. I had purchase a MY Essential Passport 1TB 2 months prior and expected the same kind of performance. A 1 hour backup on the older drive was taking more than 8 hours on this drive. I stopped the backup and I ran Atto benchmark on this drive. Out the box and it was rate at 25-30 MB/s which is USB 2.0 speed.I Have a My Essentials Passport (which is also USB 3). So I took the cable from that drive and ran the benchmark, it read/wrote at 115-120 MB/s which is what I expected in terms of performance from this drive; its very close to eSata speeds with the proper cable. I changed USB 3 ports and saw no change in performance. I reattached the original cable provided and the speed went to USB 2.I contacted WD technical support and was told that I had a defective cable and that I would receive one in 4-5 days. When I got back from vacation the cable had arrived and I ran the ATTo benchmark against the drive. Initially it was performing properly, but when it got to the 1024 test it failed. From that point on this drive with the new cable performed at 25-35 MB/s. I called support again, told them their cable does not support the drive. Yet if I put the working cable from the other drive in either USB 3 port, the drive worked great.I was told by the support person I spoke to at WD that they would overnight a new cable and that it would arrive by Tuesday. As it's now Thursday and a new cable has not arrived I can only surmise that these cables are defective and not USB 3 rated. I have spoken to tech support twice and have been told that the cables on it's way. I finally convinced them to give me a tracking number. Well the status says it hasn't been picked up.Now if you have a cable problem fess up and give a date-certain as to the delivery? I tire of calling and getting the same answer. It's all about the cable with this item, if you got it (the proper USB 3 Cable) you can expect the performance gains, because I see them. I just have to remove the cable from my other drive to see it.

reviewText: I exercised this little drive pretty hard and it performed. Here is what I did:I used my Apple iMac to test the drive. This computer only offers USB 2.0, so that is what I used. I used this drive as a Time Machine backup device, with data encryption. Unless you are an Apple user, that won't mean much to you. But this is relevant to any customer: Using the drive for the first time kept it writing, without interruption, for 48 hours straight. Apple's software wrote data to every available spot on the disk drive. When you have 2 terabytes of spots to write, it takes about two days. I kept the drive connected for another 12 hours too. During that time, the Time Machine software wrote a modest amount of data to the drive, once per hour.No problems! I also tested the physical cable connection of this drive. This is a particular area of concern to me, because I know of several portable disk drives that have faulty connectors, which renders the entire drive useless. One of these faulty drives was a Western Digital 1 terabyte drive. However, this particular drive was great! I used the USB 3.0 cable that ships with the drive. With my finger, I tapped the cable end, near the disk drive. I (gently) picked up the drive and dropped it about half an inch. I did all this while the disk drive was busy writing data. No problem! These little drives can also accept a micro USB 2.0 cable, and I repeated these tests using just such a cable. Again, no problem.There are not very many 2 terabyte drives of this size on the market. It is therefore not surprising that you will pay a bit of a premium for this one, where the premium is measured in dollars per megabyte. But this premium is not unreasonable. I must say, I am really impressed by this drive. So many bytes, yet so small!I have several other portable drives that I can compare to this one. For appearance and apparent quality, I like the Toshibas best. Second place goes to Buffalo Technology. The Western Digital drives look just a bit too plasticky to my eyes. I was concerned that all that plastic might cause the drive to overheat and fail. But I did run it for two and a half days, and it never got more than slightly warm. Again, I am really impressed.

reviewText: I have an older (2008) Lenovo Laptop that I really like and it runs beautifully. I am not ready to give it up. I take a lot of photos and the hard drive is getting pretty full. I bought theWestern Digital My Passport 1 TB USB 3.0 Portable Hard Drive - WDBBEP0010BBK-NESN (Black)to archive photos and other older files. The laptop only has 2 USB ports, so I have a 4-port hub plugged into one. It had a pair of external speakers and a mouse antenna plugged into two of the ports. The moment I plugged the My Passport drive into a third port, both the speakers and the wireless mouse went dead. Apparently the drive requires a dedicated port and/or hogs all the power. After the warranty expired the passport stop working on my MacBook. The warranty expired on Sept. 30th, 2013 and the Passport stopped working on October 13, 2013 and I am being told that there is nothing they can do about it. I have to suck it up I guess. Will not shop WD any more.

Now, it's not recognizable by my laptop or home PC. Amazon wouldn't refund the money after 34 days and I now have to jump through hoops to get a replacement from WD. Garbage... Can't even get a simple External Hard Drive right. Used it twice, by the way. Added some music and movies the first time. Removed some movies and added others the second. Third go around it was unrecognizable.

Overall, I guess this drive does what I need it to do. Use it to backup my PCs data files. Works fine and the hardware encryption, which I understand is good, is important. But... The first one I bought failed. Started a backup and it died. Exchanged it for a new one. Wasn't happy about having some of my data on it, which I couldn't wipe before I returned it. I have two now, and they work fine. Faster than my old 2.0 drives, but not rocket-fast like the advertising implies. Don't like the backup software that came with it; after the initial full backup, it just backs up changes. And it assumes it'll always be hooked-up to the PC. Sure I'm worried about my PCs hard drive crashing, but what if the house burns down. I keep two backups; one offsite. Anyway, tested the backup software a few times; didn't like the results; don't trust it. Same is true with Windows Backup. I just copy files instead. One thing really disappoints me; the drive won't unmount ("safely remove"). Read that a lot of people have this problem. Like them, I also asked Western Digital about it. Clearly it's a problem with their drive, but they won't admit it; they just have you jump through pointless fixes. That said, I just make sure the drive's finished before I disconnect it and that seems to work fine. Had I already not bought the first one, which led me to buy a second one, I would have chosen another brand or at least a different model.

None of my computers would recognize it. reviewText: I got one of these for my wife to replace her prior WD passport which just died the other day. the price was definitely right on this one. it seems to work fine. she uses it for time machine backups. the only thing I do not like is that they have changed the plug adapter that fits into the HD so old cables we have no longer will fit this particular HD.

The drive looks nice, and if you believe the marketing hype, the answer to your prayers. The cold reality is that the "SmartWare" software on this drive is absolutely terrible and more than takes away from any positives about this drive. It's also not easily removable because some of it is built into the drive's firmware!CrystalDiskMark shows it reads 80.93MB/s and writes 79.81MB/s. Not bad, but a Seagate 1TB Expansion drive I have gets closer to 90MB/s on both read and write.After installing their SmartWare software, everything on the drive - plus that of any other external USB hard drives - vanished. All the backups I had on my Seagate drive disappeared. Only after uninstalling their software did this go away. Trying to use this software caused my quad-core system to go to 100% (after about 15 minutes and just 36GB) and made the system nearly unresponsive. I never have that problem with Acronis TrueImage going out the same USB 3.0 PCI-Express card to different drives. Tried it a second time after a cold reboot, and the same thing happened.You'd think you can just reformat the drive and be done with their software, but no. Since it's part of the drive's firmware, there's a utility you have to download in order to disable it. This didn't work on multiple Windows 7 64-bit systems, whether using USB 3.0 or 2.0. So this drive is nothing more than a paperweight to me.Do yourself a favor and look at other WD drives that don't have their "SmartWare" software, or pick up a different brand such as Seagate. Don't take my word for it - just search around the Internet and you'll find all kinds of horror stories about this drive, and most of them say roughly the same thing.
