reviewText: The Western Digital 2TB Passport portable hard drive disappointed me with write speeds of only 80-100 MB/s with 20-30GB size files. I have seen reviews showing 50% more speed. It has a simple white LED on the cable connection side to indicate power and read/write. The device has a USB 3.0 only connection on it.

The reason is that internally, this drive has no SATA interface. It's strictly USB 3.0, hard wired to the drive. Why is this a problem? Well, I've had two of these 2TB drives and they both have wonky USB interfaces. Very temperamental, one stopped working completely, the other connects only intermittently, if the stars align and you hold your tongue just so. The data is fine, it's still all on the drive, and the disk drive itself seems perfectly fine, when it deigns to connect. But it just doesn't like to connect over USB. Google it - lots of people have trouble with these drives USB interface. I thought it was the cable for a while. Now, pretty sure that's not the problem.Now, this is not an unusual problem, and in the event, on a drive that had a SATA interface with a simple USB interface plugged into it inside the case, you could take apart the drive and do something else. You could get a cheap USB housing with its own new SATA-USB board. You could just plug it into you computer's SATA cable. You could get one of those little dongle thingy hot plug usb adapters. In short, you could still make use of the drive and access your data.But no. WD not only stuck a crummy wonky USB interface on the things, they hard soldered it to the drive so that if and when it goes, the drive is useless. (You can actually have them fixed it seems, but it's an ordeal and cost about as much as a new drive.)If I get another USB drive, I will make sure someone has taken one apart and it has a normal SATA interface inside. I've read the Toshiba Canvio Basic is this way, but not sure.I will not EVER buy another WD usb drive, that much is for dang sure.
summary: Very very practical reason not to buy one of these drives.

Despite this product being advertised as Windows 8 Compatible, it does NOT support the new Windows 8 Storage Spaces technology. One other reviewer here reported the same problem, but I only found his review after I had received and unsuccessfully tried my 4 new 2TB drives. I called WD tech-support, and I was very happy with the way they handled the call, but unfortunately they confirmed in the end, that these drives won't work in a Storage Pool.The DO work perfectly in Windows 8 for normal use, though. Disk Management sees them as any other drive, they format just fine and out of the 4 drives I ordered, none were DOA. So, overall, this is a great drive, if you don't want to combine multiple ones of them into a single drive using Storage Spaces.In HDTune, the drives were able to hammer out around 100MB/s, if used with no more than 2 drives simultaneously on the same hub. With 4 drives on one USB 3.0 hub, I got about 53MB/s each when benchmarking them all at the same time.Aside:I did find a way to run the drives as a single drive in RAID mode in the end, but for this, I had to install the free VMware Player (VirtualBox has much worse I/O performance) and set up a virtual Debian Linux system, pass the 4 drives to it, put them into a RAID 5 using mdadm, and share this drive back to the Windows 8 System using Samba. It's definitely a hack and nowhere near as convenient as the Storage Spaces would have been, but it has two big other advantages, also:1. The performance is stellar! Supposedly Parity Mode for Storage Spaces is very slow.2. I get more space, since the Storage Spaces' Parity Mode always inflates the data by 50%, no matter how many drives you have, whereas a Linux RAID 5 only uses the space of 1 drive for redundancy. So, with Linux I get a 6TB drive out of my 4 2TB Passports, whereas Storage Spaces (should it have worked) would only have given me 5.33TB. This discrepancy gets bigger the more drives you have: For 10 drives, for example, you get 18TB from Linux vs. 13.33TB from Windows.
summary: Caution: Does NOT work with Windows 8 Storage Spaces!

reviewText: I bought this drive and the external enclosureWestern Digital WD Nomad Rugged Casefor use with my Retina MBP. The WD site stated that the case was not compatible with the 2TB model, so I was planning to modify it so it would accept this drive. To my surprise, the case has two removable spacers with some rubber fingers on them. You can snap out the spacers and re-apply the rubber fingers, over the location where the spacers were installed. The drive will fit in the case and close with minimal effort. It does not feel like you are forcing it and if it were any easier to close, the drive would be lose and I would be concerned it would bounce around if it were to fall.I wanted a USB 3 drive that was self powered and portable. I have about 15 WD caviar green and black drives in several NAS, eSATA towers, servers and toasters. For the most part I have been happy with WD drives. My only bad experience was a batch of WDEADS20 drives that I bought near the end of the life cycle, due to a compatibility issue my thecus NAS had wit the newer WDEARS drives. Within about 18 months from purchase, 3 of the 5 drives failed to the point the NAS would not use them. I was able to get them replaced with minimum hassle from WD and have continued to be a customer. I have also had over 20 years of good experience with WD drives and recently pulled out a storage bin of about 20 old USB drives ranging in age of 5 to 10 years. Some of the drives had not been started in years and I was able to read them all.I am planning to run virtual machines from this drive since the HD in my new RMBP is only 256GB. I had a couple virtual machines running in fusion on my early 2008 MBP. I had upgrade the internal drive to a 500GB momentus XT that averages 75MB/S write and 95MB/S read. This drive is averaging about 77MB/S on both the read and write speed so I am down a little on the disk I/O, compared to the internal drive of my old MBP. However, I think the net disk I/O may be slightly better since there will be less disk contention having the VMs and the host share the same drive. I only have my Bootcamp image setup in fusion and since it is running on the internal SSD, I can't comment on the real world performance of this drive for running VMs. I will try to post an update after I have a chance to run a couple VMs from this drive.If you are looking for the fastest USB drive, stick with SSD. You can get a faster USB 3 spinning drive if you go up to a 7200 RPM drive, but those will require a power supply and will not be as portable as this one.Why four stars you may ask. I guess I was a little disappointed that the drive was not a little faster. a 1.5TB WD scorpio blue has a transfer rate of 83MB/sec. The 2TB My Passport has more density which should equate to a better transfer rate all things remaining the same.

I am updating my review below. The drive stopped working all of a sudden and I lost all my data. My computer stopped recognizing the drive and it makes an intermittent beeping sound when you plug it in. I have tried plugging it on another computer, and the same issue persists. Quiet sad that I lost all my data. My wife's WD hard drive also stopped working a few months before mine.I love this hard drive, Great capacity, very quiet and does't get hot. Its quite compact for its capacity and I have had no issues using it so far. I also bought a Western Digital for my Wife and hers works well too so I guess they make good products.

reviewText: Pros: Good Storage, easy to set up and very compact and light but well builtCons: A little expensive, USB 3.0 but not as fast, may be that's how USB 3 generally is. Too many software updates for WD software that comes with the disk to manage it. You can certainly skip the software.

The drive connects to a USB 3 port and runs at SATA II speeds (max 3 gps).For the record, SATA II (technically SATA revision 2.0) has a max of 3 Gbit/sec which equates to 384 MB/sec.USB 3 can handle a max of 5 Gbits/sec, which equates to 640 MB/secI'll bet the hard disk inside this device is a SATA II disk for two reasons:1) It's darned hard to find a 2.5" size harddisk that operates at SATA III (6gps);2) This device operates at the same speeds as another device I have that comprises a SATA II disk and a USB 3 to SATA IIenclosure. Doing 60 GigaByte file ops, the avg speed is roughly 3 gps3 Gbit/sec with both devices.So this drive is not bad. It does indeed connect to USB 3. It is indeed 3 times faster when connected to USB 3 than when it's connected to USB 2. But when connected to USB 3 it does not yield USB 3 speeds of 5 gps. On USB 3, it does allow SATA II speeds, which are faster than USB 2 because USB 2 chokes SATA II.So we're not being lied to, but one can easily be misled. But we are used to being misled by harddisk manufacturers--It's how big?

The only way to stop it is to unplug it or shut the computer off. (Computer in sleep still powers the USB port so the drive runs.)2. I noticed that when scheduled backups were supposed to be done, the lights were not indicating activity. I checked the WD SmartWare and it said a backup had been performed. After several days of this, my suspicion led me to compare the files and size of the backup to my computer library. The backup was way short. Since the settings specified saving 5 versions of each file the backup should have been much larger. I did a manual backup. About 10 seconds later it said the backup was complete. I had added 3 files, but the backup size was still well short of what it should have been.3. Next I retrieved some frequently used files. Only 2 versions had been saved although the settings specified 5 versions. I retrieved them to find that they had not been backed up in over a week. And only twice in 3 weeks. reviewText: Western Digital My Passport 1 TB USB 3.0 Portable Hard Drive - WDBBEP0010BBK-NESN (Blue)Almost idiot proof. After fighting a "Less than 2 Step" backup system with it's repeated failures & replacement units DOA I decided to bite the bullet. I had previously purchased a smaller WD Passport for picture/music backup 5 years before & it still functions perfectly. Yesterday the new HD arrived. Yes it's case is plastic but well made. Hell the one I bought 5 years ago is plastic also. Not a problem. This unit is smaller than the 120 GB unit I already owned. Fresh out of the box I connected it to my HP laptop and using, 3rd party, free imaging backup software I completed a 254 GB backup in slightly under 2 hours. Mind you this was a full backup. Future backups likely will require less than 15 minutes. Much to-do has been made about the WD supplied cable. I had no problems but am going to purchase an aftermarket high end cable as a safety measure. These are available for less than 7 bucks. Note I used third party software. I did this because it has been my experience WD's software is their weakest link. Just my opinion and I know people who swear by WD's software FWIW. I just prefer other available programs.

I am very happy with my passport. It is very compact and convenient, works great. I love that I don't have to have this somewhere but can just store it out of the way. It is convenient that it just plugs into the usb for power too.

The usb cable included with WD Passport is faulty. Even though it supports the USB 3.0 speeds, when I try to move over large files sizes (2GB+ per video file), the WD passport crashes and I end up with a corrupted file and a semi-faulty drive.The Drive I bought is the 2TB version. And the RPM is a consumer standard, meager 5400 RPM. Then again, you get what you pay for, so the price is decent.I have tested this with a third-party USB 3.0 cable and the transfer moves over successfully without any hiccups.I wish they just included a Y-Cable that has a USB 3.0 for transfer and a USB 2.0 for power. The reason for this is because I tried this with a powered ANKER USB 3.0 hub and the data transfer still fails.Not long after, the WD drive ended up corrupted/inaccessible even from a third-party USB 3.0 cable so I tried to format it. The drive became faulty after the format and would not be recognized.The product is beautiful, but if it doesn't work, there's no need to buy from WD when there are many competitors out there with cheaper or faster external HDD's.I would like to thank Amazon for fantastic customer service in refunding me my purchase.I would NOT recommend this product to others until they replace the standard ~5" USB 3.0 cable with a Y-cable.
summary: The usb cable included with WD Passport is faulty.

And I only get a day or two of use for the Fire, more power-hungry than the regular black and white Kindle, which I can use, even with speakers, for about a week before recharging.Good points: You can get a version with a set of adapter plugs and use it overseas. If that's what you want, don't get this one, getKindle PowerFast International Charging Kit (for accelerated charging in over 200 countries, also compatible with other android and iOs devices)because you get the same fast charger plus all the plugs you need for various countries.It is faster than the small standard USB charger--a lot faster. But the PRICE....really?Bad Points:As I mentioned, I think it's pricey.AND...the Kindle Fire (I have the next-gen, not-HD version) has some kind of plug issues that mean sometimes it will connect with the charger and sometimes you come back and it's disconnected and sitting there twiddling its thumbs and not charging at all. You have to fiddle with the plug into the socket to make sure it's connected, and even then, it doesn't always want to obey. This is a Kindle Fire issue, but I mention it because this charger doesn't make it charge any better, if that is your issue. FYI.The PowerFast charges at 9W (standard USB is 5W --the wattage is the POWER being pushed to your Kindle. More wattage, faster charging, like pressure in a garden hose.) Power increases by squares, so since 9 watts is 1.8 times as much as 5 watts, if you multiply 1.8 by 1.8, the square is 3.24, thus the PowerFast is 3 times as fast as charging with USB.HOWEVER, the Fires will charge at either 9 OR 5 Watts, but the Kindle E-Readers such as the Keyboard or Touch that are B&W; and not backlit, will only charge at 5 Watts, meaning, this won't speed you up for the black and white readers--they restrict the power down to 5 Watts, meaning no matter how fast you push the charge at the E-Readers, they won't take it up any faster. But...they charge pretty quickly as it is.I called Amazon, and they told me that these power supplies are "wide-ranging power units" meaning, they can be plugged into a 220 volt socket (with an adapter to fit the type of outlet on the plug) and not need a step-down transformer to reduce the voltage to 110. So if you have a plug adapter to fit into the different conformation of various European and UK sockets, you can simply plug in and charge if you are outside the United States.While not essential, this makes keeping the Kindle charged up a lot easier, and becausethe Fire runs down faster than my b&w; Kindle Keyboard, so if you use your Kindle a lot, you probably will find you want faster charging. That's what I found. It doesn't seem to be exactly 3X as fast, but it is faster than charging off my USB port on my PC.

reviewText: I realize that this is half-price with a Fire order, but even at that cost point, and certainly at full price, I'd recommend you look elsewhere.Continuing with the Kindle Fire HD theme of "why in the world did they put the cable port there" - the starring act of which is the inclusion of the charging port on the left ("bottom" in landscape mode) side of the Fire HD - this adapter not only is big enough that it will potentially block other outlets by itself, but the cable comes out of the bottom side of it, meaning that it might block multiple outlets on a power strip as well.There are numerous ~10W adapters which will not block other outlets and which have the cable coming "out" of the outlet, so as not to block things. For this price - half off and certainly full price - you can find one with the same or better power specs, likely with two ports (for charging one 10W device or two lower-power devices), which also has a folding plug (such as theIPAD-2USB), and which won't block outlets.Yes, the box it comes in is very well-designed, almost Apple-like. Yes, the fit and finish are nice. Yes, if you have plenty of outlet space and don't want a 10W adapter (this one is only 9W, which will be an issue with some devices that want 10W), this will work for you. For me, if they'd have moved the plug from the "bottom" to a "side", most of my issues would go away, at least at half price. At full price? This isn't worth it.

reviewText: The PowerFast does re-charge the Kindle Fire in a very short time. It charges the Kindle Fire much faster than charging it through a computer using the USB cord.

The Kindle Fire HD "fast" charger is a required item for those who purchased the 8.9" HD Kindle Fire and want a speedier charge time. Before purchasing it, there are few things to keep in mind.The HD Kindle Fire does come with charging capability through the USB cable supplied with the Kindle. Using the USB cable connected to a computer, it will take up to 13-1/2 hours to charge. What makes the charger you're looking at "fast" is it charges at a higher amperage than that of a USB connection charge through a computer. The "fast" charger will charge your Kindle in about four hoursIf you've upgraded from the older Kindle Fire and still have that charger, you can use it instead of buying this one. The older charger is rated at 5v, 1.8A and will work fine with the new Kindle. Your charging time will be about the same as the "fast" charger. In fact, any charger rated at 5v and capable of delivering 1.8A or more will work fine as long as it terminates with a micro-B USB connector. Purchase this charger if 1) you don't have a charger and want to charge your HD Kindle Fire at a faster rate and/or 2) you want a spare charger in case your old one fails.One of the drawbacks of the new HD Kindle Fire is there is no way to tell the current charging state. The new charger doesn't come with an LED indicating when the charge is complete and the power button on the new HD Kindle Fire doesn't illuminate and change color when fully charged (this was a feature of the old Kindle Fire that was lost with the new one). There is an app that will tell you how full your battery is while charging. Search for and download an app called "Battery HD" from the Amazon Apps for Android store. There are two versions of the app, the standard for free and the Pro version for $2. This app will show you the exact charge state of your battery while it is charging.The charger sold here is only the plug-in wall charger, sans cable. The USB cable supplied with your Kindle Fire when you purchased it is inserted into it. In fact, any USB 2.0 cable with a micro-B connector can be used. As stated, the charger does not come with an LED indicator. It has a square form factor with the plug prongs not centered, so when plugging it into an outlet, it may block the adjacent outlet in a two-outlet receptacle. In this situation, plug it in upside down to accommodate the adjacent plug.It's pretty obvious that Amazon is seeking added revenue by requiring user's to purchase the "fast" charger separately. The best time to purchase the charger is during an Amazon promotion. I was able to secure one for 50% off the regular price, but that was a one-day promotion and who knows when that price will be revisited.If you're ambitious, seek out a third-party charger that meets the specs for this charger (5v, 9W, 1.8A minimum, terminating in a micro-B USB connector). Otherwise, do what most people do and purchase the "fast" charger and be done with it. The increase in charging time is well worth the price of the charger.

About me:I have a Macbook pro running Mac os and win 7A first gen Xoom tablet which I still sorta love due to the internal and sd card storage space.An Iphone 4.First Gen. NookWhy I chose the Kindle Fire HD:1. Storage, storage! I wanted a small tablet I could travel with that would keep a big chunk of my movies and books stored, so I wouldn't need to worry about wifi. This shouldn't be as big of a problem as it is, but between flights and family without wifi, it's turned into an issue for me.2. Amazon ecosystem. I buy lots of video from Amazon that I stream on a rokyu. I love that I can download those to keep on my FireHD for offline viewing when I travel. I love how easy it is to access my wishlist and to buy books and videos. I love that I can easily stream Prime videos. The automatic cloud storage and streaming of Amazon content is a nice extra, too.3. Books. I have a Prime Membership, and all those free books listed with Prime were taunting me. There's no getting them unless they're downloaded with an actual Kindle. There is also a lending program which is a nice bonus.4. The new whispersync. I'm an Audible addict, and I thought that was a pretty cool concept. I haven't tried it out yet, but hey, it's there and waiting for me.5. It has all the necessary video apps/abilities: Hulu, Netflix, HBOgo, and of course, Amazon.So far I'm glad I got the FireHD. It turns out that Amazon Instant Videos take up less space than I'd anticipated. So far, I've been able to fit 57 episodes of various TV shows, one movie, and 8 books onto 14 gigs of storage. Not bad at all.What IS bad is that the video portion of my downloads can't be backed up. There doesn't seem to be a way to access where they're stored on the Kindle so that I can move them onto my storage drive. This means that I'll have to delete, download other videos, delete, and redownload if I want to switch my stored videos around. This is wasting my bandwidth and time and was almost a deal breaker.There is a bit of lag online, but nothing too annoying. Websites come up quickly, and the wifi is quick and stable during downloads.I'm sick to bloody death of the Ad. Not ads, *AD*. I honestly wouldn't mind seeing deals and bargains when I come out of sleep mode, but for the love of commerce, show me something besides that bleepin' Discover ad!The screen is very nice, but not as beautiful as people are saying. Or maybe I was just expecting too much. Detail in dark scenes can be difficult to see, and the glare is pretty awful, though better than on my Xoom.The battery life is horrifically bad. Seriously. In the last 20 minutes, 5% has been sucked away just sitting and having the device storage space checked. One hour of video uses about 30%. Using pretty much any function will kill it fast. However, the battery doesn't drain if left alone over night.So, to sum it up, if you are part of Amazon's ecosystem, I see the FireHD as the best choice available. It's a nice little tablet with decent storage and good video capability. However, if I wasn't a Prime member and if I didn't purchase Amazon's instant videos, I would choose something else.**Update 11-6-12**After using the Kindle Fire HD for awhile, I would give it 3.5 stars if I could. The things I love about it have remained great, but some problems have come up.1. Odor. When the device heats up, there is a strong outgassing odor. This is a separate issue from Amazon's "leather" case, which I had to remove due to fumes. The device is much, much worse than my Xoom and its case ever were. I'm wondering if it's a byproduct of the antiglare lamination on the screen? Granted, I'm sensitive to odors, but many people are, and this is something to consider. 13 days of use, and the smell is still very bad.2. Silk browser. I finally see what people are complaining about on the lag. Some websites are fine, but some aren't. It seems to depend on the types of ads used on the site. For instance, the Dead Island wiki is completely unbrowsable on Silk. I went over to XDA Developers and got Dolphin and Flash links that work wonderfully on the Kindle Fire HD. There is still a bit of lag on heavily monetized sites, but they can definitely be browsed without too much trouble. However, I shouldn't have to waste my time hunting down a link to make my device work online. Amazon should give us a browser that works and/or provide Dolphin for download in their app store. They have chosen to do neither.3. Device lag. Occasionally the device will freeze up for a second or two when browsing libraries, favorites, apps, etc.4. The sound stops working after being disconnected from HDMI output to T.V. Turning it off and on again gets the sound working. This is a minor annoyance, but it's adding to a growing list.5. Extreme heat. The Kindle Fire HD gets very hot during video applications. Since 70% of the reason I bought it was so I could conveniently take my Amazon video library with me, this is a concern.At this point, I'm still glad I purchased the Fire HD, but just barely. I buy so many instant videos through Amazon that it really is the best option for me. I just wish the odor, heating, and lag hadn't become such an issue.****Update 12-5-12...Downgraded my review to 3 stars. It should probably be more like 2.5.****I seem to be in a cycle of returns on my Kindle Fire HD. Mine has the backlight bleed issue which somehow only became obvious when I downloaded the Dark Knight app. The issue was camouflaged partly because Amazon highlights the top edge of the screen and put our kindle info across where the problem usually is.The bleed became glaring when I got my first game app, and it had lots of full screen black.Amazon CS was great as usual, and they sent me a new Kindle. The new one also has a backlight bleed issue and additionally drops wifi. In testing the new Fire HD, it dropped a streaming movie constantly. So, I put both units on my lap, and streamed with my old Fire HD with no issues. I watched the wifi icon on my new device (not streaming it, just watching the wifi connection), and it dropped wifi about 6xs within 5 mins or so. I'll be contacting Amazon for yet another return, but I'm feeling dubious.On another note, Dolphin has proven unstable over time. I've switched to Opera mobile which is generally more stable but not perfect or my first choice for a browser, if all were working equally well. The quest to find a reliable browser has become hugely annoying.So. I hate the glitches. I hate not having a stable browser. I hate the light bleed. I hate the heat. I hate the odor issue which by now is much better, but still slightly present when the unit heats up.I also hate that I've become so attached to this darn thing. The size, weight, and storage space are awesome. Still, if I didn't have such an extensive Amazon video library, I would have returned it and good riddance.
summary: A good choice IF you are a part of Amazon's ecosystem

Unless you're fully invested in the Amazon ecosystem, this isn't the tablet for you. It functions more as a storefront for Amazon than as a tablet. I bought the Google Nexus 7 instead and have been far happier with it.

First off - anyone who has an Amazon Prime account, and or reads Kindle books - you're going to be so happy with a Kindle Fire HD. All the video content that is available for FREE with your Prime account is at your fingertips. I have used other Android tablets (Motorola Xoom, Samsung Galaxy Tab 7.7, and Google Nexus 10). None of them allow you to watch Prime videos "out of the box" - you can get around it by installing some web browsers and then side-loading Adobe Flash - but it's not very reliable. On the Kindle Fire HD the video quality and the sound are great! All your Amazon apps are there .. all your Kindle books are there. No, the Google Play Store isn't available, and most (all?) Google-branded apps are not available. But you can still do a lot of things without any Google apps. And yes, you can get your Google Mail. It's very basic, but it does the job. And all my music is up on Amazon's cloud. I've purchased some MP3s from Amazon, but you can use the "importer" - it will scan your computer, and upload your music to the cloud - including the songs you got from iTunes.One thing to consider. Your experience will only be as good as your WiFi service. If you only have access to poor WiFi service you're going to have problems - with the Kindle Fire HD - as well as ANY WiFi only device. In the past year I've upgraded my internet service from basic speed to higher speeds. And I've gotten a dual-band WiFi router. So for me WiFi flies on the Kindle Fire HD.I wasn't sure before I ordered it if I should get it - and had even prepared myself to send it back after 48 hours. I'm glad I got it. Just wish I had waited a few days to order the 7" .. the day I received the 7" Amazon cut the prices of the 8.9". But, that's the way it is with electronics. All things considered - I'm happy I got it and it'll keep me occupied for a long time!PS .. I've seen some reviews who complain about the ads. Seriously? There's an ad on the lock screen - and you click on offers on the top menu. There's NO inconvenience whatsoever. If you don't want the ads just pay the extra $15-or-so bucks to get rid of them. But they're not in your face and they don't distract from the experience.And for a cover - I got the I-Blason cover - it's my 2nd one (I have one on my Nexus 10, too). It's well made, it's sturdy, and the fit is nice'n'snug so that your tablet doesn't move around. A great addition.Added 03/25/2013: For those of you who know how customizable the Android system is - you're probably going to be disappointed with the Kindle Fire HD. Unless you root it - there's virtually no customization you can do. I haven't, and don't plan on rooting mine. The home screen is the carousel - which is a slider showing the last apps/books/movies/music/etc that you've used. When it sits on my desk at work it would be boring to look over and see that all the time. So I got the TerraTime app and added it to my 'favorites' (that's the star the the bottom right corner of your screen. TerraTime is the earth which spins - and shows night time and day time around the globe. It has a lot of custom settings - and it spins so it's always moving. Kind of like "living wallpaper" for Android - but there is no actual living wallpaper for the Kindle Fire HD. It's simple, but it does the job of not having to look at the carousel all the time.
summary: I thought it was good before I ordered - it's even better than I thought!

reviewText: We bought one of these for the whole family (mom, dad, 5 year old and 7 year old) to use. So far the kids have used it the most.I set it up with the available "Free Time" app to limit the applications and content they have access to. It worked perfectly. I was able to set up a profile for each child and configure it exactly the way I wanted to. You can limit the books they see, the videos they see, and the games/applications they see. You can also set up time restrictions so for instance they can read books for an unlimited amount of time but only play games for an hour and watch videos for an hour. Also, I have it set up with password protection so if the kids happen to be playing a game with ads and they click the ad, they are prompted for the password instead of being brought to the ad site.My in-laws have the Nook and I don't know of any app that is comparable to "Free Time" to limit what the kids have access to.The only thing that could make the Kindle better is if you could install apps from the Google Play store instead of just the Amazon App store.One thing to note is that I had a little trouble getting the Kindle to recognize my Gmail account. I kept entering the correct email address and password but it kept telling me that the email or password was wrong. I finally read another review that told me I needed to enable IMAP on my Gmail account. Even after I did that, I still couldn't connect. The secret was that I have two-step verification turned on, so Gmail needs an application-specific password. However, the error message didn't specify this, it just kept saying the password was wrong. Once I generated an application-specific password and plugged it in, my Gmail connected flawlessly. I still don't know how to sync my contacts and calendar, but I'm just happy to have my email working for now.I would definitely recommend the Kindle Fire HD as a family-friendly device.

It was also during this call that I learned that I had the previous generation (2012) device which I was not informed of when I purchased the unit. However, it was now early December and like many people I am extremely busy so I knew I would not have much time to use it until after Christmas. On December 28th I plugged the unit in to charge, 4 hours later it still did not have enough of a charge to power up; 14 hours later it had maybe 25% of a charge and another charger had overheated. I did a factory reset and called customer service. I explained that this was the second unit that I have had that had this issue and that I really did not want it replaced with the same model. I was told that I had two options: engineering could look into the issue, which could take 24-48 hours and possible fix it or it could be replaced with the same model. I could not get my money back and they would not give me any credit to purchase another model.Other issues that I've with both units that I have received is that despite the information on the product page, you cannot use the item while it is charging. If the battery is too low, it acts crazy and the battery rapidly depletes. When the battery level is higher and you try to use it the battery level continues to decrease even when the unit is plugged in to an AC outlet. I have never got to use the unit anywhere near length of time that there technical information says you can before it needs to be charged; even following all the tips to increase battery time. I've never had one charge as quickly as the Amazon technical info says it will. I understand why they now have a MAYDAY Button on the new units!To say that I am upset and angry is an understatement. I have burnt up $60.00 of Amazon chargers that have not been replaced, 2 OEM chargers, and spent hours on the computer and the phone on a device that is unsatisfactory. I feel that Amazon knows that there are issues with this model and they are just trying to ride out the one year warranty period. Up until this point I have always felt that there customer service was the best, they really tried to make sure there customer was 100% satisfied but they have really let me down over this one issue.
summary: BUYERS BEWARE!!!! DISAPPOINTED, DISGUSTED AND TOTALLY DISSATISFIED WITH AMAZON'S SERVICE & THIS DEVICE (0 STARS)

reviewText: While the hardware is decent, there are a few things that I don't like which made me choose the Nexus 7 over this.1) Lack of Google Play Apps. reviewText: Bought this for my x'mas gift. After over a month of using it, I love it even thought it has its limitations, but it servers me well as a mobile media center.This is my 1st tablet and 1st Kindle, so I don't have any experience to compare with other tablet nor different version of Kindle. Anyway, I like what I got even though it has some bugs that will explain more as follows.Bugs:1) sync with Facebook, e-mail, contacts, & calendars - except e-mail, all the rest aren't able to sync together. I have tried few times, it keeps asking me to set up an e-mail account, which I did. I have checked Kindle supports to see if I set them up properly, however, the steps it shows are the same as what I did. Therefore, I can't use contacts & calendars on Kindle, but I have those on my cell phone ... For the Facebook, I can use it from "web" instead, so it takes me few more clicks, but it's okay. These bugs may be good for me, at least, I don't want to too attach to Amazon, especially my personal stuff in calendars / friends & families' contacts ... etc. So, they don't brother me much!2) Kindle doesn't like hand sanitizer on the fingers, it will freeze screen or react crazily. I have read my Kindle at the gym, but every time when I use sanitizer on my hands, or spray tiny of them on the paper towel to wipe the machine that I gonna work on. My fingers aren't wet either, but a tiny coat of sanitizer. My kindle doesn't like it at all, and it works improperly; it won't response to my fingers or freeze screen even I turn it off and turn back on ... Now, I have to use the sanitizer after working out the machine, then I don't have any problem of using my Kindle during the gym session.Additionally, it freezes the screen or doesn't have any response to my cold fingers (without any sanitizer on). What I do is rubbing my hands to get warmer, and it does have normal response afterwards.Like:1) the build is solid; cool looking, decent weight and size on the go. I put an anti-glare screen protector, which protect the screen not only from scratches but also from the dusts and fingerprints. It does a great job on reducing screen glare for light reflections or even under sun light.2) Crispy HD screen, brilliant color resolution, and stereo sounds are great quality. I'm impressed by this little guy. Its sounds beautiful whether on headphone or its built-in speakers. It's a joy to play with this guy for watching movies, listening songs, playing games, or reading books/magazines. Prime members can take advantages of watching free movies / tv shows / lending book s. I bought the HDMI cable to connect it with my projector, the streaming movies and tv shows run smoothly. I don't feel any delay or what so ever. Only one time, so far, Amazon server was down, and I couldn't watch anything at that night.3) my Kindle save me from isolating to this addictive online world when my MBP died recently. Likely, I had it on hands to do my normal things: checking emails, facebooking, & surfing the web. I was distress free on the period of the "technical disaster".4) Kindle becomes my best friend now, it comes with me all the time wherever I go. I have used it as a showcase to show my art pieces, current work, and resume. It works like a charm for JPG and normal PDF without any multimedia features, so it doesn't response to those videos or interactive buttons on the PDF. I'm a bit disappointed about that last time the Kindle can't show my portfolio pdf properly on an interview. It can be fixed by saving those videos separately thought.5) Reading with my Kindle is awesome. Specially, night time, I can turn the light to the level that my eyes won't feel tire but the light also won't affect my husband's sleeping. Now, I don't have to bring physical book to commute, and my Kindle can have few books that I want to read at the same time. I can also read the kindle books on both Kindle and my Mac, which is really convenience that I can do cut & paste whatever I need to another doc for references.6) Side-loaded dolphin browsers and flash player on Kindle, and I can watch youTube and any website using Flash player, including my own website. Before I was hesitated to buy Kindle because its limitation of using Flash Player, I spent quite some times to research that until I'm sure how I can watch Flash player on Kindle then I made the purchase.Dislike1) Camera - only front camera and it doesn't come with camera apps. Kindle should have came with apps for camera and cam-recorder, which is $1.99 on Kindle app store. It doesn't make sense to ask Kindle users to buy the app instead, regardless the app whether is good or not, so I won't buy it. Ended up, I spent some time on researching other camera apps that is for free. I think Amazon should free the hidden camera & cam-recorder features for all Kindle Fire HD users.Recommended Accessories:- screen protector: it only costs about $2 each, but it gives you worry free about the scratches, dust, and fingerprints; plus no maintenance of wiping off them every time of using Kindle.- case: I bought a leather-like case about $15, which is a great protection from scratches and slipping from the hands; some good ones can stand well for watching movies.- HDMI cable: if you want to watch the Kindle through big TV / projector- fast charger: highly recommended if you don't have any previous Kindle produce. I bought $10 one, which was used to be $20; It saves much time in charging.- auto charger: I just bought it few days ago for up-coming road trips. If you don't have fast charge, auto charger may be an option that you don't need to have both.Hope those help!

reviewText: I ended up upgrading to the HDX. I had nothing but problems with the Kindle Fire HD. I like the HDX much better.

Well, I really wanted the Kindle Fire HD because it has everything the Kindle Fire SD lacked. Even though I'm a Prime Member, I was too impatient to wait 2 days or 1 day shipping from Amazon, so I went to my local Best Buy to purchase the Kindle Fire HD. I was a little skeptical about the quality of KF HD. I was blown away when I started using the KF HD! The sound & picture quality is incredible! The buttons for volume and power are hard to feel but that became a non issue once I put the Amazon case on it. Everything on the KF HD works great. We use Skype on a weekly basis with no flaws. I love the IMDB integration on the KF HD (I've been referring to that website for several years).Kindle FreeTime wouldn't set up the correct way, so I contacted Amazon Support. I had to reset my KF HD in order for the FreeTime to set up parental controls. So, far FreeTime works great. My 3 year loves when he is on "His Kindle". I have my other 2 kids with their own profiles as well. The time limits allows them to have to share. Once their time is up, the kindle FreeTime locks them out and they tell me so I can activate the next child's profile. The Kindle FreeTime comes with set items that you can take off depending on your child's age or gender. My kids enjoy playing games that we play (where's my water, free flow; etc) and I added those games to each child's Free Time (which I already had on my account.) Keep in mind that once you deactivate your FreeTime, you do not have access to the set items unless you already have them on your account.I don't read books on my KF HD, I prefer to read books on my Kindle Ink Reader. I read daily for hours and love to get lost into a book. And the ink reader feels like a physical book. When reading on the web on the KF HD, I find myself zooming in to read.The only (personal) problem, is that I had to share my KF HD with my husband! Ummm...He took it all the time! I had to ask to use my own Kindle! I will be purchasing another KF HD for my kids.I am an Apple Girl (for 3 years) and a Amazon Fanatic >>(for 9 years now!) and I think that the KF HD is a solid, affordable tablet that is great for kids and adults. With that being said, I purchased the iPad Mini the day it was released and I love it! I love that all my apple products sync together. I had to put all my notes, reminders, lists; etc. that I had on my iPhone into the KF HD; which was more work then checking back between my devices to make sure I had everything. I prefer the iPad mini but that is just my personal taste. Both the KF HD and iPad mini are great devices just different depending on what you are using it for. If you are a business person, then I can tell you that the KF HD is not for you. Try other Tablets that will fit your needs.For the price, Kindle Fire HD is very affordable for those who are Budget Savvy. I don't like the whole Apple vs. Amazon's debate. Both are solid tablets and I love both Companies. I totally recommend the a Kindle Fire HD over those kid based learning devices that cost the same as the KF HD! The KF HD has everything those devices have and more! As a mom of 4 kids; ages 12 & under, I can tell you that kids will eventually get bored of those kid learning devices or out grow them. Kids will not have that problem with KF HD because there is unlimited learning available and it is displayed on a beautiful HD screen with vivid colors.

I purchased this for my wife, when her computer gave up the ghost. Let's get one point very clear: This is NOT a tablet computer, in the regular sense... With that stated, here are the pros and cons, from our perspective:Pros:Beautiful displayClear beautiful soundFast operationEasily connected to a WPA2 wireless (secured) networkCons:*Web browser will not interface with banking institution...In fairness, part of this lies in the fact that my bank has not written support for Amazon's browser. However, a browser needs to meet certain specifications in order to be considered 'secure.' We are talking, after all, about our money...*Not configurable to tasteWhile I fully understand that the ads are there to compensate for a lower price, let's place some perspective on this: the price difference is $15.00. For me, that's 1/2 an hour at work. For many, it's much more than that. What do you get, in exchange for your $15 discount? You get a lot of Amazon 'educated guesses' on what ads they think would most entice you into purchasing more products through them. I, personally, do not consider the fact that my wife cannot configure her browser as she wishes it to be, even if the extra $15 were paid.*The interface may be BASED on Android, but this is not an Android tabletThe Kindle is to tablets what Verizon is to wireless communication devices: proprietary control designed to push you toward purchasing more product controlled by the 'owner' of the operating system. Just as Verizon bastardizes the Android operating system to make sure that they are in as much control of your usage as possible, Amazon has followed suit with the Kindle and actually prevents any true customization. Again, this is not a 'Tablet PC.' This is a book reader with great display and extra features.*Purchased keyboard/carrying case was not even recognized.I am an electronic gadgets junkie. I am also an enterprise deployment engineer for a major computer solutions provider. I can script and automate most administrative functions of of an enterprise deployment of a business computer OS installation, and make it compatible (out of the box) with multiple platforms. If I have to fumble through several screens in order to try (and fail) to connect an USB keyboard, how is the average user going to feel?*Any app you use is automatically added to your carousel.While for many people this might be a god-send, neither my wife nor I consider this a feature. We consider it a nuisance. Kindle simply wants to make far too many decisions for the consumer. We are not sheeple in this house, and are quite capable of thinking for ourselves...*Either charging or keyboard, never both.The Kindle provides only one USB (micro) port, which means you can never use an external keyboard, and be charging the unit, simultaneously. for those like my wife that don't like virtual keyboards, this is definitely a drawback. For something that is billed as being as useful as Amazon claims the Kindle to be, there are some severe limitations that prevent this unit from being classified by anything other than a glorified book reader.Summary:While the Kindle is not a bad product, in and of itself, it did not fit our needs. Neither did it fulfill our expectations (based on advertising descriptions) of a tablet PC. I have built every computer I have owned, from the motherboard up. I am not technically impaired. With the Kindle in my hands, I felt very much like I was begging for the right to make decisions for myself, and still being declined. This very well may be useful for people that do a lot of reading, but it is definitely not worth the $300 we ended up spending. It took less than an hour to decide to send this back.Perspective:It is not my desire to belittle the product. The two stars are not indicative of the product, but more how the product failed to fit our specific needs. Others may have a different experience, based on their specific needs. However, We are very solid to ourselves when we stated that the Kindle is definitely not worth the asking price.

We purchased the Kindle Fire HD for my 5 year old, hoping to wean him off of my wife's iPad. We signed up for Kindle Free Time, which for $2.99/month is actually a really good deal and has a lot of included content for kids. There are plenty of apps available on the Amazon App Store. Basically, there are plenty of videos, music, games, and apps available and they are easily accessed directly from the Kindle, but beyond that the Kindle Fire HD is a below average product at best.The Pros:-A lot of content available and Kindle Free Time is a steal at $2.99/month for Prime MembersThe Cons:-Battery life is sub par, never more than 2.5-3 hours of use and charging is extremely slow, even with the $20 "fast" charger we purchased-Non-user friendly UI, everything is buried deep in the menus and extremely slow-Wi-Fi is awful, extremely slow, want a new app have to leave it for an hour or two to downloadand you can forget about streaming video, all my other devices at home stream HD Video just fine-Storage-*The Kindle starts running even slower than usual anytime the storage is below 1GB. Seriously, this is a 16GB device*When in settings looking at storage, there is a category for other and it is constantly between 3 and 5GBcannot figure where nearly a third of my data is being used (shouldn't need a third party app to manage this)To elaborate on the Pro and Cons above, I realize this is a $200 device ($220) if you want a charger. I didn't expect a super high resolution display or any other extras, but I expect that when I try to open an app it doesn't constantly crash or give me the launcher is unavailable message. I think it reasonable to expect Wi-Fi that works at least reasonably well especially since Amazon has advertised the speed of their Wi-Fi, well the Wi-Fi is almost useless. At this point, I am ready to return this Kindle and go for a used iPad Mini, I am not trying to compare the two as I know there is a $100 price difference, but at least I know the Mini will work. Perhaps it is that I am not too savvy with Android, but if the storage issue is an Android thing and 1/3 of available storage will never be available, then I just assume pay the extra $100 and get an iPad Mini.My final thoughts on the Kindle Fire HD are that Amazon should have stuck to E-Readers and let the computer companies make tablets e.g. Apple and Samsung.Update 08/29/2013:Installed a third party app to clean up my Kindle Fire and it appears the issues experienced above were related to the fact that I had just under 1GB of storage left on the device. It seems as though that should not cause the slowdown of the device like it did, but the issue is now fixed thanks to the cleaner app. An app that had not uninstalled properly was taking up nearly 3 GBs of space. The cleaner app found the app and cleaned it out. Everything seems to be working ok now. Still two stars, as the UI issues are still a problem and the fact I had to install a third party app to clean out the old program makes the OS seem a little flaky to me. In the future I will just spend a little more and get a device that is a little bit more reliable.

reviewText: The fire is the follow-up to the fire I had waited for. This one really competes with the iPad and more. I really enjoy the increase in memory and improved video capabilities with fire HD.

I've shopped Amazon heavily for several years and am an Amazon Prime member, so the Kindle Fire HD makes sense for me in a lot of ways.The Fire HD has a gorgeous screen, with colors bright and sharp, the audio is surprisingly crisp, it's easy and straightforward to operate if you have even limited experience with tablets or mobile phones, the connect to WiFi is quick and simple, and there are tons of free apps for games, entertainment, shopping, etc.My one negative -- and it's a surprise I didn't expect -- is the weight. The only place I was able to see the Fire HD before buying to look at its features was at Best Buy, where it was attached to a bulky security device. When I picked up the Fire HD, I assumed the weight was related to the security device, but that's not the case. The Fire HD is quite heavy, especially compared to other tablets.I'm a senior lady with arthritis in my hands. I had an iPad 2 which I loved, but I gave it to my daughter after 3 months because I couldn't manage the weight or bulk (this was before the Mini came out). I now have a Samsung Galaxy Tab 7.7 which works beautifully with a full Android platform and is very lightweight; but because I use it heavily for email, notes, and work-related stuff during the day, by the time I'm ready to settle in for an evening of reading, the battery life is largely used up, so I thought a separate device for reading might work well for me. (I used the Paperwhite for 6 months and don't care for it.)The Fire HD, unfortunately, is heavy and bulky, and it's hard to hold with one hand. I can sit and hold it on my lap or prop it up, but I can't hold it in one hand while I do something else with the other hand (eat, drink, etc.). In other words, for me it's not very mobile.I'm probably in the minority, and the weight doesn't mean the Fire HD isn't a great device, it definitely is! But it might not have been the best choice for me.UPDATE: 8/27/13Now that I've used the Fire HD every day for 3 weeks, I can say for sure that the weight of the device is too much for me to handle comfortably and it's a huge disappointment. I'm NOT suggesting it's a flaw of any kind. I mention it only for customers for whom weight & size might matter. I won't return it but may pass it on to my sister if the next version is lighter/slimmer. In terms of how the Fire HD works, though, I REALLY like it! My primary use is as an e-reader, but I like being able to keep up with my email, read the news/check the weather, and play an occasional game. It won't replace my Galaxy Tab 7.7 because the Fire HD doesn't have a full Android platform; but for what it does do, I'm pretty impressed.
summary: Great tablet, only one negative for me

reviewText: We have two Kindle Fire HDs in our house of this model since it came out and honestly the only reason it still gets used is we can give it to our two year old to use it. The very very very limited number of applications is the reason for this.We do not need a whole ton of applications, and my wife doesn't need an iPad for power but a basic set of applications and choices is required. You do not have that with a Kindle Fire HD; you have maybe a couple thousand apps at most to choose from and some of them (like any App store) are complete crap leaving you with a very narrow selection of applications.It REALLY REALLY needs the Google Play store; even if it is has a built in "I am going to void my warranty and enable the Google Play store option" as the extremely narrow number of applications makes it a $200 Leap Frog device with ads.The best thing about it is Kindle Free Time for giving it to my 2 year old to play.. but even that is getting old as it is not refreshed and there is a lot of books there are not interested in so we are likely going to just cancel that as well.If it had access to the Google Play store and gave us a larger selection of apps, even if they are completely under powered on the Kindle, we would at least have access to them to purchase them. I would also give it probably 4 stars vs 2 stars because it would facilitate basic tablet functionality very well for those that don't want a lot of technology but want to perform some basic tasks at a good price point. Though true Android tablets are also coming onto the market in this price point range with better stats than the Kindle and most importantly access to the Google Play store.So all an all, no matter what Kindle model or specifications are out there; the specifications do not matter unless you have access to applications and the Amazon Application store honestly just doesn't cut it.
summary: Lack of Applications makes it loose 3 stars.

I have to decide if I will return it or not and just go with another Nook.

The actual Kindle device (Prime membership for it is reviewed in detail at the end):Pros:Good, solid build quality.Screen looks great - My mom sits at a desk in front of a monitor all day at work, so I considered a Paperwhite with a concern for eye strain, but so far, so good. She says that she doesn't notice any strain on her eyes after reading for a decent period of time, and the picture is very good.Easy to navigate - locked-down OS makes it simple and fairly foolproof.My mom figured it out on her own (66 and not very technology-literate, set up an Amazon account, signed up for Prime, and was reading her first book before I got a chance to show any apps, etc.)Decent selection of apps. She will most likely only use Facebook and email, other than reading books and maybe watching some TV or movies. Maybe browse the web, but I don't know how much she'll use that instead of her desktop computer.Cons:Apps limited to Amazon App Store (missing GMail app and other standard Google apps and apps from the Google Play store that are very good).Only comes with USB cord for charging. PowerFast charger seems like a ripoff, but I thought it would be the only way my mom might remember how to charge it...Prime membership doesn't go nearly as far as I thought it would... (see below)Searching for things is a bit of a pain on the Kindle, especially if you want to sort out things that are free for Prime members... For instance, if you search for John Grisham, you'll return all of his books, in no particular order, but you can't refine the search to only bring up anything that's free (which may be none, but the option isn't even there). When you pull up the free for Prime members list, if you use the search tool, it searches everything, not just the free things.Prime membership (as an accompaniment to the Kindle)Pros:You get free 2-day shipping with a Prime account. Great, if you shop Amazon.com a lot and want to rush your shipping. This is not something that my mother would use, as she doesn't shop online much, but also, if you're over $25 on almost anything on Amazon.com, you can get free Super Save shipping (5-8 days or so) which is only a problem if you need the package REALLY soon.You get access to the Kindle Lending Library, which has an extensive selection that Prime members get to borrow from for free. (Only 1 book per month though.......see cons)Lastly, you get unlimited streaming of Amazon Instant Video, but the selection there seems fairly limited, and even more so if you're a Prime member and are looking for free stuff to watch.Now, the cons:With the Kindle, my mom set up an Amazon account with a free month of Amazon Prime. She really doesn't order anything online, and hasn't yet been able to dig into the streaming Instant Video yet. My biggest disappointment was that with the Prime membership ($80/year), you get access to the Amazon Lending Library with a huge selection of books... which is great, except that you can only borrow ONE BOOK per MONTH... so beware... It will be hard for most people to justify the cost of a Prime membership for what one book would cost per month, especially if they have a local library nearby.Prime membership also gets you free 2-day shipping on a lot of stuff on Amazon.com... which is great if you need things in a rush, or buy something that doesn't qualify for Super Saver shipping. Personally, I can live without a Prime membership and I do a LOT of shopping on Amazon.That leaves the Instant Video. From what I saw (spending about 15 minutes browsing the library) I don't know how much content is available on Instant Video that either of us couldn't get through a Netflix account already. Probably very little. I'll give her an HDMI cable in case she wants to use that to watch it on her TV instead of the 7" screen, but I really think that the content is lacking a bit. She's used to having a DVR, but her new landlord doesn't have one, so she misses some of the shows she likes. The problem is that not all of them are on Instant Video, and most of them are $3 or $4 to rent the standard definition version if it's a relatively new show. Again, not benefiting from the Prime membership.So, really, it's tough (for me, at least) to justify spending money to borrow books when the public library isn't that far away. That means that you almost have to have the Prime account, because buying the books can get really expensive without it. The downfall there, though, is that you can only borrow 1 per month. For what amounts to almost $7/month, I'd expect a lot more. I can't really justify the Prime membership for Instant Video or shipping, but I can see my mom not borrowing a lot of stuff just because of what she'd have to pay for it. So, I'll most likely pay for her Prime account to go along with the Kindle and hope she uses it to access a lot of free video, too, haha.

Got it for my wife (also gave one to my mother and mother-in-law) and they all love it. It's certainly tied in to the Amazon universe but being prime members that's probably a good thing. None of them are particularly technologically savvy but they don't have any problems using the device.

I really do like the Kindle Fire and the 7" is perfect to carry. However, I'm disappointed in the battery life. Very short compared to the original Kindle. Works great for books and games, otherwise I don't find a use for it.

When I got my Kindle Fire HD, I was soooo excited! Finally a tablet that did most of what I wanted AND had text to speech! As a busy mom on the go, I was thrilled.Yeah, that didn't last long. Right away, I found out that every single time I used the text to speech (TTS) on the Kindle app, the app would crash EVERY. TEN. MINUTES. I would be driving, and it would just stop, and the app would freeze up. I'd have to pull over, close the app, re-open it, and try to figure out where I was (because it would re-open at my last bookmark...which might be thirty pages back.) I mostly use my kindle to listen to books while I drive. I have no time to actually sit and read. Obviously, pulling over every ten minutes isn't safe. And I always fall asleep listening to a book...which is hard to do when you have to keep getting up to "reboot" it. But I was so busy I had no time to call Amazon and ask for a new one. Then....the update happened!After an update in March, which Amazon gave me NO choice in accepting, the text to speech DISAPPEARED off my kindle. I looked for help on the internet, and everyone just told me where to find it on my Kindle. Yeah, um, I use it every day. I know where it is. It was GONE.Called Amazon, got a complete and utter idiot who told me that THERE HAS NOT BEEN A NEW UPDATE TO THIS KINDLE YET. (This is late March, after ALL my friends had received the update, which this guy swore did not exist. Are you reading this, Amazon? Holy Cow!) So my friends and I all apparently imagined the update. Some of them also imagined calling customer service with problems from the update. *eye roll*Then he told me to just de-register and re-register...to which I replied "I have files side-loaded onto my Kindle that can't be replaced, they are NOT in my Cloud...are you SURE that won't erase everything off my kindle?" He said no. I asked a few more times, because at this point I didn't trust him, and he *supposedly* talked to a manager, and promised that his manager said that no, it would NOT affect my files. (This was, by the way, after repeatedly trying to explain what "side loading" is, and he claimed to finally understand me...clearly, he never did...apparently he thinks that all content comes from Amazon, and Amazon only.) The Kindle even warned me that files could be lost by de-registering, but when I pointed that out to the guy, he told me not to worry, nothing would happen.So I deregistered. Re-registered.Guess what?Yep. Kindle was wiped. Oh sure, the book ICONS were still there, making me think everything was fine, but I realized after I hung up with customer service that everything needed to be re-downloaded from the cloud, and all my sideloaded files were GONE. And so were hours and hours worth of tv shows, many of which I hadn't watched. I had to go to a wifi hotspot to re-download them, because re-doing it at home would have used up my internet data allowance. I sat in my car for hours and hours re-downloading. Thanks, Amazon dude. Thanks a lot.Yes, re-registering fixed my kindle. Sort of. For a while The constant every-ten-minutes crashing of the Kindle app stopped, and I could find the tts choices again, exactly where they were before they disappeared. All was wonderful with my Kindle Fire HD.Fast forward a couple of months. TTS is acting up again. It is repeating 1 to 2 words on every page. Yeah, that's not too distracting. And I would like to speed up the reading, but I can't find any way to do it. (Didn't there used to be a button or something for speeding it up? Yeah...there's nothing there. I'm not sure where that used to be, but if it was there like I *think* it was, it's not in the settings menu of the Kindle app any more.)To sum up? I like my Kindle Fire HD for having a convenient tablet to travel with and watch movies on. But for reading? It SUCKS. (If you like text to speech, stick with Keyboard Kindle...far superior. The only improved TTS feature for the Fire HD is the voice, which I admit, sounds much, much better.)Oh, and if anyone at Amazon is reading this...train your freaking employees. This was daytime on a weekday, and I got a guy who not only doesn't understand that de-registering wipes your kindle, but apparently his MANAGER didn't either (or the guy lied and took a pee break instead of asking). And the guy also apparently doesn't know that you can sideload files on your kindle. I mean, really, Amazon? Really? Disappointing.If the text to speech would freaking work well like it did on the Keyboard Kindle, I'd give this at least four, maybe five stars. But I've had so many problems with TTS, and it is THE most important feature to me, and I'm sure it is to a lot of other moms, sight-impaired readers, and elderly readers. It's the reason I ditched my nook for the Kindle in the first place. I recommended to my husband that he not buy the Fire HD, as he had planned to. I miss my Keyboard Kindle. For a reading experience, it was FAR superior. And I didn't have to worry about a stray finger sending me back to the beginning of the stinking book--at worst, I'd bump a button and turn one page.As for other features: it's much less convenient to surf on than my iPad was, but watching tv shows on it is awesome. They outdid themselves with the speakers. Even with the s***ty TTS, I'd probably give this 3 stars, except my customer service experience was SO bad with it...and that was a first for me, with an Amazon product.
summary: Do Not Buy if it's mostly for Reading! And Amazon "techs" don't know their product!

reviewText: I was able to put my own movies/videos on it which was very nice. It is strange that the titles of your personal videos does not show up until you click and hold them for a second. reviewText: I've had my Kindle (2nd one) for over a month now. It works pretty good for the most part. BUT, when there are issues, Kindle's Customer Support is more than inept.I've called for three issues. This was my experience for each:1. The wireless indicator repeatedly displayed an "x" on the status bar. The customer service rep was very kind and exhausted all measures to figure out the problem. All his effort was to no avail and he promptly shipped me a replacement device. (Subsequently, I had to call the customer support for my Wii device and the Wii support person resolved the connectivity issue for the Wii and resolved my Kindle issue. Unfortunately the device was already scheduled for return.)2. Kindle Free Time - the content on this feature is wonderful for children. It is not lacking at all. The problem I experienced is whenever I download books or apps, the appear on my daughter's carousel (homepage). I called Kindle support and was on the phone for at least 45 minutes, which turned out to be useless. The representative had NO clue of how to resolve the issue. At this point I just wanted to know if it's possible to stop this. If it were, I would figure out how on my own. After 45 minutes, I had to kindly ask that someone get back with me once they figure out an answer - of course she didn't call back as promised.3. My Kindle stopped displaying images. I called for support and the rep. walked me through the steps and told me which options to select in Settings. After I followed his suggestions, I go into the internet to confirm the problem has been resolved. Come to find out all my bookmarks were deleted when I selected "clear data". I was (and still am) a little upset about this. Granted I should have put on my reading glasses and read the little warning dialogue box, but I think that the rep should take a few seconds to warn you that you are about to wipe EVERY bookmark ( and I have to see whatelse). And surprise! I didn't receive a follow-up customer support email.The support for Kindle is less than adequate. For this reason alone, I will NOT purchase another Kindle this Christmas. A product is only as good as the support behind it.
summary: Kindle device - great. Customer Support - not so much.

The only problem I have with it is that when she tries to watch any type of TV show, movie, video, ect, it freezes alot. I don't know if this is normal or what but it does get a bit annoying.

i was very impressed with this device at first, but that feeling has quickly changed. the Android OS is very buggy and unstable like most Android devices that i have encountered. as an E book reader it works fine, but if you are a power user and attempt to use this thing as a tablet you will soon feel the pain and constraints of this thing. i was happy at first because i could hook up HDMI to my TV, but after several app crashes and reboots, i feel like i am testing an unfinished product.

I purchased my Kindle Fire HD last Sunday August 4th and it arrived Tuesday, earlier than the expected delivery date of Wednesday August 7th.I'd been putting off buying another Kindle since my original Kindle still works great (my first Kindle was the best purchase decision I've made), but there was a sale and I'd been reading reviews and talking to people who had bought the Kindle Fire and the Kindle Fire HD and figured it was worth a shot.I love my new Kindle Fire HD. It arrived almost completely charged and after one full charge Wednesday night I've yet to have to charge it again - I've used it about an hour or so each night before bed. The device is extremely easy to navigate and figure out. I would say it took me about thirty minutes to get my favorite apps onto the device, favorite a few websites and blogs I visit regularly, and read a sample of a book I'd ordered earlier that day. It's heavier than my original Kindle and that took a little getting used to, but I'm not complaining.I've used it outside in the bright sunshine and there was no glare which is awesome. I've watched videos from Amazon Instant Video and the HBO Go app with no issues whatsoever.I know some reviewers have complained about the Kindle Fire HD not coming with a charger, but I feel that buying the charger at a reasonable price was completely acceptable, especially since I saved some money on the actual price of the device itself.I also have no issues whatsoever with the ads on the home screen or the suggestions at the bottom of the screen. I like suggestions for other items I may enjoy. That's one of the reason I like Amazon so much - the recommendations based on other purchases I've made.The HD screen is vivid and the colors are vibrant and beautiful. The sound quality is excellent.I don't have an Ipad or other tablet to compare the Kindle Fire HD to but for a media device it's fantastic.Some reviewers also complained about the Silk browser but I have no issues with that either. I actually searched my HP laptop with Internet Explorer and the Silk browser on my Kindle Fire HD for the same website and the Kindle browser was faster than my laptop browser.I would recommend the Kindle Fire HD.
