I bought 64GB version of the card to use with GoPro Hero 3 black edition. It didn't work out. The card worked OK if camera was set to resolution with lower bit rates. E.g. worked fine in 720p with protune on, or 1080p with protune off. However, in 1080p with protune on (bitrate is just shy of 6 MB/s in this mode -- much higher then with protune turned off) it was nothing but trouble. Camera would sometime work, and sometime randomly stop recording for no obvious reason. I first suspected camera, but testing with different SD cards, it ended up being SanDisk's card that was at fault. My spare card, an old and cheap 16GB PNY (also class 10), worked just fine under same conditions and with same camera settings.Once it was obvious it was problem with the card, I found people on GoPro's forums that had trouble with this specific card as well (well, you always find these only after you figure it out for yourself, right?). Anyhow, I did some speed tests with the card by doing simple write of 1GB file full of zeros using Unix dd utility to copy 1GB of zeros from /dev/zero (where else would you find that many zeros ;-) onto a file on the card. The result was that on average, SanDisk's card would manage about 10.2 MB/s. Just barely above the bar for class 10 card. However, that was average over 1GB. During the write test, the speed was oscillating with many spikes and drops. Drops were as low as 7MB/s. Uh. I thought write speed of class 10 card should never dip below 10 MB/s? For comparison, my old cheap class 10 PNY card was chugging along at constant 13 MB/s under the same test. No spikes and no drops in speed.The card will probably work fine in most devices, as bitrates when recording 1080p video are often low enough and/or camera might have huge buffer. But if you want to use it to record video at high bitrates, and your device doesn't have huge buffer to compensate for speed bumps of this card, you may run into trouble. Be wary of using it in Hero3 in modes that have higher bit rates (e.g. 1080p with protune enabled).SanDisk's website lists part numbers as SDSDQUI-064G with adapter, and SDSDQUA-064G without adapter. This conflicts with product description on Amazon. While this is likely just Amazon not getting product description right again (a bit too common thing), it's interesting to note.[Update Apr 20 2013]:Some numbers from testing the card. The test is extremely simple. Write out 1GB of zeros onto the card using standard Unix dd command to read 128KB blocks of zeroes from special device /dev/zero and write it onto the card. 128KB * 8192 = 1GB. dd displays transfer stats once it finishes. While dd was running, I run iostat in second terminal displaying 1 second interval stats as a measure of current speed. This was done on the Mac. dd command line can be used as-is to repeat test on Linux system, however iostat command is different on Linux and would need to be modified slightly. I choose 128KB block size, as that seems to be what device drivers merges sequential writes into anyhow. Using different block sizes, results are comparable.$ dd if=/dev/zero of=test bs=131072 count=81928192+0 records in8192+0 records out1073741824 bytes transferred in 101.578307 secs (10570582 bytes/sec)So, 10 MB/s and all is good? Right? Wrong! iostat running in parallel with above dd command recorded this:$ iostat -d -w 1 disk2disk2KB/t tps MB/s123.11 76 9.12116.61 185 21.04122.94 49 5.88128.00 41 5.12128.00 89 11.11128.00 134 16.73128.00 69 8.61128.00 61 7.62128.00 99 12.36[ ... and so on until dd finishes writing 1GB of zeros to the card ... ]IMO, the last column should never dip under 10MB/s for card labeled class-10.For comparison, same test run against Samsung Pro 64GB micro-SD card:$ dd if=/dev/zero of=test bs=131072 count=81928192+0 records in8192+0 records out1073741824 bytes transferred in 52.869111 secs (20309436 bytes/sec)$ iostat -d -w 1 disk2disk2KB/t tps MB/s125.30 138 16.86117.73 157 18.03123.04 150 18.00128.00 159 19.86128.00 156 19.47126.45 160 19.73128.00 150 18.72128.00 154 19.22128.00 153 19.11[ ... and so on until dd finishes writing 1GB of zeros to the card ... ]So, Samsung is on average 2x faster, but more importantly it's speed is much more constant. And critically important, it never dips under 10MB/s.

Read speeds ranged from 15-25MB/s, while write speeds ranged from 4-8MB/sec for big files, and below 1MB/sec for small files. This is what I would call largely unusable. VERY disappointing.

Although Amazon claim it is a C10 ultra fast Memory Card, it actually has much slower write speed than other C10 microSD card (it only scores about 60% of the normal speed). For example, I have tested it against my old Maxell C10 HC microSD card. The test was done by writing the same 3035MB random data from DRAM to empty microSD card through a USB3 card reader. The resulting time was the average value from 3 tests of each device:SanDisk Ultra 32GB C10/UHS1: 5m50.816s means 8.7MB/sMaxell C10 HC: 3m38.787s means 13.9MB/sThe speed is completely unacceptable for a Class-10 claim (13% lower than 10MB/s, the lowest boundary of Class-10 device), even the over-advertisement of SD card speeds are common (claiming 30MB/s for actual 12-15MB/s). It is almost a scam. Some Class-6 card will beat this "Class-10" card.

The primary reason for buying this extra capacitySanDisk Ultra 64 GB microSDXC Class 10card was to use it inSamsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch Model GT-P5113)and I am happy to share that you can get this to work flawlessly after some initial glitches. (Read below)Firstly you need to be aware that the Samsung Tablet Model GT-P5113 currently runs with Android OS 4.1.1 with Kernel 3.0.31-523998 and Build number JRO03C.P5113UECLK7.(Jelly Bean) My experiences shared here are with that level of Android OS your experiences may vary depending on what version of OS you are running. The SanDisk Ultra 64 GB microSDXC card purchased from Amazon (Retail Packaging) gets recognized just fine however when the tablet's Media Device A.K.A 'MTP' application attempts to talk your PC via USB cable the Tablet simply reboots! and after that the card is presented to the PC. - Really strange indeed!This baffled me for couple of hours. Firstly, I attempted to format the card (exFAT) in PC and it formatted just fine. After that I attempted to use it in the tablet to see the same behavioral oddity of instantaneous reboot of the tablet as 'MTP' application tries to communicate with the PC. This made me investigate the issue further and I determined the root cause was the fact that SANDISK now seen to factory format the card with 'exFAT' but also somehow seen to include an 'offset' of 16MB at the beginning of the card which shows up as 16MB unallocated region in the initial sectors on this card under windows disk management tool.The solution is to get rid of that 'unallocated' 16MB partition on the card. You could do it in PC but that might require some windows command line experience and using 'diskpart' utility and what not and I do not want to confuse people here with that process. For most novice users The process should be very simple, Just insert the card on the tablet and use the 'native' SD Card format tool under 'settings' that Android OS 4.1.1 has and it will get rid of that 16MB partition and happily remount it. Now after this simple process the 'MTP' application works just fine with PC to transfer files to the SD card without any strange reboot phenomenon.Not sure why SANDISK formats their Class 10 card in this fashion (They never did it with their class 6 cards earlier) and there's gotta be some technical explanation for why they include that 16MB partition that only SANDISK can give. In the end if you reformat the card in the tablet (Which defaults to exFAT) the card is seen to work just fine.Bottomline:-----------This is an awesome 64GB capacity MicroSD card from a reputed manufacturer for budget minded people and gets the job done beautifully. The read and write speeds are adequate enough for most Audio,Video & picture file formats in a tablet. The glitch mentioned above forced me to give *Four* stars instead of *Five* stars but let that not stop you from making a decision to buy it.Highly recommended!Cheers!

reviewText: Hi:I ordered two card and they arrived the next day, even faster than Prime. Unfortunatey, this 64gb MicroSD card is designed to only work with ex-fat. If you're an ex-fat fan and don't ever plan to change, this is the card for you. I've been able to take all of the previous 64gb MicroSD cards I've ordered, put them in an adapter and format them in my Windows 7 desktop. I'm a NTSF fan and find it to be much more stable in tablets.With other cards that aren't intentionally crippled, I can format the card to NTSF on Monday, ex-fat on Tuesday, Fat32 on Wednesday. It's ex-fat or the highway for SanDisk.You can use EaseUS Partition Master to format the card to Fat32 for devices such as cameras and mp3 players and many, many, many others that don't support ex-fat. That being said, you only get one shot. Once it's formatted into Fat32, attempting to format back to Exfat or NTSF hoses the card. I couldn't reformat to NTSF no matter what I tried. Once again, don't bother trying to format in your computer, ex-fat is the only choice.Any card that needs a special utility to format to anything other than ex-fat shouldn't be supported. Don't buy it! It's designed to fail.Shame on you Sandisk!Update 9/24/12:***************************I spoke with Sandisk technical support and they confirmed that Sandisk Ultra 64gb MicroSd cards are not compatible with Android 4.0 and above. This would be for Class 10, SanDisk Ultra 64 GB microSDXC Class 10 UHS-1 Memory Card 30MB/s with Adapter SDSDQUA-064G-U46A as well as SanDisk 64GB Mobile Ultra MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1 30MB/s Memory Card with SD Adapter (NEW VERSION) - Retail Packaging with Komputerbay SDXC USB Reader.I did not have any success formatting the class 10 card with EaseUS Partition Master. SanDisk recommended the free utility, HPUSBDISK.exe and I successfully downloaded it from Softpedia. I was unable to format the card with NTSF but successfully converted one of the cards to Fat32 for a friend who wants to use it in a SanDisk mp3 player, that of course is not compatible with ex-fat.Acting on Sandisk advice I am returning the unopened class ten cards with the KomputerBay reader. I spoke with a patient and gracious tier-one tech support person and the party line seems be that consumers only use MicroSD cards in phones. I don't know what they're thinking: cameras, mp3 players, tablets, adapters and so on. Anyway it's a known issue.I can confirm that the class 6 64gb MicroSD card can be formatted in Windows7 back and forth to most any format so after returning four class 10 cards, I'm back to class six.It's still unconscionable to deliberately design these cards to be incompatible. I hope SanDisk will come up with a solution or recall the cards. Buyer beware.Update: 9/29/12**********************I received my two replacement class 6, 64gb MicroSD cards and it took less than five minutes to open the horrible packaging and to perform a quick format to NTSF. Done!I gave my friend the Class 10 64gb MicroSD card formatted into Fat32 by HPUSBDISK.EXE and he couldn't read it on his computer. As it turns out, the class 10 cards are not only incompatible with most devices bur also with most usb card readers. Another trip across town.I can confirm that the IOGEAR SD/MicroSD/MMC Card Reader/Writer GFR204SD (Green/Gray) selling on Amazon for $6.99 works. So after countless hours of wasted effort, my friend has a card formatted to Fat32 that works with a SanDisk mp3 player.Once again, SanDisk has admitted that these cards are not compatible with Androd 4.0 or above, that being 100% of Android tablets and a majority of Android phones. These cards are intentionally crippled by design.To quote a friend:"Per the SDHC standard, the format is FAT32. SDXC (64 GB and larger) the spec calls for exFAT. Microsoft has limited the OS to only format larger cards as exFAT and will not allow FAT32. Also, seems they have found a way to also block NTFS. Thus far, very few Android devices can read exFAT because they refuse to pay M$ for licensing of the exFAT file system. "To all masochists out there--buy this card. To everyone else--unsafe at any speed.

reviewText: I'm afraid I don't get the rave reviews. The online video you are directed to with the included instructions, reference a "Start" and a "Finish" tab that you use to peel off each side. Either fix the inaccurate instructional video, or provide better quality control at the factory to ensure the finish side & tab actually exist.The other really big problem with this is the protector is that it is cut just slightly too large. The tolerances on the dimensions and cutouts of this protector do NOT need to be so ridiculously tight! It's OK to have it just slightly smaller than the overall dimensions of your screen, but this protector is not. The end results is it is impossible to start applying the protector on the bottom edge and get it to line up perfectly as you work your way up applying it. You're going to need a micrometer and an industrial "clean room" to get this thing lined up and applied properly and without lint bubbles. You're always just barely off as you apply it and by the time you finish applying the protector, the top edge is off center, causing major bubbles on the outside edge of the side that is just barely overlapping off the side AND the cut out hole in the protector is partially on top of your front camera now, obstructing it. As you apply it, you find out about half way up that you're off centered or out of alignment, so you peel it back down and start over, but after several times of doing this, you inevitably have dust now attached to the "sticky" side of the protector, so even if you do get it somehow miraculously aligned, the protector is ruined due to the bubbles you'll get with the dust/lint particles on it.This protector really needs to be just slightly smaller for the width and length and the cutouts for the home button, camera, and speaker also need to be just slightly larger. This would allow you to apply it on the first try without needing to be so ridiculously accurate with the alignment from bottom to top, thus eliminating the longer exposure to dust/lint. Sorry, but this protector was nothing but a waste of time.

I worked for ATT and applied hundreds of screen protectors to iPhones and everything else. It's simple.First clean off the screen with a dry cloth obviously.Second, take a piece of cellophane tape and touch the sticky side to the glass over and over until you have covered the entire face. That is all you have to do to get lint off. Don't use canned air or a fan. It just kicks up more dust and is a waste of time. All you need is tape!Then apply the screen protector. It helps if you bend it lengthwise and center it on the ear and button holes. Then once lined up, drop the edges and smooth out any bubbles quickly. The quicker you can center it and drop it, the less likely you are to have any lint sneak in.If you do see any lint under the screen protector after applying it, don't worry. Just lift up a corner with a piece of tape to avoid touching the underside of the protector, and take a second piece of tape and repeat the lint removal procedure, targeting the spots where you've noticed lint. Then just lay the protector back down and smooth out any bubbles.I've had tons of practice so I can do it perfectly, but it's not hard for anyone to do.

While the first problem is more about being precise, the second one is more pressing - as soon as the protective first layer (green marker) is peeled off, dust start attaching to the inner part of your protective screen, and the only option is to use the stickers provided and try removing it. I read somewhere to use the steam room trick to prevent that from happening, and at this point I'd recommend to do it, since attempting in a normal environment will most likely result in a lot of dust collected. As I said once it's on, it looks great, but installation is a problem.

I have both the anti-glare and the HD Clear protectors. For me, the reduction in image quality with the anti-glare was a bit too much, so I've opted for the HD Clear. However, the reduced finger prints and screen smear was tough to walk away from. Both products serve a purpose and it is user preference for sure.I'd like to add that Tech Armor customer support and service is about the best I've ever dealt with. I made an order mistake and their rapid response to correct my mistake was flawless. They really are the first place I will look to for iphone accessories.

Ordered these for my iPhone 5 and can't be happier. I cleaned my screen using the microfiber cloth (included), then used the lint tape (included) to remove stray particles of dust, then installed the screen according to the instructions. After using the cardboard squeegee (included) to coax out the bubbles (then removing the top layer protection film), the screen looks simply amazing! The cutouts for the button, speaker, and camera are perfect. I can't even tell that I have a screen protector installed, it's that good! I'm very impressed!
summary: Looks great, you can't tell it's there!

reviewText: Problem number one with this product is the sticker they put on it. When you remove it he leaves a residue.Problem number two is you cannot view the phone with polarized sunglasses.

Perhaps its just me but I had a hard time getting this onto my iphone (new) without air bubbles. After multiple unsuccesful tries, I tried the one that came with my iphone protector (Incipio Dual PRO) and it worked the first time.
summary: OK-hard to get on without bubbles

reviewText: product came on time, 3 screen protectors, and works well. So affordable for the price I paid and product is in great quality.

I was highly impressed with Tech Armor's line of screen protectors. I have them for the iPhone 5, Galaxy Note 2 and S3, and the HTC DNA. Every one of them is a perfect fit and I have never had any problems with air bubbles or fingerprints. And they last super long. I highly recommend this product!

I have always had the clear protective covers. They were prone to fingerprints, they get oily and sometimes the sensitivity of the screen dimishes, etc, etc, etc....I decided to pull the trigger on this 'matte' screen protector and it's awesome. No fingerprints, no glare and it gives it a real cool look that the clear protectors can't pull off. Opening the package you receive a cloth, 3 protectors and a plastic/rubber piece to help with installation. It's very easy to install. You slightly peel off the backside plastic and place it on the screen and it practically lays itself without bubbles.As far as the cosmetics, it's hard to explain but with this 'matte' cover on the face of the phone it make it's look like the back of the phone. A few times I thought my phone was upside down until I realized the home button was in plain view. It basically gives the phone a very solid and slick look. Another way of saying it, it doesn't look like glass with it on. It looks solid and gives it a pretty cool look to the phone.PLEASE KEEP IN MIND WHEN BUYING THIS SCREEN PROTECTOR... IF you like HD viewing and that is a HUGE priority with having a phone then expect to have that diminish slightly. It looks beautiful with it on BUT it does slightly take away from the vivid HD appearance. Again, if playing games or watching movies is your thing then it does slightly take away from the vivid, crystal clear experience. Even so, it still looks beautiful and vibrant.Also, because it's a 'matte' finish, it gives the display a sense of depth to it. The actual touch / feel / swiping feels great. Very slick and never gets oil'd up by your fingertips.Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend this protector if you are a fan of the 'matte' finish. Both my wife and I have it and love it. Definite purchase!
summary: Perfect Fit. Looks Great. Great feel.

reviewText: These were not matte finished. They did not cut glare. And the paper tabs that you are supposed to remove did not come off cleanly and left an unsightly glob of paper debris and adhesive on the screen. Simply a horrible experience. Product returned.
summary: Not matte. Not cutting glare. Not good.

reviewText: I purchased these screen protectors based on the large amount of positive reviews, that and they were inexpensive. They were really clear but the protectors are made of a plastic that is somewhat sticky, it isn't as smooth as other screen protectors (the invisible shield line is smoother) and they all left a residue on my iPhone 5 after removing them. The worst aspect of installing these protectors is that they would not sit flush with my iPhone 5. It took me a while to finally get one of the screen protectors completely straight only for there to be a hair right in the middle of it. I threw that one away and opened up the second screen protector. I installed it fine but then it came up whenever I installed a soft gel case on my iPhone 5 simply because it wasn't sitting completely flush around the edges of the phone. It was crinkled so I threw it away. I couldn't even install the 3rd one as it never stuck to my phone. I ended up throwing all three protectors away, driving down to a retail store, picking up different ones, and they work much better. I don't recommend buying these as they are inexpensive for a reason. I'm not sure how people are using these with cases on their iPhones as I could never get it to work.
I was rather disappointed by the shimmer in the LCD. I'm told it would go away, but its been a while. Seems to loose some of the brightness too.
summary: Its ok, but I'll probably get something else in a few months.

reviewText: It works, screen isn't too distorted or blurred.Good thing it came with 3, my mother scratched one within the first week.

Needed to quickly buy a screen protector for my new iphone 5. Had great sucsess with the Power Support HD anitglare brand that Apple sells in its store for $15.00 a pair. But they aren't available in Amazon yet, so went with the Tech Armor. It goes on easy enough and not hard to get the bubbles out. My only complaint is the cover leaves major oil / finger prints to the point of distraction.The Power Support HD doesn't leave as many prints however the anti-glare feature does dull the vibrant colors. Plus the Power Support is very expensive.So for the money, Tech Armor is fine but if you tend to get annoyed by oil prints from your finger, try another product.
summary: Decent, but finger prints are distracting

reviewText: While the surface seems particularly susceptible to smears from either body oil or lotion, the protectors seem fine. Application and cleaning prior to attaching require (as always) great care and patience for best result.

Put simply, this screen doesn't do what it says it will. You can still see the activity on the screen when viewed a person sitting next to you, its just appears darker. I would not recomend this to anyone looking for privacy from the random stranger sitting next to you.

The package came with 3 protectors, which was a good bargain at $6.95. However, when I put the protector on, I noticed my phone was less responsive to touch. I'm not sure if the iPhone 5 is affected more by screen protectors or what, but I had to remove it in order to be able to use my phone.
summary: Fast shipping, but affects response on iPhone 5

reviewText: This screen protector is AMAZING. It's crystal clear, and if you install it correctly, you don't even notice that you have a screen protector applied. The home button is easy to access, and the speaker and camera hols are cut perfectly to size. The installation is easy, and it comes with instructions on how to do it! I have to say, the niftiest thing that they give you to install is this "Tech Armor Dust Removing Tape". Of course, it's just tape, but it doesn't leave a sticky residue on your iPhone, and it removes the dust easily!Overall, I highly recommend this screen protector. There is nothing wrong with it at all.
summary: Tech Armor iPhone 5S / 5C / 5 Case is Wonderful

reviewText: my screen protector scratches up immediately after application. true, the screen is anti-glare and matte, but there are so many scratches on it that it wouldn't matter any way.

at least one of them didn't fit correctly, no matter what i did. Since i only needed 2 to work correctly, I was covered. So for what you're paying? not worth it. Will they be effective at protection - probably.

reviewText: These are easy to put on as long as you are careful and just take some time when first applying it to your iPhoneGreat screen protectors for iPhone 5 and helps prevent finger print marks. Only minor drawback is the matte screen finish diminishes the brightness and clarity of the Retina display a little bit.
summary: Great screen protectors, no fingerprint marks!

reviewText: This is a good product and fits the iPhone 5s perfectly, if it is carefully installed. Instructions for application of the film are well-written, and are complete, and should be followed to the letter. Attention to cleanliness is very important. I had a problem with aligning the film so that the home key, and camera and earpiece were centered, and in the process wasted two of the three films in the package. Very important: do not touch the adhesive side of the film; If you must reposition the film, use either the dust removal tape strips provided, or ordinary plastic tape, like Scotch, to lift it. I give only three stars because I felt the positioning instructions were not strong enough.
Great kit! I have installed a good number of these and this is one of the best shields to apply in terms if ease, quality and durability.
summary: Great screen protector...quality film and easy install

reviewText: Screen protector went on nice and felt premium. No bubbles or other issues very straight forward.The privacy protector itself is grainy and ruins the retina display. I wish this was advertised in the description because it made the product unusable for me. If the protector was privacy but was clear on oroper viewing angle it would be much better.Additionally, I wish it offered a little more practice from more viewing angles as the only real blocked viewing angle is almost exactly flat with the phone. I will be returning this product.
Fairly easy to install (well, as easy as any of these protectors are to install). I like the anti-glare surface and have not had any issues with lack of touch response.

I've always used the wet version of Zagg and has protected my screen. I needed something quick as I can't find the wet version anymore. This works fine. Easy to clean, I use Spray Nine disinfectant since it disinfects virus and bacteria in 30-45 seconds, not 4-10 minutes like Lysol, Clorox or any store brand (Yes, I bet you've never disinfected...read your "disinfectant" instructions and see how long the contact time of being WET is). summary: I'm reluctant to use the word but I will: PERFECT!

reviewText: These are really the worst screen protectors I have ever had in regards tosmudges and fingerprints, have no idea what all the great reviews are allabout, I am returning, just not worth the money.

And so on.Now I'm empty-handed and looking for somethng else...the fool and his money are soon parted.

It's great to have an amazon basics option for an iPhone 5 charger ... but they need to go back to the drawing board, as it doesn't fit many popular cases.What, 2 stars just for that little oversight? It's a major oversight IMO, and needs to be fixed.

reviewText: Super cheap, but falls apart at connected easily; Cheap enough to make up for that short coming since it still works. Also love the color black, but that is a personal thing

reviewText: Both cords require me to move the cord around so it starts charging. I don't abuse my cables, but these didn't last very long at all. I'm only going to buy Apple ones from now on.

Very disappointing.The other one works fine - maybe I just got a dud, which is unusual for Amazon.

This cover good SAFTEY for iPad 4G with stand kid DONOT break it nobody have this cover only I Blason I love this cove and price is veery good to buy

I have a hard time justifying the price for such a small cable (4 inch version), but in all fairness it is nice to have this in the console of my car ready to charge my phone without having to have the excess wire rolled up! The cable itself is great quality and works perfectly.

reviewText: The lightning end of the cable is too thick around the base to fit into the phone with a cover on it. The plastic is soft enough, however, to trim down with a dremel, (which I also bought on Amazon...) which is what I had to do. Works fine and it stays in the car for emergencies.
it works fine till it broke. Only lasted for almost 5 month. I thought it could survive longer. but you get what you paid for.
does the job in charging but after using it for 2 months, if started wearing and tearing, i ail pay little more and get the original one from apple store

reviewText: The cord charges my phone fine but it will not recognize device when hooked up to my computer. Tried on both my Apple computers with same result.

I was using this cable as one I kept downstairs and used it a couple of times per week. In less than 3 months, the cable no longer works. It didn't come apart like it did for others, just stopped working completely.

I have purchased three of these. One for each car. Take a lot of abuse (heat) but just keep working. The ends are reenforced which many of the $1-$2 cables I have purchased for inside the house don't have and are their ultimate downfalls. Just as sturdy as original apple cables. Thanks amazon.

Not having the ability to use these with iTunes to sync is really irritating . I would have spent the extra money if that would have been clear. This is purely a charging cable. If you use your laptop to charge at work and walk around a lot it also gets irritating when you plug back in and your iphone always says Trust this computer? Trust or don't trust. Every single time.
summary: Purely a charging and not for use with iTunes.

reviewText: As usual, AmazonBasics products have an excellent level of quality. Unlike the imported cables you'll find for pennies on the dollar on other websites, this cable is actually Certified by Apple. Because of this, you won't get that annoying "This accessory is not certified and may not work correctly." message which has started popping up in iOS7.I'm using this with my new iPhone 5S with no problems, and am very happy with the quality. I also use it plugged into the accessory port of my Chevy Equinox, and the stereo makes a connection to the phone just fine (something else that didn't work with one of those cheap imported cables.)
summary: Certified Cable: No Errors in iOS7 with iPhone 5S

reviewText: Bought this cable to replace a super cheap generic cable that failed after 30 days. The "out of the box" build quality was far superior, about of the quality of a premium cable that would come with a device. My only complaint about this cable is it's only a $4 saving over buying an Apple original cable.
The lightning connector end is a bit larger than the Apple version so it didn't fit in the first bumper I purchased. Not a big deal though. And with the money you save you can buy 10 bumpers.

The cable sheath has pulled away from the connector housing.I have this cable next to my bedside table and I certainly don't pull on it too hard. There's a problem with this cable design and for this pricetag there should have been a much longer return policy.Stay away from these iphone5 cables; they're junk.I really like the AmazonBasics series of cables. There was no tear or stress that caused this defect after I received it; the insulation just wasn't secured in the housing. This caused the shielding to fray and eventually I noticed that the cable was really hot when I disconnected my phone. I have no idea if it could start a fire, but it definitely was hot enough to burn skin.I'm hopeful that this is just a random mfg flaw, but it's the reason that I only gave this 3 stars instead of 5.

reviewText: No excuse for the bulkly size of this adapter, just poor engineering by the Amazon Basics department. The cable functions great, but it's simply too big to work with just about any case. Amazon is better than this and I hope they plan on revising the design soon.

reviewText: This works as described but it takes an extra long time to charge devices......looking for something much faster charging speed.

reviewText: For the first three months, this cable was very good. I used it nightly to recharge my iPad. Some of them did stop working, but that was after way more than 4 months of use. This is not the first Amazon basics product I've bought, but it will be the last.

reviewText: Works perfect. iPhone 5 and iPad Mini.Just like Apple. I like the Black color better too.Strongly Recommended. Seems very study and well made. Looks like it will last.

reviewText: Works unlike other third party chargers. I highly recommend that you do purchase an original lightning cable if you use a Lifeproof or Defender case on your phone as the lightning connector on this one is thicker than the original lightning cable.

poor quality.

lightning plug housing is larger than apple design. does not fit into a lifeproof 5S caseit is going back

So now I pretty much just have a long cable specific for my iPad because I don't want to take off my case every night.I am thinking about trying to sand down the sides of the cable, but I may just end up returning it. To force you to get this one??? I love Roku products but I say get the 2 and save the $30.

reviewText: Got this for my husband for Christmas. We love our Roku, we have 4 of them in the house, this being the newest and best. Absolutely no problems or complaints!

Great interface and lots of online content. However, this device will not play your video files directly off of a local network or NAS drive. If you want to do that, get a WDTV Live. Even with an attached usb drive, there are many video formats the Roku 3 will not play.
summary: Won't play video files directly over LAN

reviewText: Great item. I decided I no longer wanted to pay for cable. This device steams plenty of free stations including up to date news and ESPN. I pay for Netflix and Hulu, so I am at 15$ per month opposed to 139$ I was paying Comcast. I also splurged 15$ for a digital antenna and get local stations, together these save me lots of cash

Great picture, simple set up is five minuets or less. Loads of apps and channels with more to come. Easy to use. Small size delivers excellent quality picture and well worth Amazon's below retail price. Truly the best streaming device I've seen on the market.

Have used Roku XD/s o a long time. Decided to go with the RoKU 3Pros:- Good 1080 HD picture. the best thing is the search. I can enter a term like "Hitchcock" and it will give me all of his movies availabe on Amazon, Hulu, Blockbuster and several other sites I have on the RoKU. This works great. You can list movie,actor, director ect. I also think the remote is great.Cons: none

I bought this after having trouble with my bluray streaming Netflix. A friend who has a couple Roku's recommended. Works great. Easy to set up. I like it so much that I bought one for my father for his birthday.

I bought this directly from Roku, it's about 6 dollars cheaper here if you're a Prime member. Its great! It's tiny, and extremely easy to set up. I bought two, one is wired to my router, one is on wifi, they both stream very well, no buffering. Set up both in 15 minutes. Very easy to use once installed even if this is your first venture into the techno era. I highly recommend this and will be buying another.
I bought this for my 75 year old farther, and he figured it out in about an hour and loves it. We have very fast wireless and it works flawlessly.

I bought this Roku 3 as a second unit. The first was a Roku 2 that is attached to an aging but still quite workable CRT television with a 4:3 aspect ratio and Composite and S-Video inputs. The Roku 2 and the CRT television are connected via composite and the picture is good. I was, however, disappointed with the user interface.Enter the Roku 3, which I've attached to a modern 40" flat-screen LCD-lit LED television via HDMI. The user interface on the Roku 3 is better than was that of the Roku 2. The picture quality of the Roku 2 and Roku 3 seem about the same (tested using HDMI to the new TV for both tests. The Roku 2 UI has since been automagically updated to that used by the Roku 3 UI. This was unexpected and a pleasant surprise.Another pleasant surprise was the inclusion of a set of ear buds that plug into the remote control unit of the Roku 3 allowing a user to listen privately. This is a simple but quite effective and useful capability.In the end, if you buy a Roku 3 instead of a Roku 2 you will lose composite output to gain the private listening capability. Assuming you are using a TV or computer monitor with HDMI and 1080p (and perhaps 720p) resolution, this is a worthwhile trade-off.
summary: Good upgrade from a Roku 2, provided you have HDMI

reviewText: I first got one for a relative who likes to watch Netflix on her TV but had to relocate away from a cable connection. The Roku 3 processed the wifi signal from the cable router (Comcast) over a 10' through an interior wall flawlessly. It was also easier to use and more responsive since the receiver is on all the time but not connected to any Internet app until instructed by the remote. The remote connects with its base station via radio wave, not infrared, which obviates the need to point the remote toward the base station. Lots of free or subscription apps available and the "shopping" experience is very simple since you are forced to give a credit card number, a password and an email address during the first time log on process. I was impressed enough to buy one for myself to replace the perfectly functional but slower and somewhat clunky WD Live+ device. I already had an Ethernet connection at my TV so I can't give an assessment of the wifi reception.

If you don't mind the slightly steep price comparing to other products, it's truly a great steaming device that delivers picture so great that I honestly think it's better than the movie theaters (especially for the super HD titles from Netflix). From my personal experience, don't go thru the trouble of buying a Roku 2 and end up returning it to upgrade it for a Roku 3. Just buy a Roku 3 if you have to save up - it's worth it! The Roku 2 does 1080 dpi also, but the HD images would delay (due to latency?) and showing doubled and snowy images for fast images such as when the camera is panning. Although short delays, but it gets old really quick once you notice it. The Roku 3 processor is advertised as 5x faster, not sure what that means in geek measurements, but it sure makes the delay virtually non-existent, resulting in content HD images - super cool! Another thing is that seems a little silly to me is that this is a device priced for 1080 DPI streaming, but the default is at 720 DPI out of the box...so make sure you go to the settings to set the display to 1080 if you TV supports it.One last comment, I saw others gave this a 1 star because it requires credit card during registration and set up. They do that because they need to have the means to charge you if you decide to stream pay-per-view movies such as new releases in Amazon. But they won't charge you for no good reason (I hope...lol).Bottom line - quality 5 = stars, but steep price = 3 stars, average = 4 stars.
summary: Price a bit steep - but superb picture quality!

reviewText: I got rid of my cable...I had a problem paying $100/mo when I only watched a couple of programs. I purchased the Roku instead of the AppleTV because Apple does NOT allow me to channel my Amazon Prime, Roku does. I am really pleased with the Apps and the ease of use. I do wish I could stream directly from my PC though...Youtube, Hulu (free version), video files, etc.

I had the Roku 2 and the HDMI failed after a year. They refused to repair it. So I am not happy with their "throw away" attitude. Is it worth the price? Not to me; but my family likes to watch Amazon movies so it seems the best device for that. as to having a headset on the remote.. just a buzz item for kids.. if it sold for $45, it would be worth the money, else it is over priced for a non repairable device.
summary: Ok but is it worth the price?

reviewText: I have 2 of these. One in Living Room and another in my Man Cave. I had been trying to figure out how to "easily" play my Music Videos Wireless to my Projector. First tried Apple TV and used an I Phone/ I Pad. I didn't like that setup. Having to hold an I pad while sitting at the Bar was Cumbersome. So in comes the Roku. Loaded up an 8 Gb Flash Drive. Much better. This is as close to what I wanted to do as anything I've tried. However, nothing is perfect. The remote is great as it's Wi_Fi. Not having to point at Device. I can sit anywhere in the Room. ( Bar ) The Videos that come through to the Projector though aren't as clear as when I play them from MY PC (also hooked up to the Projector) The audio also doesn't seem quite as good. This all goes through my Yamaha A1020 AVR to the Projector. Also, every so often when Playing a Video the Roku freezes and reboots. I then play the next Vid and no problem. This doesn't happen a lot but enough to not give this thing 5 Stars. Another thing is the Media Player App to access the Media on the Flash Drive. It's very basic and doesn't have any way to control Volume.
summary: So far, so good. But, not perfect.

reviewText: I have a WD TV Live Hub 500GB Media Center and several WD TV Live players. I needed another device to go in the Living Room and I had heard allot of good things about the Roku 3 so I decided to give it a try. It does everything my WD TV Players do except one thing, it won't accept just any USB device for playback of video or music. I didn't know that it required a USB device from Roku or I wouldn't have bought it. Hard to understand why companies think they can get away with locking you into their proprietary devices. The WD Live TV media players will accept any USB external device and so far I haven't found a format they won't play. Silly me for thinking about trying something new, if it isn't broken don't fix it. Geez, I guess I'll never learn, LOL

I have been able to link up with most programs but am having a problem with Spirit Clips from Hallmark. Roku is doing what it said it would and seems easier to navigate than my previous device by another company.
summary: So far so good with Roku

reviewText: I have owned a 3 rokus , the XD the 2 and now the 3. This one is the best, added you tube and the processer is fast. No need for cable or satellite, an outdoor antenna and internet Netflix and Hulu Plus, you will have more channels of entertainment than any of the others offer. Plus fewer commercials, not to mention the money saved. The world wide web is your DVR. The search feature is great too! So glad I got this little jewel.

I have the Roku 2 HD and wanted the latest for my bedroom. The Roku player version 3 has been very fickle about reception. I have to move it about a lot to get channels. I am hoping an upgrade will do the trick.Make sure to Google Roku private channels so you can have even more. I'm disappointed, most of the free channels are lame and you end up having to buy a decent channels subscription. Sure it could be less than cable, but you'll end up with lower quality channels too. The only thing I rave about is the ability to get world news from round the globe and it has a usb port. The usb port will only play mp4 files so if you have any other format you'll have to convert your files. This is a nice feature, I hope Roku gets more quality free channels and usb support for all video formats.Keep in mind this is HDMI only so it won't work with older TV's.Vidimo Se!
summary: Fickle Reception & Lots of Pay Channels

reviewText: I have two of these for two TVs in two rooms. You can move them from one TV to another, but on the original TV I use with, the plug is very difficult to get to. Not worth my time/effort for the price. I have Acorn TV (British TV) and need this to watch - never had an issue with using, never re-loads like sometimes my smart TV does. I also LOVE the fact I can plug in headphones on the remote. I have some wireless headphones that have lots of static, but these do not have any. Great product for a great price. Highly recommend.

I just switched from Roku XR (3 years old) to Roku 3. Navigation is lightning fast by comparison. Streams load initially much faster. As for streaming performance, thus far it appears to be better. When in debug mode, it is showing higher speeds than it did with same connection to the Roku XR. The speedtest channel is also showing better numbers. I will need to test this over weeks to confirm it is indeed the new Roku, but I believe it is at this point. I only use wired, and thus have not tested the wireless connection.The only thing that appears worse is the sound quality for music, such as Pandora. It sounded better on the Roku XR for whatever reason. The Pandora sound through the Roku 3 sounds a bit distorted, no matter which audio settings are set to.Overall, I would recommend upgrading, as the speed of navigation alone will reduce the frustration factor significantly.
I like the fact that I can watch tv at night and not bother anyone. The ear phones on the remote is a killer idea
it has a lot of channel but its like cable, some channel is useless, it does not have youtube channel. most of the channel is pay-per-view services like netflix and amazon. I guess its ok.

It is great that they added headphones into the remote control! However, they took away the secondary A/V channel that worked alongside the HDMI, like in the Roku 2. It only has one HDMI output. This makes it impossible to hook up the device to a separate surround sound system, without some sort of splitter and/or converter.
summary: Give and take from the Roku 2

reviewText: I was looking for something that I could use, my wife, my father and my in-laws...and this is perfect! I tried a VIZIO GoogleTV at first, but decided it wasn't as smooth to use as I needed and once I got this I realized anyone can use it even if they aren't a "techie" type of person. I got this running with my Plex server along with other Channels that all work perfectly! Bought a 2nd one for my father and it sadly was a lemon, but Amazon sent me a replacement (next-day) with free return shipping, so I won't count this against the product since Amazon.com stands behind what they sell so well!

Most people know what a Roku is, and know its pros/cons. So this is for those of you overseas like me, and want to know if it will work on 220v. The answer is "yes".The adapter says its only rated for 110v, but after doing some Googling around the internet I found a few brave folks out there that tried it out to see what would happen... and it worked. One guy even posted some info that it works on 220v, but was just never tested at the manufactor, so that's why it only says 110v.I plugged it into my wall outlet, and it worked without problems.

No matter what I did or how I hooked the unit up to my system I could not get it to play sound through my receiver speakers. The TV comes through the speakers, the Blu-Ray player comes through the speakers but the Roku would only come through the TV speakers. I tried switching it to the Blu-Ray player wiring and Input but no luck. I tried to redesignate the unit to another input HDMI, no luck.Back to Amazon for a refund.My TV plays Netflix anyway.

Not much to say, the Roku 3 works, is easy to use, and the remote works great. Really like the headphone input, let me watch in bed after my wife is out cold. The download time is very fast, at least compared to my Wii.

Roku 3 - Advantages! (Over Roku 1)Has Wired connection option - If your wired connection is not strong that means your Wifi connection is even worse. Having a wired connection from your router would be a definite plus.YouTube Channel - Save all your favorite YouTube videos to a YouTube Playlist - and play right on your TV.The Roku 3 has a better operating system - which means it gets more timely updates then other Roku products, like the YouTube channel is available now (3/24/2014) only for Roku 3Speed - The Speed difference is VERY noticeable when you play movies stored on your home network. 5-10 times faster to load.USB Slot - Allows you to plug in your USB stick and have photo slides shows, play video or music on your TV.MicroSD Slot - You can take the MicroSD card out of your Camera and now view your photos on the big screen.One issue I have with ALL Roku's - the Surround System is 'Dolby Digital Plus' aka DD+ - so if you have an older sound system that does not recognize DD+ you will not be able to play true Surround. (But most Surround system can Simulate surround using Stereo system) That is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.
summary: Great product, should have purchased one long ago!

reviewText: Roku 3 report so far. Still a fairly straightforward, simple install, but not as much as the gen 1. Much, MUCH faster. PBS channel works on this one, and it has a lot of good stuff. GUI disappointing, especially for netflix (too much time spent optimizing it for screens bigger than my 26" left it with skinny little white type on dark backgrounds, impossible to read). On the plus side, it's also a teeny, tiny little box. Cute.Last but not least, THERE WAS A COMMERCIAL. What the heck? That annoys me. Also, the remote keys no longer work the same for each vendor (e.g., Netflix to Amazon to Smithsonian to whatever else I tried earlier), and it's annoying. The remote has also dropped the ok from the middle of a 4-directional pad to a single key below a cross-shaped set of 4 arrow keys. This leaves less space between the keys, and it feels like I'm about to hit a key I am not intending to hit just about every time, and I did, several times.Another big annoyance is that it doesn't ever fall asleep (except for one time), so a very bright, white light is on 24 hours a day.I plan on giving it a thorough workout for a few more days to try and determine if the added speed makes up for the annoyances. Not sure yet by a long shot.
summary: Eh. It's been a week. Good and bad.

reviewText: Roku 3 was quick to install and simple to set up, it is also very easy to use. I would recommend this product.

Says "HDCP Unauthorized" every single day (possibly because I turn my TV off and on). Roku offers no solution to this problem besides rebooting the Roku, and won't even put an explanation on that screen.Instead of "HDCP Unauthorization", why can't the screen say "Sorry, we're having a problem connecting to your TV. Please try A, B, and C, or see our web page at D, or call us at this phone number for tech support". This level of indifference to customers, and technical incompetence, is infuriating. Ready to throw my Roku 3 out the window.
summary: Unacceptable bugs, and little/no tech support or even ackknowlegement from Roku

reviewText: The only thing it really lacks is a YouTube app and TwitchTV app. Besides that it's gold. Headphones are pretty crappy though.

The Roku 3 is fast, the menus and navigation much improved and user friendly and the video quality is very good and, as noted, there is a lot of content previously unavailable the best of which like Amazon Prime, Hulu, Vudu and Netflix require paid subscriptions, the worst, like Popcorn, include intrusive commercial content as the price of admission. PBS although somewhat limited is not bad. In the end there probably is something for everyone.As for Netflix, their streaming library is very limited and may not be worth the $7.99 a month for some bad movies. Their original programming is excellent, however and you might consider using your free 30-day trial to watch House of Cards which is terrific and the new season of Arrested Development which isn't as good as past seasons.In short, Roku 3 very good, content less so but that seems to be ever changing.

The Roku 3 was received without any issues or problems. For that I greatly appreciated the smoothness of the shipping process with Amazon. That said, I've completely enjoyed using the Roku 3 and have not had any issues with it whatsoever. I completely enjoy using it and watching my movies and videos through its easy to use interface, too. If you are looking for something that is very straightforward to setup and use and does not come with the premium price, this is a great purchase.
summary: Easy out of the box setup and use!

reviewText: The Roku does provide a nice gateway to major streaming services. The device itself is well made, the controller easy to use, and the audio headphones a nice bonus. Yet as a game controller the device is sorely lacking and lag between movement and response is a fatal shortcoming.What makes the device of value is access to streaming channels not possible through the usual apps included with Blu-ray, HDTV and Bluray players. In that, it is worth trying if you have the means. Yet I would go a step further to say that the Roku is not 100% vital to cut-the-cord or to have at all. Not yet. Not a waste to buy, but not yet mature.

The Roku works perfectly out of the box. I can watch Netflix, Hulu, Amazon Prime, and HBO effortlessly. It is really handy to be able to use my phone as a remote too. I would recommend these units to everyone.

This is our first Roku and it's quite a handy product to stream Amazon Prime videos to our TV. It's simple to install and you can get it up and running within minutes. I'd give it a five star rating if it had more "Channels". Right now - Perhaps 4.5.
summary: Looks great, run great - Amazon Prime App!

reviewText: this is the ultimate product for starting the process of replacing cable/satellite television. there are tons of apps free and paid that allow you to watch almost anything. My kids cant get enough of it I had to purchase another one for myself.

This would be 5 stars... but the thing freezes so often. I believe it is overheating. It freezes when viewing hd movies or listening to Pandora for a long time. The only way to reset it is to unplug it, and plug it back in. I can't believe the reviews for this thing are so positive. Maybe I just got a lemon.

We have two (abandoned and unsupported) Logitech Revues which we love. The full keyboard (and ability to also watch live TV without grabbing an additional remote to change HDMI inputs gives that device an edge.) That being said, the Roku is a fast, simple interface, and a good aggregator of our various subscription services (Amazon Prime, Netflix, HBO-GO) as well as tons of Internet content (much of it free.)Great for kids in College with limited funds who can watch on our dimes without expensive subscriptions...
summary: Don't ever complain there's "nothing to watch" again !

reviewText: Works well and has replaced my TV entirely. I started my journey with and Apple TV but the Roku was so very much better I got rid of the Apple TV. The remote is fantastic with a headphone output which defeats the audio out, very elegant. I use this for Netflix, and Amazon prime and they work great.HBOGO however does not work, and that is a disappointment.There are some threads on this in forums where people blame network issues. I've tried a bunch of fixes but HBOGO unfortunately simply stalls on loading 90% of the time.

Yes, I dinged it a star because it gets hot just sitting there doing nothing. There should be a lower power state that doesn't leave it so warm even when it is not in use.We have ours hard-wired via ethernet cable and never have a problem with dropouts or buffering. The offerings are good, but honestly you can get most of the ones you want in a Smart TV. The interface on the Roku 3 is lightening fast. That is the most significant difference we notice. It is just a much more pleasant experience to use it when all your clicks are responded too immediately.Additionally, the search function is greatly improved. You can search for an actor, for instance, and it will search across all your channels to let you know where you can see that actor.This is our third Roku, we had two of the first generation ones. It is definitely a large upgrade worth it for any current Roku owner.
summary: Great Media Player - Gets little hot

reviewText: Any cheaper HD streamer will do the same. As an outsider of the USA user I'm not using it to its max with the best Audio and Video Internet streaming providers. And what it's left with, is cheap and outdated movies music and programs. As a user of Apple Tv streamer who's not "fully loaded" like the Roku 3. The Apple Tv streamer gives less but better quality options to enjoy. I wish Rokus developers were concentrate putting quality and not quantity.
BE ADVISED, YOU HAVE TO PROVIDE A CREDIT CARD NUMBER TO ACTIVATE AND SETUP AND ACCOUNT. THEY CLAIM IT'S FOR MY OWN CONVENIENCE, DO ME A FAVOR ROKU, I DO NOT NEED THAT FAVOR.
summary: CREDIT CARD INFO A MUST TO SETUP ACCOUNT !!!

reviewText: Be careful If you don't live in US, Canada or Europe.... This box is worst than the other types.... for use outside US, Canada or Europe They do not have Netflix or Crackle, AMAZING!!! everybody could access both by internet.Shame on Roku all I have is garbage......
summary: Be careful If you don't live in US, Canada or Europe

reviewText: I am a long time Roku fan and have owned a Roku 1, 2 and 3. In some ways the Roku 3 is a big improvement (the increased processing power, more reliable wireless ability - the old units would often ship with dead wireless adapters - and it doesnt seem to restart nearly as much).The big problem is in the software changes which I hope some reverts soon with a software update. These are the features that have been removed:1) In Roku 2 you can press down and see the basic info about what you are watching - useful for tv shows cause you can see the name of the show, season, episode, year aired - this feature is replaced in Roku 3 with the ability to turn captions on ad off, something you rarely mess with!?? If you want that info you have to stop what you are watching and then go to more episodes and then find the episode you were watching.... very annoying!!!2) if you half watched an episode THEY REMOVED THE OPTION TO RESUME OR PLAY FROM BEGINING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I could understand if the feature never existed but why remove it on youre latest and greatest model??Roku!!! Please fix this with a software update and I'll update this to 5 stars and go back to telling people door to door how amazing roku is in my spare time :-)
summary: Works Great BUT THEY REMOVED VITAL FEATURES!

reviewText: I bought the Roku because of the high ratings and that it has the most mature app marketplace versus other streamers. However, I need it to be a sling catcher and it severely under-excels at that purpose. To catch sling, you have to install the iPhone or Android app on your smartphone and then push it to the Roku. It doesn't work with my iPad mini and I don't want to tie up any of my phones to serving video. That makes it essentially worthless as a sling device -- if I am going to dedicate a device, why wouldn't I get a Widi caster or AppleTV. Makes no sense Roku -- get your act together.I ended up getting the WDLive, which is perfect as a sling device. Unfortunately it doesn't get Amazon Prime video. Why do I need to make tradeoffs?
summary: Not acceptable as a sling catcher!

reviewText: I can't get HBO go working thanks to Comcast and since it does not have a fiber connection and my stereo does not have HDMI abilities I am out of luck getting 5.1 audio out of my roku like I did on my old unit. Luckily I have an apple TV so HOB GO works on this unit.
summary: might not be worth it if you have HBO and comcast - get the apple TV

reviewText: I didn't know I was signing up for an onslaught of commercials ... over and over and over and over and over and over again! Sometimes the same commercial plays three times in a row! I've seen the Bic woman's shaver, the Lexis ad and the U.S. Navy ads at least 100 times each in the 5 days or so that I have had the player. If you don't own one, you think I'm exaggerating. If you do own one and you use it for other than watching movies, you know I'm not.I bought this player because I was tired of the sluggishness of the interactive features of my Toshiba Blue-Ray player. One of the things I've valued about that Toshiba is that I can watch several news shows I like, with absolutely NO commercial interruptions at all. In comparison, although Roku has a much larger selection, the quality sucks due to constant and repetitive splurges trying to sell me something, over and over, that I am never in my lifetime going to buy. They only have four or five advertisers, so those ads are repeated again and again ... etc.As a comparison, with the Toshiba, I can watch the NBC evening news, in its entirety, without commercial interruption. The Roku breaks that show up into selected segments, not giving you the entire show and each of those segments is preceded by 2 or 3 commercials. The segments, at times, may be as short as 30 seconds - so, within a 1 minute time span, you have viewed 30 seconds of news and 3 minutes of 30 second commercials.One of the channels I loaded was a small set of special documentaries, which was interrupted, literally, every three minutes by the same set of commercials.There are some other nice features about this player - such as USB and micro-sd. But these are outweighed, for my usuage, by constantly irritating crap!I am returning this item.

I don't even know where to begin. First the Roku won't work without being updated, you can't link to WiFi without it. No ethernet cable.... well you could sit on hold for a half hour, talk with a terrible customer service agent who wants all your personal information (customer service for the Roku isn't free BTW) and have them give you the same information you could look up online in 2 seconds.You have to do some insane manipulating to get it to force update - and even then things don't work.WiFi is not maintained when your television is turned off - which means EVERY time you grab the remote to watch the Roku you have to navigate to setup and re-initialize the WiFi.WTF - my WD media player was way better than this POS.
summary: If I could return it I would

reviewText: I had to buy the Roku 2 because you have to have an HDMI connection. The DVI-HDTV cable does not carry audio. The remote is much better on the Roku 3 as well.
Returned due to not that much to watch as expected. It was very fast but lacked youtube. Was looking for more free stuff to watch.

There are basically two drawbacks with the Roku 3 I've bought:1. The support of video formats is very limited, notably the lack of AVI support. Unforgivable.2. If living outside USA, Canada or Europe, the Netflix channel is not available, even if Netflix is available in other countries (like in my case, in Argentina).I am really disappointed...
summary: Disappointing product after so many good reviews

reviewText: This was buggy in the beginning. Updates have improved reliability. Still has occasional connection issues. Still addicted though so put up with the issues. Hope version 4 will be better.

Good - This is the best new toy I have tried in years! I spend more time on Roku 3 than U-Verse TV or surfing. All I need is Roku 3 with Netflix and Amazon Prime plus rabbit ears. And wifi, of course.BAD - I hope the Roku USB channel actually gets fixed for video someday and I wish sellers would not keep pretending that this is a feature rather than a fraud! I do not consider having to use Handbrake with preset, “Regular – High Profile” to to create or convert files that play well on the Roku player as acceptable. Be warned. Buy a WD player if you want to play your video files.If you want a Streaming Player, get this, but do not believe that this will play video files from USB, ignore the lies that say otherwise!

I have 2 other ROKU players I love all of them I purchased the ROKU3 because of the faster load times and the ear phones so I can not bother others people The only problem I had was the batteries failed in the controller after 1 month I purchased new batteries and all is well . I have become to use ROKU3 as my main form of entertainment after purchasing Amazon Prime to watch my internet movies and TV shows.Great Job
I purchased this over iTV, in part was buying into the notion that this device was easy to talk with other devices. I guess I am wrong!
summary: too difficult streaming video content from pad or phone

reviewText: Recently bought and set up. Interface is easy to navigate. Finding channels is simple. I use amazon prime which provides a lot of included content. It is easy to rent content from the many available channels. The picture is very good on 50 inch Panasonic plasma. Sometimes while watching the streaming buffer runs out and then I need to either wait or exit program and go back in. This has only happened a handful of times, which isn't much of a problemTHE BAD... This Roku drops its connection to my wireless router almost every single day. Because of these drops I can't have young kids use the Roku, and my less tech-savey family members can't use it without my help. I tried showing off that this is a cool device but it seems like a beta product, my family shrugged and say they'll stick with cable TV. Another minor complaint is that the remote isn't backlit.If Roku can fix the wireless drop problem then my rating will go up 2 more stars. My wireless network is very stable and strong, the Roku sits less than 20 ft away.
summary: good but not great because it drops wireless network almost every day

reviewText: Waste of Time and money. I bought the ROKU 3 for netflix and other online content but cannot use it because although I have a netflix account the ROKU 3 won't work in my country. So I will just stick to my old faithfull WD live Player that I have had for a few years now does just what I want. You can't even change the DNS on the ROKU so you can't even hide it,and the aps thing is just frustrating.Just imagine I bought this thing on Amazon and can't even get Amazon.
would not recognize our wireless router (an RT-N16) which has had absolutely no connectivity problems with any of our other networked stuff.

My wife is totally blind. We had Sky Angel IPTV until they stopped service February 14, 2014. She could punch in channel numbers and view any of her dozen favorite channels. Or she could push channel up & down to scan all of them. She was even able to operate the wonderful feature of watching any Christian channel program for up to 48 hours after a show ran. Email, FB, surf websites etc. She is getting comfortable with an iPhone now and can use most of the features. reviewText: According to Roku, there is no power button on this device because it uses so little electricity that a user should never have to unplug it. This bad thing about this product is that after about a week it will lose it's internet connection forcing you to either press the reset button that is hard to get to, or unplug the device.The one simple item that Roku could have equipped with this is a power button but they couldn't foresee a need for it and now I have to unplug the device once a week to be able to use it. I love the idea of a Roku device, but this version isn't very useful for many home theatre setups. Let me explain.Issues:* Only a single HDMI output for video AND audio.* If you have digital audio (optical or RCA) connections to your receiver, you are screwed.* If you want to split the video signal, you are screwed.* If you have a projector and need to split the audio, you are screwed.* If you have a low bandwidth broadband connection, much of the HD streaming will be SD-only.* If you have a residential broadband connection, there may be data caps that come into play if you watch 1 movie a day for the month. 720p HiDef movies are about 1.5-2.5G of streaming. If your ISP caps at 150G or 250G, well, you can do the math. This probably will not affect most homes, unless you are stay-at-home and stream a bunch.* If you care about real password security, the Roku website / device fails. 6-12 characters only. 2 credit cards were locked by my banks because I used a 40+ character password during account signup and all the failed attempts were seen as fraud. No error was shown on the "enter new password" page, before the "continue" to credit card page was displayed. Phone support ended up creating an account that didn't have any credit card for me. The update password screen DOES display an error for long passwords that the new account page was/is missing. If I'm entering any financial data into a website, I want 30-80 character passwords. 12 characters is laughable these days - less than 24 hrs to be hacked by a pro with a $1000 PC.Cheap HDMI audio splitters are available for $50-ish, but with HDCP, those devices will not work for 5.1 audio. The specification requires downsampling. It takes a semi-illegal $400 device to split the HD video and audio and retain full resolution HD and 5+ channel audio. Sad.I love the built-in wifi and Ethernet, but I'd happily have wifi only or wired ethernet only for a digital audio-out with either optical or RCA ports that support 5+ channel audio. I actually miss the component and digital audio outputs from older devices.If you just want to connect the Roku3 directly to a TV, like in a bedroom - it is an excellent device, provided your TV supports HDMI. My TV needs to be powered off and on to reset the HDMI connection after the Roku is rebooted or inputs on the TV are changed. The Roku splash screen works perfectly after a reboot, but then goes blank, until the HDMI communication is reset somehow. TV power on-off is the easiest way, though hot plugging the HDMI cable works too.I suppose if I had an HDMI capable receiver, that could solve the audio/video issue too, but HDMI is notorious for incompatible connections between different devices, even from the same maker. Roku, receiver, TV all have to communicate perfectly for this to work - there is often a failure.My TV has a digital audio output ... that gets downsampled to 2.1 channels at best. 5.1 is lost.My projector doesn't have any audio out at all ... except a crappy 1W speaker.Plus, the Roku doesn't have a power-on/off button. THAT drives me crazy.3 stars due to the limited usefulness of the device. Looks like I need to spend $400+ on some other equipment to make this $99 device work in my home.[===== August Update =====]I wanted to love the Roku3, I really did. Recently, I connected the Roku to an older, early generation TV, and got to see the NO HDCP Device Connected error. Guess we won't be watching Roku on that device. Tried to watch content that is NOT copyrighted on the Roku - even then the HDCP error was displayed. NASA doesn't copyright anything, their content in public property. It shouldn't be HDCP protected, but it is .... why?In the last few weeks, I've noticed much more buffering breaks while watching content. It happens mostly during prime-internet time in the evenings. During morning or daytime, the only streaming issues are due to ISP failures.
summary: WARNING - HDMI with HDCP only - Got a projector?

reviewText: I have been using a dedicated mini-itx computer as a home theater system for years and I figured that a dedicated box might provide somewhat better video rendering. The Windows XP; Silverlight; Atom processor; Nvidia ION graphics combination doesn't have perfect video. There is often a horizontal 'crease' mid-frame.I only watch Netflix -- the sundry other channels are unimportant to me.I have just installed the ROKU3 which is straightforward enough but the basic selection display is low-resolution. I'm guessing it defaults to 720p while in menu-mode and only goes to 1080p mode when streaming. It feels as if I'm stuck on cable TV.I plugged a USB keyboard into the ROKU's USB socket but it isn't possible to use keyboard entry. Searching for titles is like text messaging on a dumb-phone.All-in-all it is disappointing. The product it too TV-like and insufficiently computer-like.A day later:The Android app for the Roku makes the product tolerable. In fact once the Roku is set up, the remote can be abandoned in favor of the app since text input is MUCH easier on Android. It remains a pity that the Android tablet version is IDENTICAL to the phone version -- this is dumb and utterly lazy of Roku. The tablet version should enable the user to engage in the full web experience of Netflix (or other channel) and then simply direct the streaming to the Roku. The backspace key on the Android phone DOESN'T work on the Roku. The Roku has a VERY poor app.Much later:I'm trying to use the Roku3 with an inexpensive video projector and a basic stereo system. The projector has an HDMI input but no audio output. I bought an HDMI audio 'splitter' which outputs left and right stereo to two RCA jacks and passes through the HDMI video to the projector.At times the set-up works fine but at other times (seemingly randomly) I get no video nor audio. If I hook up the Roku3 directly to the projector I can get the video to work, though it seems to slip into 720p mode. When things are not working well I connect a 3.5mm jack into the Roku3's remote and am able to get poor quality audio into my system. The Roku3 software is up to date.Restarting the Roku3 and/or the splitter does not seem to solve the problem. I have read that the 'clever' HDMI interface automatically configures itself for surround sound and disables the regular stereo mode. I have set the Roku3 for stereo use, NOT for surround sound. The HDMI splitter is the second one I have purchased -- I had previously purchased an HDMI 4 x 2 matrix hub but had the same kind of problem -- so it isn't the splitter.This is VERY frustrating. I'm irritated that the Roku3 doesn't have it's own audio audio output. The 3.5mm jack on the remote is really quite silly.I'm guessing that there is some kind of handshaking protocol that the HDMI interface has that communicates the mode of operation but that the Roku3 does not control satisfactorily.I've been told I SHOULD have bought the less expensive Roku 2 !!!Oh, and by the way don't try Roku's support chat:One of our representatives will be with you shortly. You are number 22 in the queue. Your wait time will be approximately 19 minute(s). Thank you for your patience.So "shortly" in Roku-land is 19 minutes...The Roku on-line chat eventually told me: "Roku is designed to connect to your TV directly. We could not be sure about connecting it using such splitters. We could try some troubleshooting steps. But we couldnt be sure that it would work."So it appears Roku isn't designed for home theaters...

So this won't be a in depth review. I didn't keep it long enough to do that. But there are a few good/bad things I have to mention:The Good:- User Interface seems reasonably well done. UI is responsive.- Easy to setup on my WIFI network.- Lots of online content available... at a price.- Roku made it really easy to cancel my account on their website.The Bad:- Even if I don't actually want to purchase content on my Roku, I still need to provide them my credit card. WHY?- Playing my own content *only* works via USB pendrive/etc. I can't stream it via SMB/NFS/etc. This ended up being why I returned the Roku, since 95% of what I want to do is stream content from my local computer and I don't want to have to deal with copying files to USB pendrives everytime I want to watch something.- No keyboard on the remote. This makes filling in search boxes a lot more painful then alternatives- The remote and Roku box itself just seem like it was made in China on the cheap. (and yes, it says made in China). I'm a bit concerned how long the remote will last- especially if kids are using it to play games. If you stripped off the logo's, nobody would ever confuse this with a product made by Apple which tend to feel more solid and scream well made/designed.Overall, I think the Apple TV is a nicer integrated product which basically does everything the Roku does (well other then games, but I already have a PS3 for that). The key reason I bought this though was to watch content I had on my hard drive and wanted to stream to my TV. My old Boxee Box did that wonderfully (well until it started having HDMI problems). Otherwise, there are probably better solutions out there.
